Homage to the Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Fully Awakened Buddha ^T-1

# In the Abhidhamma Piṭaka ^0

## Points of Discussion ^5-0

### Discussion of the Person ^5-1-0

#### The Plain Question of Real Fact ^5-1-1-0

##### Forward and Reverse ^5-1-1-1-0

[By this mark the question of our own school is shown] Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact [variant: saccikaṭṭhaparamaṭṭhenāti (Syā., Pī., Ka., Sī.)]? Yes. Is the person found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found? That should not be said.
Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found." What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said, then surely [variant: no vata re (Syā., Pī.)] "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong.
The forward set of five. ^5-1

[By this mark the question of the other school is shown] Is a person not found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is the person not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found? That should not be said.
Acknowledge the counter-refutation. If a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found." What you say here — that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said, then surely "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong.
The counter-refutation set of four. ^5-2

But if you think that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said, then on the grounds of that assertion of yours [variant: tvaṃ (Syā.); the sub-commentary should be consulted], you, admitting this [the sub-commentary should be consulted], must be refuted in this way. So we refute you, and you are rightly refuted [variant: suniggahitova (Syā.)].
If a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found." What you say here — that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said, then surely "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is not found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is not found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong on your part.
The refutation set of four. ^5-3

If this refutation is a wrong one, then see the matter there in just the same way [variant: hevameva (Syā.)]: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said. Yet we, admitting this, should not be refuted by you in this way on the grounds of that assertion. And still you refute me, and we are wrongly refuted [variant: dunniggahitāva (Syā.)].
If a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "The person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found." What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said, then surely "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found" should not be said — is wrong on your part.
The application set of four. ^5-4

One should not be refuted in this way. So, as for the refutation you made: "If a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: ‘The person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found.’ What you say here — that ‘a person is found as a real and ultimate fact’ should be said, but ‘the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found’ should not be said — is wrong."
"But if ‘the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found’ should not be said, then surely ‘a person is found as a real and ultimate fact’ should not be said either. What you say here — that ‘a person is found as a real and ultimate fact’ should be said, but ‘the person is found as a real and ultimate fact in the same way as any real and ultimate fact is found’ should not be said — is wrong on your part." Therefore the refutation that was made is badly made. The counter-refutation is well made. The line of argument is well made.
The conclusion set of four.
The first refutation. ^5-5

#### Plain Comparison ^5-1-9-0

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact, and is material form found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is material form one thing and the person another? That should not be said.
Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "Material form is one thing and the person another." What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "material form is one thing and the person another" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "material form is one thing and the person another" should not be said, then surely "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "material form is one thing and the person another" should not be said — is wrong… ^5-17

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact, and is feeling found as a real and ultimate fact… is perception found… are mental formations found… is consciousness found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is consciousness one thing and the person another? That should not be said.
Acknowledge the refutation. If a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and consciousness is found as a real and ultimate fact, then surely you must also say: "Consciousness is one thing and the person another." What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and consciousness is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "consciousness is one thing and the person another" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "consciousness is one thing and the person another" should not be said, then surely "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and consciousness is found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and consciousness is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "consciousness is one thing and the person another" should not be said — is wrong… ^5-18

And the eye element is found as a real and ultimate fact… the ear element is found… the nose element is found… the tongue element is found… the body element is found… the visible-form element is found… the sound element is found… the smell element is found… the taste element is found… the touch element is found… the eye-consciousness element is found… the ear-consciousness element is found… the nose-consciousness element is found… the tongue-consciousness element is found… the body-consciousness element is found… the mind element is found… the mind-consciousness element is found… the element of mental objects is found as a real and ultimate fact… ^5-20

#### Comparison by Analogy ^5-1-10-0

Is material form found as a real and ultimate fact, and is feeling found as a real and ultimate fact, and is material form one thing and feeling another? Yes. Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact, and is material form found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is material form one thing and the person another? That should not be said.
Acknowledge the refutation. If material form is found as a real and ultimate fact, and feeling is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is one thing and feeling another; and a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact — then surely you must also say: "Material form is one thing and the person another." What you say here — that "material form is found as a real and ultimate fact, and feeling is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is one thing and feeling another; a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "material form is one thing and the person another" should not be said — is wrong.
But if "material form is one thing and the person another" should not be said, then surely "material form is found as a real and ultimate fact, and feeling is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is one thing and feeling another; a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact" should not be said either. What you say here — that "material form is found as a real and ultimate fact, and feeling is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is one thing and feeling another; a person is found as a real and ultimate fact, and material form is found as a real and ultimate fact" should be said, but "material form is one thing and the person another" should not be said — is wrong… ^5-28

Acknowledge the refutation. Should it not be said that "a person passes on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, this round of rebirth is without discoverable beginning [variant: anamataggāyaṃ (Ka.)]. No first point is known of beings who, hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, pass on and wander on" [S. Ni. 2.124]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, a person passes on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world. ^5-75

Does a person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? That should not be said… ^5-76

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a human being, becomes a god? Yes. Is that very same human being that god? That should not be said… ^5-77

Is that very same human being that god? Yes. Having been a human being, one becomes a god; having been a god, one becomes a human being. The one who has been a human being is one, the god is another; so the claim that the one who has been a human being is this very same one passing on is wrong…
For if that very same person, passing away from here, passes on to another world without being different, then in that case there will be no death, and the killing of living beings is not found either. There is action, there is the result of action, there is the result of actions that have been done; while wholesome and unwholesome actions are ripening, the claim that this very same one passes on is wrong. ^5-78

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a human being, becomes a spirit, becomes a ghost, becomes a hell-being, becomes an animal, becomes a camel, becomes an ox, becomes a donkey, becomes a pig, becomes a buffalo [variant: mahiso (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)]? Yes. Is that very same human being that buffalo? That should not be said… ^5-79

Is that very same human being that buffalo? Yes. Having been a human being, one becomes a buffalo; having been a buffalo, one becomes a human being. The one who has been a human being is one, the buffalo is another; so the claim that the one who has been a human being is this very same one passing on is wrong…
For if that very same person, passing away from here, passes on to another world without being different, then in that case there will be no death, and the killing of living beings is not found either. There is action, there is the result of action, there is the result of actions that have been done; while wholesome and unwholesome actions are ripening, the claim that this very same one passes on is wrong. ^5-80

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a noble, becomes a brahmin? Yes. Is that very same noble that brahmin? That should not be said… ^5-81

Is there anyone who, having been a noble, becomes a merchant, becomes a labourer? Yes. Is that very same noble that labourer? That should not be said… ^5-82

Is there anyone who, having been a brahmin, becomes a merchant, becomes a labourer, becomes a noble? Yes. Is that very same brahmin that noble? That should not be said… ^5-83

Is there anyone who, having been a merchant, becomes a labourer, becomes a noble, becomes a brahmin? Yes. Is that very same merchant that brahmin? That should not be said… ^5-84

Is there anyone who, having been a labourer, becomes a noble, becomes a brahmin, becomes a merchant? Yes. Is that very same labourer that merchant? That should not be said… ^5-85

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does one whose hand has been cut off remain one whose hand is cut off, one whose foot has been cut off remain one whose foot is cut off, one whose hand and foot have been cut off remain one whose hand and foot are cut off; one whose ear has been cut off… whose nose has been cut off… whose ear and nose have been cut off… whose finger has been cut off… whose thumb has been cut off… whose tendon has been cut… one with a crippled hand… one with webbed fingers… one with leprosy… one with boils… one with a skin disease… one with consumption… one with epilepsy… a camel… an ox… a donkey… a pig… does a buffalo remain a buffalo? That should not be said… ^5-86

Should it not be said that "that very same person passes on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world"? Yes. But isn't it the case that a stream-enterer, passing away from the human world and reborn in the world of the gods, is a stream-enterer there too? Yes.
If a stream-enterer, passing away from the human world and reborn in the world of the gods, is a stream-enterer there too, then surely you must also say: "That very same person passes on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world." ^5-87

Since a stream-enterer, passing away from the human world and reborn in the world of the gods, is a stream-enterer there too, is it for that reason that that very same person passes on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Is it taken, then, that a stream-enterer, passing away from the human world and reborn in the world of the gods, is a human being there too? That should not be said… ^5-88

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does one pass on without becoming different, without having changed? That should not be said… ^5-89

Does one pass on without becoming different, without having changed? Yes. Does one whose hand has been cut off remain one whose hand is cut off, one whose foot has been cut off remain one whose foot is cut off, one whose hand and foot have been cut off remain one whose hand and foot are cut off; one whose ear has been cut off… whose nose has been cut off… whose ear and nose have been cut off… whose finger has been cut off… whose thumb has been cut off… whose tendon has been cut… one with a crippled hand… one with webbed fingers… one with leprosy… one with boils… one with a skin disease… one with consumption… one with epilepsy… a camel… an ox… a donkey… a pig… does a buffalo remain a buffalo? That should not be said… ^5-90

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does one pass on with material form? That should not be said… Does one pass on with material form? Yes. Is the soul the same as the body? That should not be said…
With feeling… with perception… with mental formations… does one pass on with consciousness? That should not be said… Does one pass on with consciousness? Yes. Is the soul the same as the body? That should not be said… ^5-91

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does one pass on without material form? That should not be said… Does one pass on without material form? Yes. Is the soul one thing and the body another? That should not be said…
Without feeling… without perception… without mental formations… does one pass on without consciousness? That should not be said… Does one pass on without consciousness? Yes. Is the soul one thing and the body another? That should not be said… ^5-92

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does material form pass on? That should not be said… Does material form pass on? Yes. Is the soul the same as the body? That should not be said…
Does feeling… perception… mental formations… does consciousness pass on? That should not be said… Does consciousness pass on? Yes. Is the soul the same as the body? That should not be said… ^5-93

Does that very same person pass on from this world to another world, and from another world to this world? Yes. Does material form not pass on? That should not be said… Does material form not pass on? Yes. Is the soul one thing and the body another? That should not be said…
Does feeling… perception… mental formations… does consciousness not pass on? That should not be said… Does consciousness not pass on? Yes. Is the soul one thing and the body another? That should not be said. (Abbreviated.)
When the aggregates break up, if the person breaks up too,
that becomes the view of annihilation, which the Buddha rejected.
When the aggregates break up, if the person does not break up,
the person is eternal, exactly equal to nibbāna (final release).
Inquiry into passing on. ^5-94

#### Inquiry into Dependent Designation ^5-1-16-0

Is a person designated on the basis of material form? Yes. Is material form impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. Is the person too impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? That should not be said… ^5-95

On the basis of feeling… on the basis of perception… on the basis of mental formations… is a person designated on the basis of consciousness? Yes. Is consciousness impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. Is the person too impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? That should not be said… ^5-96

Is a person designated on the basis of material form? Yes. Is a blue person designated on the basis of blue material form? That should not be said… on the basis of yellow material form… on the basis of red material form… on the basis of white material form… on the basis of visible material form… on the basis of invisible material form… on the basis of impinging material form… is a non-impinging person designated on the basis of non-impinging material form? That should not be said… ^5-97

Is a person designated on the basis of feeling? Yes. Is a wholesome person designated on the basis of wholesome feeling? That should not be said… Is a wholesome person designated on the basis of wholesome feeling? Yes. Does wholesome feeling bear fruit and have results — fruits that are desirable, lovely, pleasing and wholly satisfying, leading to happiness, with happy results? Yes. Does the wholesome person too bear fruit and have results — fruits that are desirable, lovely, pleasing and wholly satisfying, leading to happiness, with happy results? That should not be said… ^5-98

Is a person designated on the basis of feeling? Yes. Is an unwholesome person designated on the basis of unwholesome feeling? That should not be said… Is an unwholesome person designated on the basis of unwholesome feeling? Yes. Does unwholesome feeling bear fruit and have results — fruits that are undesirable, unlovely, displeasing and unsatisfying, leading to suffering, with painful results? Yes. Does the unwholesome person too bear fruit and have results — fruits that are undesirable, unlovely, displeasing and unsatisfying, leading to suffering, with painful results? That should not be said… ^5-99

Is a person designated on the basis of feeling? Yes. Is an indeterminate person designated on the basis of indeterminate feeling? That should not be said… Is an indeterminate person designated on the basis of indeterminate feeling? Yes. Is indeterminate feeling impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. Is the indeterminate person too impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? That should not be said… ^5-100

On the basis of perception… on the basis of mental formations… is a person designated on the basis of consciousness? Yes. Is a wholesome person designated on the basis of wholesome consciousness? That should not be said… Is a wholesome person designated on the basis of wholesome consciousness? Yes. Does wholesome consciousness bear fruit and have results — fruits that are desirable, lovely, pleasing and wholly satisfying, leading to happiness, with happy results? Yes. Does the wholesome person too bear fruit and have results — fruits that are desirable, lovely, pleasing and wholly satisfying, leading to happiness, with happy results? That should not be said… ^5-101

Is a person designated on the basis of consciousness? Yes. Is an unwholesome person designated on the basis of unwholesome consciousness? That should not be said… Is an unwholesome person designated on the basis of unwholesome consciousness? Yes. Does unwholesome consciousness bear fruit and have results — fruits that are undesirable, unlovely, displeasing and unsatisfying, leading to suffering, with painful results? Yes. Does the unwholesome person too bear fruit and have results — fruits that are undesirable, unlovely, displeasing and unsatisfying, leading to suffering, with painful results? That should not be said… ^5-102

Is a person designated on the basis of consciousness? Yes. Is an indeterminate person designated on the basis of indeterminate consciousness? That should not be said… Is an indeterminate person designated on the basis of indeterminate consciousness? Yes. Is indeterminate consciousness impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. Is the indeterminate person too impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? That should not be said… ^5-103

On the basis of the eye, should one say "a person with eyes"? Yes. When the eye has ceased, should one say "the person with eyes has ceased"? That should not be said… On the basis of the ear… on the basis of the nose… on the basis of the tongue… on the basis of the body… on the basis of the mind, should one say "a person with a mind"? Yes. When the mind has ceased, should one say "the person with a mind has ceased"? That should not be said. ^5-104

On the basis of wrong view, should one say "a person of wrong view"? Yes. When the wrong view has ceased, should one say "the person of wrong view has ceased"? That should not be said. On the basis of wrong intention… on the basis of wrong speech… on the basis of wrong action… on the basis of wrong livelihood… on the basis of wrong effort… on the basis of wrong mindfulness… on the basis of wrong concentration, should one say "a person of wrong concentration"? Yes. When the wrong concentration has ceased, should one say "the person of wrong concentration has ceased"? That should not be said. ^5-105

On the basis of right view, should one say "a person of right view"? Yes. When the right view has ceased, should one say "the person of right view has ceased"? That should not be said… on the basis of right intention… on the basis of right speech… on the basis of right action… on the basis of right livelihood… on the basis of right effort… on the basis of right mindfulness… on the basis of right concentration, should one say "a person of right concentration"? Yes. When the right concentration has ceased, should one say "the person of right concentration has ceased"? That should not be said… ^5-106

Is a person designated on the basis of material form and on the basis of feeling? Yes. Are two persons designated on the basis of two aggregates? That should not be said… Is a person designated on the basis of material form, on the basis of feeling, on the basis of perception, on the basis of mental formations, on the basis of consciousness? Yes. Are five persons designated on the basis of five aggregates? That should not be said… ^5-107

Is a person designated on the basis of the eye base and on the basis of the ear base? Yes. Are two persons designated on the basis of two sense bases? That should not be said… Is a person designated on the basis of the eye base, on the basis of the ear base… on the basis of the base of mental objects? Yes. Are twelve persons designated on the basis of twelve sense bases? That should not be said… ^5-108

Is a person designated on the basis of the eye element and on the basis of the ear element? Yes. Are two persons designated on the basis of two elements? That should not be said… Is a person designated on the basis of the eye element, on the basis of the ear element… on the basis of the element of mental objects? Yes. Are eighteen persons designated on the basis of eighteen elements? That should not be said… ^5-109

Is a person designated on the basis of the eye faculty and on the basis of the ear faculty? Yes. Are two persons designated on the basis of two faculties? That should not be said… Is a person designated on the basis of the eye faculty, on the basis of the ear faculty… on the basis of the faculty of one who has final knowledge? Yes. Are twenty-two [variant: bāvīsatiyā (?)] persons designated on the basis of twenty-two faculties? That should not be said… ^5-110

Is one person designated on the basis of single-aggregate existence? Yes. Are four persons designated on the basis of four-aggregate existence? That should not be said… Is one person designated on the basis of single-aggregate existence? Yes. Are five persons designated on the basis of five-aggregate existence? That should not be said… In single-aggregate existence, is there just one person? Yes. In four-aggregate existence, are there just four [variant: cattāro (?)] persons? That should not be said… In single-aggregate existence, is there just one person? Yes. In five-aggregate existence, are there just five persons? That should not be said… ^5-111

Just as a shadow is designated on the basis of a tree, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form? ( ) [(Yes.) (?) — so too in the three rounds that follow] Just as a shadow is designated on the basis of a tree, and the tree is impermanent and the shadow too is impermanent, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form, and is material form impermanent and the person too impermanent? That should not be said… Just as a shadow is designated on the basis of a tree, and the tree is one thing and the shadow another, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form, and is material form one thing and the person another? That should not be said… ^5-112

Just as a villager is designated on the basis of a village, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form? Just as a villager is designated on the basis of a village, and the village is one thing and the villager another, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form, and is material form one thing and the person another? That should not be said… ^5-113

Just as a king is designated on the basis of a kingdom, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form? Just as a king is designated on the basis of a kingdom, and the kingdom is one thing and the king another, in the same way is a person designated on the basis of material form, and is material form one thing and the person another? That should not be said… ^5-114

Just as the shackle is not the shackled one, but the one who has the shackle is the shackled one, in the same way is material form not the possessor of material form, but the one who has material form the possessor of material form? Just as the shackle is not the shackled one, but the one who has the shackle is the shackled one, and the shackle is one thing and the shackled one another, in the same way is material form not the possessor of material form, the one who has material form the possessor of material form, and is material form one thing and the possessor of material form another? That should not be said… ^5-115

Is a person designated with each moment of mind? Yes. With each moment of mind, is a person born, does a person grow old, die, pass away and get reborn? That should not be said… When a second moment of mind has arisen, should one not say "it is the same one" or "it is another"? Yes. When a second moment of mind has arisen, should one not say "a boy" or "a girl"? It should be said.
Acknowledge the refutation. If, when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say "the same one" or "another," then surely you must also say: "When a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say ‘a boy’ or ‘a girl’." What you say here — that it should be said that "when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say ‘the same one’ or ‘another’, but when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say ‘a boy’ or ‘a girl’" — is wrong.
Or else, if, when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say "a boy" or "a girl," then surely you must also say: "When a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say ‘the same one’ or ‘another’." What you say here — that it should be said that "when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say ‘the same one’ or ‘another’, but when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say ‘a boy’ or ‘a girl’" — is wrong. ^5-116

When a second moment of mind has arisen, should one not say "the same one" or "another"? Yes. When a second moment of mind has arisen, should one not say "a woman" or "a man" or "a householder" or "one who has gone forth" or "a god" or "a human being"? It should be said.
Acknowledge the refutation. If, when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say "the same one" or "another," then surely you must also say: "When a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say ‘a god’ or ‘a human being’." What you say here — that it should be said that "when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say ‘the same one’ or ‘another’, but when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say ‘a god’ or ‘a human being’" — is wrong.
Or else, if, when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say "a god" or "a human being," then surely you must also say: "When a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say ‘the same one’ or ‘another’." What you say here — that it should be said that "when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should not say ‘the same one’ or ‘another’, but when a second moment of mind has arisen, one should say ‘a god’ or ‘a human being’" — is wrong… ^5-117

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't it the case that whoever sees, whatever they see, by whatever means they see — that one sees, sees that, sees by that means? Yes. If whoever sees, whatever they see, by whatever means they see — that one sees, sees that, sees by that means — then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-118

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't it the case that whoever hears… whoever smells… whoever tastes… whoever touches… whoever knows, whatever they know, by whatever means they know — that one knows, knows that, knows by that means? Yes. If whoever knows, whatever they know, by whatever means they know — that one knows, knows that, knows by that means — then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-119

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't it the case that whoever does not see, whatever they do not see, by whatever means they do not see — that one does not see, does not see that, does not see by that means? Yes. If whoever does not see, whatever they do not see, by whatever means they do not see — that one does not see, does not see that, does not see by that means — then surely you must not say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact."
Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't it the case that whoever does not hear… whoever does not smell… whoever does not taste… whoever does not touch… whoever does not know, whatever they do not know, by whatever means they do not know — that one does not know, does not know that, does not know by that means? Yes. If whoever does not know, whatever they do not know, by whatever means they do not know — that one does not know, does not know that, does not know by that means — then surely you must not say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-120

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, I see beings passing away and being reborn — low and high, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and in bad destinations — and I understand how beings fare according to their actions" [M. Ni. 1.213, slightly different]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, a person is found as a real and ultimate fact. ^5-121

Since the Blessed One said, "Monks, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, I see beings passing away and being reborn — low and high, beautiful and ugly, in good destinations and in bad destinations — and I understand how beings fare according to their actions," is it for that very reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, does the Blessed One see material form, or does he see a person? He sees material form. Is material form the person; does material form pass away, is material form reborn, does material form fare according to its actions? That should not be said.
With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, does the Blessed One see material form, or does he see a person? He sees a person. Is the person material form, the visible-form base, the visible-form element; is it blue, yellow, red or white; is it knowable by the eye; does it strike against the eye; does it come within the range of the eye? That should not be said.
With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, does the Blessed One see material form, or does he see a person? He sees both. Are both material form, the visible-form base, the visible-form element; are both blue, both yellow, both red, both white; are both knowable by the eye; do both strike against the eye; do both come within the range of the eye; do both pass away, are both reborn, do both fare according to their actions? That should not be said.
Inquiry into dependent designation. ^5-122

#### Inquiry into Human Agency ^5-1-17-0

Are good and bad actions found? Yes. Is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? That should not be said… ^5-123

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is a doer and instigator of that one found? That should not be said… ^5-124

Is a doer and instigator of that one found? Yes. Then for each one in turn is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no complete nibbāna without clinging? That should not be said… ^5-125

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is a person found, and is a doer and instigator of the person found? That should not be said… ^5-126

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is nibbāna found, and is a doer and instigator of nibbāna found? That should not be said… ^5-127

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is the great earth found, and is a doer and instigator of the great earth found? That should not be said… ^5-128

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is the great ocean found, and is a doer and instigator of the great ocean found? That should not be said… ^5-129

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is water found, and is a doer and instigator of water found? That should not be said… ^5-131

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is air found, and is a doer and instigator of air found? That should not be said… ^5-133

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Are grass, wood and trees found, and is a doer and instigator of grass, wood and trees found? That should not be said… ^5-134

Are good and bad actions found, and is a doer and instigator of good and bad actions found? Yes. Are good and bad actions one thing, and the doer and instigator of good and bad actions another? That should not be said… ^5-135

Is the result of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is one who experiences the result of good and bad actions found? That should not be said… ^5-136

Is the result of good and bad actions found, and is one who experiences the result of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is one who experiences that one found? That should not be said… ^5-137

Is one who experiences that one found? Yes. Then for each one in turn is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no complete nibbāna without clinging? That should not be said… ^5-138

Is the result of good and bad actions found, and is one who experiences the result of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is a person found, and is one who experiences the person found? That should not be said… ^5-139

Is the result of good and bad actions found, and is one who experiences the result of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is nibbāna found, and is one who experiences nibbāna found? That should not be said… ^5-140

Is the result of good and bad actions found, and is one who experiences the result of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is the great earth found… is the great ocean found… is Sineru, king of mountains, found… is water found… is fire found… is air found… are grass, wood and trees found, and is one who experiences grass, wood and trees found? That should not be said… ^5-141

Is the result of good and bad actions found, and is one who experiences the result of good and bad actions found? Yes. Is the result of good and bad actions one thing, and the one who experiences the result of good and bad actions another? That should not be said… ^5-142

Is heavenly happiness found? Yes. Is one who experiences heavenly happiness found? That should not be said… ^5-143

Is heavenly happiness found, and is one who experiences heavenly happiness found? Yes. Is one who experiences that one found? That should not be said… ^5-144

Is one who experiences that one found? Yes. Then for each one in turn is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no complete nibbāna without clinging? That should not be said… ^5-145

Is heavenly happiness found, and is one who experiences heavenly happiness found? Yes. Is a person found, and is one who experiences the person found? That should not be said… ^5-146

Is heavenly happiness found, and is one who experiences heavenly happiness found? Yes. Is nibbāna found, and is one who experiences nibbāna found? That should not be said… ^5-147

Is heavenly happiness found, and is one who experiences heavenly happiness found? Yes. Is the great earth found… is the great ocean found… is Sineru, king of mountains, found… is water found… is fire found… is air found… are grass, wood and trees found, and is one who experiences grass, wood and trees found? That should not be said… ^5-148

Is heavenly happiness found, and is one who experiences heavenly happiness found? Yes. Is heavenly happiness one thing, and the one who experiences heavenly happiness another? That should not be said… ^5-149

#### Inquiry into the Higher Knowledges ^5-1-18-0

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't there someone who performs feats of psychic power? Yes. If there is someone who performs feats of psychic power, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-193

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't there someone who hears sounds with the divine ear… who knows the minds of others… who recollects past lives… who sees forms with the divine eye… who realizes the destruction of the taints? Yes. If there is someone who realizes the destruction of the taints, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-194

Since there is someone who performs feats of psychic power, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is whoever performs feats of psychic power a person? And is whoever does not perform feats of psychic power not a person? That should not be said… ^5-195

Is whoever hears sounds with the divine ear… whoever knows the minds of others… whoever recollects past lives… whoever sees forms with the divine eye… whoever realizes the destruction of the taints a person? And is whoever does not realize the destruction of the taints not a person? That should not be said…
Inquiry into the higher knowledges. ^5-196

#### 15-18. Inquiry into Relatives and So On ^5-1-19-0

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But doesn't a mother exist? Yes. If a mother exists, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-197

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But doesn't a father exist… a brother… a sister… a noble… a brahmin… a merchant… a labourer… a householder… one who has gone forth… a god… doesn't a human being exist? Yes. If a human being exists, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-198

Since a mother exists, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is there anyone who, not having been a mother, becomes a mother? Yes. Is there anyone who, not having been a person, becomes a person? That should not be said… Is there anyone who, not having been a father… not having been a brother… a sister… a noble… a brahmin… a merchant… a labourer… a householder… one who has gone forth… a god… not having been a human being, becomes a human being? Yes. Is there anyone who, not having been a person, becomes a person? That should not be said… ^5-199

Since a mother exists, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a mother, becomes not a mother? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, becomes not a person? That should not be said…
Is there anyone who, having been a father… a brother… a sister… a noble… a brahmin… a merchant… a labourer… a householder… one who has gone forth… a god… having been a human being, becomes not a human being? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, becomes not a person? That should not be said… ^5-200

#### Inquiry into Realization ^5-1-20-0

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But doesn't a stream-enterer exist? Yes. If a stream-enterer exists, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-201

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But doesn't a once-returner exist… a non-returner… a worthy one (arahant)… one liberated in both ways… one liberated by wisdom… a body-witness [variant: kāyasakkhī (Syā.)]… one attained to view… one liberated by faith… a Dhamma-follower… doesn't a faith-follower exist? Yes.
If a faith-follower exists, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-202

Since a stream-enterer exists, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is there anyone who, not having been a stream-enterer, becomes a stream-enterer? Yes. Is there anyone who, not having been a person, becomes a person? That should not be said… ^5-203

Is there anyone who, not having been a once-returner… not having been a non-returner… not having been a worthy one… not having been one liberated in both ways… not having been one liberated by wisdom… not having been a body-witness… not having been one attained to view… not having been one liberated by faith… not having been a Dhamma-follower… not having been a faith-follower, becomes a faith-follower? Yes. Is there anyone who, not having been a person, becomes a person? That should not be said… ^5-204

Since a stream-enterer exists, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a stream-enterer, becomes not a stream-enterer? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, becomes not a person? That should not be said…
Is there anyone who, having been a once-returner… having been a non-returner, becomes not a non-returner? Yes. Is there anyone who, having been a person, becomes not a person? That should not be said…
Inquiry into realization. ^5-205

#### Inquiry into the Community ^5-1-21-0

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But don't the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, exist? Yes. If the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, exist, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-206

Since the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, exist, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Do the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, appear because a Buddha appears? Yes. Does the person appear because a Buddha appears? That should not be said…
Does the person appear because a Buddha appears? Yes. When the Buddha, the Blessed One, has attained final nibbāna, is the person cut off — is there no person? That should not be said…

#### Inquiry into the Nature of Real Fact ^5-1-22-0

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is the person conditioned? That should not be said… Is the person unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? That should not be said. ^5-208

Is the person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Apart from the conditioned and the unconditioned, is there some other, third category? That should not be said… ^5-209

Apart from the conditioned and the unconditioned, is there some other, third category? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these two elements. Which two? The conditioned element and the unconditioned element. These, monks, are the two elements" [M. Ni. 1.125; differs only in the form of address]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "apart from the conditioned and the unconditioned, there is some other, third category." ^5-210

Is the person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Is the conditioned one thing, the unconditioned another, and the person another? That should not be said… ^5-211

Are the aggregates conditioned, is nibbāna unconditioned, and is the person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Are the aggregates one thing, nibbāna another, and the person another? That should not be said… ^5-212

Is material form conditioned, is nibbāna unconditioned, and is the person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Is material form one thing, nibbāna another, and the person another? That should not be said. Is feeling… perception… are mental formations… is consciousness conditioned, is nibbāna unconditioned, and is the person neither conditioned nor unconditioned? Yes. Is consciousness one thing, nibbāna another, and the person another? That should not be said… ^5-213

Is a person's arising evident, is its passing away evident, is its change while it lasts evident? Yes. Is the person conditioned? That should not be said… The Blessed One said: "Monks, there are these three characteristics of the conditioned that mark it as conditioned. Of conditioned things [variant: katamāni tīṇi (A. Ni. 3.47)], monks, arising is evident, passing away is evident, and change while they last is evident" [A. Ni. 3.47]. A person's arising is evident, its passing away is evident, its change while it lasts is evident; in that case, the person is conditioned. ^5-214

Is a person's arising not evident, is its passing away not evident, is its change while it lasts not evident? Yes. Is the person unconditioned? That should not be said… The Blessed One said: "Monks, there are these three characteristics of the unconditioned that mark it as unconditioned. Of unconditioned things, monks, no arising is evident, no passing away is evident, and no change while they last is evident" [A. Ni. 3.48]. A person's arising is not evident, its passing away is not evident, its change while it lasts is not evident; in that case, the person is unconditioned. ^5-215

Is the person who has attained final nibbāna in the state of existing, or in the state of not existing? In the state of existing. Is the person who has attained final nibbāna eternal? That should not be said… In the state of not existing. Is the person who has attained final nibbāna annihilated? That should not be said… ^5-216

On what does a person depend in order to continue? It continues in dependence on existence. Is existence impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. Is the person too impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? That should not be said… ^5-217

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't there someone who, when feeling a pleasant feeling, understands: "I am feeling a pleasant feeling"? Yes. If there is someone who, when feeling a pleasant feeling, understands: "I am feeling a pleasant feeling," then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-218

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't there someone who, when feeling a painful feeling… when feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands: "I am feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling"? Yes. If there is someone who, when feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands: "I am feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling," then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-219

Since there is someone who, when feeling a pleasant feeling, understands: "I am feeling a pleasant feeling," is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is whoever, when feeling a pleasant feeling, understands "I am feeling a pleasant feeling" a person; and is whoever, when feeling a pleasant feeling, does not understand "I am feeling a pleasant feeling" not a person? That should not be said…
Is whoever, when feeling a painful feeling… whoever, when feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands "I am feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling" a person; and is whoever, when feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, does not understand "I am feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling" not a person? That should not be said… ^5-220

Since there is someone who, when feeling a pleasant feeling, understands: "I am feeling a pleasant feeling," is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is the pleasant feeling one thing, and the one who, when feeling a pleasant feeling, understands "I am feeling a pleasant feeling" another? That should not be said… Is the painful feeling one thing… Is the neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling one thing, and the one who, when feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, understands "I am feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling" another? That should not be said… ^5-221

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't there someone who dwells contemplating the body as a body? Yes. If there is someone who dwells contemplating the body as a body, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-222

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't there someone who dwells contemplating feelings as feelings… the mind as mind… mental objects as mental objects? Yes. If there is someone who dwells contemplating mental objects as mental objects, then surely you must also say: "A person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-223

Since there is someone who dwells contemplating the body as a body, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is whoever dwells contemplating the body as a body a person; and is whoever does not dwell contemplating the body as a body not a person? That should not be said…
Is whoever dwells contemplating feelings as feelings… the mind as mind… mental objects as mental objects a person; and is whoever does not dwell contemplating mental objects as mental objects not a person? That should not be said… ^5-224

Since there is someone who dwells contemplating the body as a body, is it for that reason that a person is found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. Is the body one thing, and the one who dwells contemplating the body as a body another? That should not be said… Are feelings one thing… is the mind one thing… are mental objects one thing, and the one who dwells contemplating mental objects as mental objects another? That should not be said… ^5-225

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Look on the world as empty, Mogharāja, always mindful;
uprooting [variant: ohacca (Syā.), uhacca (Ka.)] the view of self, one may in this way cross beyond death;
one who looks on the world in this way, the King of Death does not see" [Su. Ni. 1125; Cūḷani. 88, Exposition of the Question of the Young Man Mogharāja]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-226

Does a person look? Yes. Does it look together with material form, or does it look without material form? It looks together with material form. Is the soul the same as the body? That should not be said… It looks without material form — then is the soul one thing and the body another? That should not be said… ^5-227

Does a person look? Yes. Does it look from within, or does it look after going outside? It looks from within. Is the soul the same as the body? That should not be said… It looks after going outside — then is the soul one thing and the body another? That should not be said… ^5-228

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. The Blessed One said: "There is a person who is practising for their own welfare." Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, a person is found as a real and ultimate fact. ^5-229

Should it not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact"? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. The Blessed One said: "Monks, there is one person who, arising in the world, arises for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, the welfare and the happiness of gods and humans" [A. Ni. 1.162-169]. Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, a person is found as a real and ultimate fact. ^5-230

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. The Blessed One said: "All things are not-self" [M. Ni. 1.356; Dha. Pa. 279, in the Dhammapada]. Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-231

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. The Blessed One said: "One has no doubt and no uncertainty that what arises is only suffering arising, and what ceases is only suffering [variant: dukkhaṃ (S. Ni. 2.15)] ceasing; one's knowledge of this does not depend on anyone else. It is to this extent, Kaccāna, that there is right view" [S. Ni. 2.15]. Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-232

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But didn't the nun Vajirā say this to Māra the Evil One:
"Why do you believe in ‘a being’, Māra? Is that a speculative view of yours?
This is a heap of mere formations; no being is found here.
"Just as [variant: yathāpi (many editions)], when the parts are put together, the word ‘chariot’ is used,
so, when the aggregates are present, there is the convention [variant: sammati (Syā., Kaṃ.)] ‘a being’.
"It is only suffering that comes into being; suffering stays and passes away;
nothing but suffering comes into being, nothing but suffering ceases" [S. Ni. 1.171]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-233

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But didn't the venerable Ānanda say this to the Blessed One: "‘The world is empty, the world is empty,’ it is said, venerable sir. In what way, venerable sir, is it said that ‘the world is empty’?" "Because, Ānanda, it is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, therefore it is said that ‘the world is empty’. And what, Ānanda, is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self? The eye, Ānanda, is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self; visible forms are empty… eye-consciousness is empty… eye-contact is empty… whatever is felt — pleasant, painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that arises with eye-contact as its condition, that too is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self. The ear is empty… sounds are empty… the nose is empty… smells are empty… the tongue is empty… tastes are empty… the body is empty… touches are empty… the mind is empty… mental objects are empty… mind-consciousness is empty… mind-contact is empty… whatever is felt — pleasant, painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that arises with mind-contact as its condition, that too is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self. Because, Ānanda, it is empty of a self or of what belongs to a self, therefore it is said that ‘the world is empty’" [S. Ni. 4.85]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-234

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. The Blessed One said: "Monks, if there were a self, would there be ‘what belongs to my self’?" "Yes, venerable sir." "Or, monks, if there were what belongs to a self, would there be ‘my self’?" "Yes, venerable sir." "Monks, since a self and what belongs to a self are not found [variant: anupalabbhamāne (M. Ni. 1.244)] as true and established, then this standpoint for views [variant: yamidaṃ (Syā.) yampitaṃ (M. Ni. 1.244)] — ‘That is the world, that is the self; after death I shall be permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change; I shall stay just like that for ever and ever’ — is this not, monks, wholly and completely a fool's teaching?" "What else could it be, venerable sir? It is wholly and completely a fool's teaching, venerable sir" [M. Ni. 1.244]. Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-235

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. The Blessed One said: "Seniya, there are these three teachers found existing in the world. Which three? Here, Seniya, a certain teacher declares a self as true and established in this present life, and declares a self as true and established in the life to come.
"Then again, Seniya, a certain teacher declares a self as true and established in this present life, but does not declare a self as true and established in the life to come.
"Then again, Seniya, a certain teacher does not declare a self as true and established in this present life, and does not declare a self as true and established in the life to come.
"Of these, Seniya, the teacher who declares a self as true and established in this present life, and declares a self as true and established in the life to come — this one, Seniya, is called the eternalist teacher.
"Of these, Seniya, the teacher who declares a self as true and established in this present life, but does not declare a self as true and established in the life to come — this one, Seniya, is called the annihilationist teacher.
"Of these, Seniya, the teacher who does not declare a self as true and established in this present life, and does not declare a self as true and established in the life to come — this one, Seniya, is called the teacher who is the Fully Awakened One. These, Seniya, are the three teachers found existing in the world" [Pu. Pa. 131, in the Puggalapaññatti; the same in meaning]. Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-236

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. Did the Blessed One speak of "a ghee pot"? Yes. Is there anyone who makes a pot out of ghee? That should not be said… In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." ^5-237

Is a person found as a real and ultimate fact? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One one who speaks the truth, speaks at the right time, speaks of what is real, speaks of things as they are, speaks without error, speaks without deviation? Yes. Did the Blessed One speak of "an oil pot… a honey pot… a molasses pot… a milk pot… a water pot… a drinking-water dish… a drinking-water cup… a drinking-water bowl… a permanent meal… constant rice gruel"? Yes. Is there any rice gruel that is permanent, constant, eternal, not subject to change? That should not be said… In that case it should not be said that "a person is found as a real and ultimate fact." (Abbreviated.)
The eightfold refutation with its abbreviated repetitions; passing on; dependent designation;
with the moment of mind, the fifth; the good; with psychic power and the citing of discourses, the eighth.
Inquiry into the nature of real fact.
The Discussion of the Person is finished. ^5-238
