Is there really such a discourse? Yes. If "for one who has entered the first meditative absorption, speech has ceased," and there really is such a discourse, then surely you must not say: "One in a meditative attainment has verbal expression."
Since "for one who has entered the first meditative absorption, speech has ceased" [S. Ni. 4.259, 263], and there really is such a discourse, does that one have verbal expression? Yes. Since "for one who has entered the second meditative absorption, thinking and examining have ceased" [S. Ni. 4.259, 263], and there really is such a discourse, does that one have thinking and examining? That should not be said…
Since "for one who has entered the first meditative absorption, speech has ceased" [S. Ni. 4.259, 263], and there really is such a discourse, does that one have verbal expression? Yes. Since "for one who has entered the third meditative absorption, joy has ceased; for one who has entered the fourth meditative absorption, in-and-out breathing has ceased; for one who has entered the base of the infinity of space, the perception of material form has ceased; for one who has entered the base of the infinity of consciousness, the perception of the base of the infinity of space has ceased; for one who has entered the base of nothingness, the perception of the base of the infinity of consciousness has ceased; for one who has entered the base of neither perception nor non-perception, the perception of the base of nothingness has ceased; for one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling have ceased" [S. Ni. 4.259, 263; A. Ni. 9.31; D. Ni. 3.344], and there really is such a discourse, does that one have perception and feeling? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "one in a meditative attainment has verbal expression"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One said that sound is a thorn [variant: kaṇṭako (Syā.), A. Ni. 10.72] to the first meditative absorption [the question is asked on the basis of the Thorn Discourse, A. Ni. 10.72]? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first meditative absorption, then surely you must also say: "One in a meditative attainment has verbal expression."
Since the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first meditative absorption, does one in a meditative attainment have verbal expression? Yes. The Blessed One has said that thinking and examining are a thorn to the second meditative absorption… that joy is a thorn to the third meditative absorption… that in-and-out breathing is a thorn to the fourth meditative absorption [A. Ni. 10.72]… that the perception of material form is a thorn for one who has entered the base of the infinity of space… that the perception of the base of the infinity of space is a thorn for one who has entered the base of the infinity of consciousness… that the perception of the base of the infinity of consciousness is a thorn for one who has entered the base of nothingness… that the perception of the base of nothingness is a thorn for one who has entered the base of neither perception nor non-perception… that perception and feeling are a thorn for one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling [A. Ni. 10.72] — does that one have perception and feeling? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "one in a meditative attainment has verbal expression"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Ānanda, a disciple named Abhibhū of the Blessed One Sikhī, the worthy one (arahant), the Fully Awakened One, standing in the Brahmā world, made his voice heard throughout the ten-thousandfold world system:
‘Make an effort, go forth, apply yourselves to the Buddha's teaching;
shake off the army of death as an elephant shakes a hut of reeds.
‘Whoever dwells heedful [variant: vihessati (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ.), viharissati (Ka.)] in this Dhamma and discipline
will abandon the round of births and make an end of suffering’" [A. Ni. 1, in the Book of Threes; S. Ni. 1.285]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one in a meditative attainment has verbal expression.
The Discussion of Verbal Expression is finished. ^5-333

#### The Second Chapter ^5-10-7-0

##### (15) 6. Discussion of Uttering "Suffering" ^5-10-7-1-0

Is uttering "suffering" a factor of the path, included in the path? Yes. Do all who speak the word "suffering" develop the path? That should not be said.
Do all who speak the word "suffering" develop the path? Yes. Foolish ordinary people speak the word "suffering" — do foolish ordinary people develop the path? That should not be said. A killer of their mother… a killer of their father… a killer of a worthy one (arahant)… a shedder of a Buddha's blood [variant: lohituppādako (Sī., Ka.); but elsewhere only "ruhiruppādako" is found]… a splitter of the Community speaks the word "suffering" — does the splitter of the Community develop the path? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Uttering "Suffering" is finished. ^5-334

#### The Second Chapter ^5-10-8-0

##### (16) 7. Discussion of the Duration of Mind ^5-10-8-1-0

Does a single state of mind last for a day? Yes. Is half a day its moment of arising, and half a day its moment of passing away? That should not be said.
Does a single state of mind last for two days? Yes. Is a day its moment of arising, and a day its moment of passing away? That should not be said.
Does a single state of mind last for four days… last for eight days… last for ten days… last for twenty days… last for a month… last for two months… last for four months… last for eight months… last for ten months… last for a year… last for two years… last for four years… last for eight years… last for ten years… last for twenty years… last for thirty years… last for forty years… last for fifty years… last for a hundred years… last for two hundred years… last for four hundred years… last for five hundred years… last for a thousand years… last for two thousand years… last for four thousand years… last for eight thousand years… last for sixteen thousand years… last for an aeon (world-age)… last for two aeons… last for four aeons… last for eight aeons… last for sixteen aeons… last for thirty-two aeons… last for sixty-four aeons… last for five hundred aeons… last for thousands of aeons… last for two thousand aeons… last for four thousand aeons… last for eight thousand aeons… last for sixteen thousand aeons… last for twenty thousand aeons… last for forty thousand aeons… last for sixty thousand aeons… last for eighty-four thousand aeons? Yes. Are forty-two thousand aeons its moment of arising, and forty-two thousand aeons its moment of passing away? That should not be said.
Does a single state of mind last for a day? Yes. Are there other things that arise and cease many times in a single day? Yes. Do those things change more quickly than the mind? That should not be said.
Do those things change more quickly than the mind? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, I do not see any other single thing that changes as quickly as the mind. So much so, monks, that it is not easy even to find a simile for how quickly the mind changes" [A. Ni. 1.48]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "those things change more quickly than the mind."
Do those things change more quickly than the mind? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Just as, monks, a monkey roaming through a forest, through a great wood, grabs hold of a branch, lets go of it and grabs another, lets go of that and grabs another; in the same way, monks, what [variant: yadidaṃ (many editions)] is called ‘mind’, or ‘mentality’, or ‘consciousness’ arises as one thing and ceases as another, by night and by day" [S. Ni. 2.61]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "those things change more quickly than the mind." ^5-335

Does a single state of mind last for a day? Yes. Does eye-consciousness last for a day? That should not be said. Does ear-consciousness… nose-consciousness… tongue-consciousness… body-consciousness… an unwholesome state of mind… a state of mind accompanied by greed… accompanied by hatred… accompanied by delusion… accompanied by conceit… accompanied by wrong view… accompanied by doubt… accompanied by sluggishness… accompanied by restlessness… accompanied by shamelessness… a state of mind accompanied by lack of moral fear last for a day? That should not be said…
Does a single state of mind last for a day? Yes. With the very same state of mind with which one sees a visible form with the eye, does one hear a sound with the ear… smell a smell with the nose… taste a taste with the tongue… feel a touch with the body… know a mental object with the mind… with the very same state of mind with which one knows a mental object with the mind, does one see a visible form with the eye… hear a sound with the ear… smell a smell with the nose… taste a taste with the tongue… feel a touch with the body? That should not be said…
Does a single state of mind last for a day? Yes. With the very same state of mind with which one goes forward, does one go back; with the very same state of mind with which one goes back, does one go forward; with the very same state of mind with which one looks ahead, does one look around; with the very same state of mind with which one looks around, does one look ahead; with the very same state of mind with which one bends a limb, does one stretch it; with the very same state of mind with which one stretches a limb, does one bend it? That should not be said… ^5-336

Does a single state of mind of the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space last for their whole life span? Yes. Does a single state of mind of human beings last for their whole life span? That should not be said.
Does a single state of mind of the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space last for their whole life span? Yes. Does a single state of mind of the gods of the Four Great Kings… of the Thirty-three gods… of the Yāma gods… of the Tusita gods… of the gods who delight in creating… of the gods who wield power over the creations of others… of the gods of Brahmā's assembly… of the gods who are Brahmā's ministers… of the Great Brahmā gods… of the gods of limited radiance… of the gods of boundless radiance… of the gods of streaming radiance… of the gods of limited glory… of the gods of boundless glory… of the gods of refulgent glory… of the gods of great fruit… of the Aviha gods… of the Atappa gods… of the Sudassa gods… of the Sudassī gods… of the Akaniṭṭha gods last for their whole life span? That should not be said.
The gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space have a life span of twenty thousand aeons — does a single state of mind of the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space last for twenty thousand aeons? Yes. Human beings have a life span of a hundred years — does a single state of mind of human beings last for a hundred years? That should not be said.
The gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space have a life span of twenty thousand aeons — does a single state of mind of the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space last for twenty thousand aeons? Yes. The gods of the Four Great Kings have a life span of five hundred years — does a single state of mind of the gods of the Four Great Kings last for five hundred years… last for a thousand years… last for two thousand years… last for four thousand years… last for eight thousand years… last for sixteen thousand years… last for a third of an aeon… last for half an aeon… last for one aeon… last for two aeons… last for four aeons… last for eight aeons… last for sixteen aeons… last for thirty-two aeons… last for sixty-four aeons… last for five hundred aeons… last for a thousand aeons… last for two thousand aeons… last for four thousand aeons… last for eight thousand aeons… the Akaniṭṭha gods have a life span of sixteen thousand aeons — does a single state of mind of the Akaniṭṭha gods last for sixteen thousand aeons? That should not be said.
Does the mind of the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space arise from moment to moment and cease from moment to moment? Yes. Do the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space pass away from moment to moment and are they reborn from moment to moment? That should not be said.
Does a single state of mind of the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space last for their whole life span? Yes. Do the gods reborn in the base of the infinity of space pass away with the very same state of mind with which they are reborn? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Duration of Mind is finished. ^5-337

#### The Second Chapter ^5-10-9-0

##### (17) 8. Discussion of Hot Embers ^5-10-9-1-0

Are all formations (conditioned things), without exception, hot embers? Yes. But isn't there pleasant feeling, bodily happiness, mental happiness, heavenly happiness, human happiness, the happiness of gain, the happiness of honour, the happiness of vehicles, the happiness of beds, the happiness of sovereignty, the happiness of lordship, the happiness of the householder, the happiness of the ascetic life, happiness with taints, happiness without taints, happiness bound up with attachments, happiness free from attachments, material happiness, non-material happiness, happiness with joy, happiness without joy, the happiness of meditative absorption (jhāna), the happiness of liberation, the happiness of sensual pleasure, the happiness of renunciation, the happiness of seclusion, the happiness of peace, the happiness of awakening? Yes. If there is pleasant feeling… the happiness of awakening, then surely you must not say: "All formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Are all formations, without exception, hot embers? Yes. Are all formations painful feeling, bodily pain, mental pain, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair? That should not be said.
Should it not be said that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, all is burning! And what, monks, is the all that is burning? The eye, monks, is burning, visible forms are burning, eye-consciousness is burning, eye-contact is burning; and whatever is felt [variant: yampidaṃ (S. Ni. 4.28)] that arises in dependence on eye-contact — whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant — that too is burning. Burning with what? ‘Burning with the fire of greed, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, ageing and death, with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs and despairs,’ I say. The ear is burning, sounds are burning… the nose is burning, smells are burning… the tongue is burning, tastes are burning… the body is burning, touches are burning… the mind is burning, mental objects are burning, mind-consciousness is burning, mind-contact is burning; and whatever is felt that arises in dependence on mind-contact — whether pleasant or painful or neither painful nor pleasant — that too is burning. Burning with what? ‘Burning with the fire of greed, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, ageing and death, with sorrows, lamentations, pains, griefs and despairs,’ I say" [Mahāva. 54; S. Ni. 4.28]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should be said [variant: tena hi (Sī., Syā.), tena hi na vattabbaṃ (Ka.)] that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Are all formations, without exception, hot embers? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. Which five? Visible forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire and enticing; sounds cognizable by the ear… smells cognizable by the nose… tastes cognizable by the tongue… touches cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire and enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure" [M. Ni. 1.166; S. Ni. 4.268]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Should it not be said that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "It is a gain for you, monks, it is well gained by you, monks, you have obtained [variant: paṭividdho (many editions)] the right moment for living the holy life (the life of spiritual training)! Monks, I have seen the hells called ‘of the six bases of contact’. There, whatever visible form one sees with the eye, one sees only what is undesirable, not what is desirable; one sees only what is unlovely, not what is lovely; one sees only what is disagreeable, not what is agreeable. Whatever sound one hears with the ear… smell one smells with the nose… taste one tastes with the tongue… touch one feels with the body… mental object one knows with the mind, one knows only what is undesirable, not what is desirable; one knows only what is unlovely, not what is lovely; one knows only what is disagreeable, not what is agreeable" [S. Ni. 4.135]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should be said [variant: tena hi na vattabbaṃ (Syā., Ka.)] that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Are all formations, without exception, hot embers? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "It is a gain for you, monks, it is well gained by you, monks, you have obtained the right moment for living the holy life! Monks, I have seen the heavens called ‘of the six bases of contact’. There, whatever visible form one sees with the eye, one sees only what is desirable, not what is undesirable; one sees only what is lovely, not what is unlovely; one sees only what is agreeable, not what is disagreeable. Whatever sound one hears with the ear… smell one smells with the nose… taste one tastes with the tongue… touch one feels with the body… mental object one knows with the mind, one knows only what is desirable, not what is undesirable; one knows only what is lovely, not what is unlovely; one knows only what is agreeable, not what is disagreeable" [S. Ni. 4.135]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Should it not be said that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One said: "What is impermanent is suffering" [S. Ni. 3.15], and "All formations are impermanent" [Dha. Pa. 277; M. Ni. 1.356]? Yes. If the Blessed One has said: "What is impermanent is suffering," and "All formations are impermanent," then surely you must also say: "All formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Are all formations, without exception, hot embers? Yes. Is giving something whose fruit is undesirable, unlovely, disagreeable and unsatisfying, with suffering as its outcome and suffering as its result? That should not be said.
Is virtue… the observance day (uposatha)… meditative development… the holy life something whose fruit is undesirable, unlovely, disagreeable and unsatisfying, with suffering as its outcome and suffering as its result? That should not be said.
But isn't giving something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? Yes. If giving is something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result, then surely you must not say: "All formations, without exception, are hot embers."
But isn't virtue… the observance day… meditative development… the holy life something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? Yes. If the holy life is something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result, then surely you must not say: "All formations, without exception, are hot embers."
Are all formations, without exception, hot embers? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Happy is seclusion for one who is content, who has heard the Dhamma and who sees;
happy in the world is freedom from ill will, restraint towards living beings.
"Happy in the world is freedom from greed, the going beyond sensual pleasures;
the removal of the conceit ‘I am’ — this indeed is the highest happiness [Mahāva. 5; Udā. 11, also in the Udāna].
"That happiness reached through happiness is utter happiness;
the three true knowledges attained — this indeed is the highest happiness"?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "all formations, without exception, are hot embers."
The Discussion of Hot Embers is finished. ^5-338

#### The Second Chapter ^5-10-10-0

##### (18) 9. Discussion of Gradual Breakthrough ^5-10-10-1-0

Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. Does one develop the path of stream-entry gradually? That should not be said. Does one develop the path of stream-entry gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry gradually? That should not be said.
Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. Does one develop the path of once-returning gradually? That should not be said. Does one develop the path of once-returning gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of once-returning gradually? That should not be said.
Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. Does one develop the path of non-returning gradually? That should not be said. Does one develop the path of non-returning gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of non-returning gradually? That should not be said.
Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. Does one develop the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) gradually? That should not be said. Does one develop the path of arahantship gradually? Yes. Does one realize the fruit of arahantship gradually? That should not be said. ^5-339

What does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry abandon by seeing suffering? They abandon one quarter of identity view, doubt, clinging to rules and rituals, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a stream-enterer and one quarter not a stream-enterer; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of stream-entry and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; one quarter one who has at most seven more lives, one who goes from family to family, one with a single seed, one endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… in the Community… endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, and one quarter not endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones? That should not be said.
What do they abandon by seeing the origin… by seeing cessation… by seeing the path? They abandon one quarter of identity view, doubt, clinging to rules and rituals, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a stream-enterer and one quarter not a stream-enterer; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of stream-entry and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; one quarter one who has at most seven more lives, one who goes from family to family, one with a single seed, one endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… in the Community… endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, and one quarter not endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones? That should not be said… ^5-340

What does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning abandon by seeing suffering? They abandon one quarter of gross sensual desire, gross ill will, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a once-returner and one quarter not a once-returner; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of once-returning and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body? That should not be said… What do they abandon by seeing the origin… by seeing cessation… by seeing the path? They abandon one quarter of gross sensual desire, gross ill will, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a once-returner and one quarter not a once-returner; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of once-returning and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body? That should not be said… ^5-341

What does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning abandon by seeing suffering? They abandon one quarter of even subtle sensual desire, even subtle ill will, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a non-returner and one quarter not a non-returner; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of non-returning and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; one quarter one who attains final nibbāna (final release) in between… one who attains final nibbāna on landing… one who attains final nibbāna without exertion… one who attains final nibbāna with exertion… one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and one quarter not one who goes upstream, not one who goes to the Akaniṭṭha realm? That should not be said…
What do they abandon by seeing the origin… by seeing cessation… by seeing the path? They abandon one quarter of even subtle sensual desire, even subtle ill will, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a non-returner and one quarter not a non-returner; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of non-returning and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; one quarter one who attains final nibbāna in between… one who attains final nibbāna on landing… one who attains final nibbāna without exertion… one who attains final nibbāna with exertion… one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and one quarter not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? That should not be said… ^5-342

What does a person practising for the realization of arahantship abandon by seeing suffering? They abandon one quarter of greed for the realm of form, greed for the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a worthy one (arahant) and one quarter not a worthy one; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized arahantship and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; are they one quarter free from greed… free from hatred… free from delusion… one who has done what had to be done, who has laid down the load, who has reached their own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, who is completely liberated through final knowledge, who has lifted the cross-bar, filled in the moat, pulled out the pillar, who has no bolt, a noble one, whose banner is lowered, whose burden is put down, who is unfettered, who has won complete victory; one by whom suffering has been fully understood, its origin abandoned, its cessation realized, the path developed; by whom what is to be directly known has been directly known, what is to be fully understood has been fully understood, what is to be abandoned has been abandoned, what is to be developed has been developed… what is to be realized has been realized, and one quarter one by whom what is to be realized has not been realized? That should not be said…
What do they abandon by seeing the origin… by seeing cessation… by seeing the path? They abandon one quarter of greed for the realm of form, greed for the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, ignorance, and the defilements that go together with them. Then are they one quarter a worthy one and one quarter not a worthy one; are they one quarter one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized arahantship and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and one quarter one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; are they one quarter free from greed… free from hatred… free from delusion… one who has done what had to be done, who has laid down the load, who has reached their own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, who is completely liberated through final knowledge, who has lifted the cross-bar, filled in the moat, pulled out the pillar, who has no bolt, a noble one, whose banner is lowered, whose burden is put down, who is unfettered, who has won complete victory; one by whom suffering has been fully understood, its origin abandoned, its cessation realized, the path developed; by whom what is to be directly known has been directly known, what is to be fully understood has been fully understood, what is to be abandoned has been abandoned, what is to be developed has been developed… what is to be realized has been realized, and one quarter one by whom what is to be realized has not been realized? That should not be said… ^5-343

Is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing suffering, to be called "one on the way"? Yes. When suffering has been seen, are they to be called "one established in the fruit"? That should not be said. While seeing the origin… while seeing cessation, are they to be called "one on the way"? Yes. When cessation has been seen, are they to be called "one established in the fruit"? That should not be said.
A person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing the path, is to be called "one on the way" — when the path has been seen, are they to be called "one established in the fruit"? Yes. While seeing suffering they are to be called "one on the way" — when suffering has been seen, are they to be called "one established in the fruit"? That should not be said… While seeing the path they are to be called "one on the way" — when the path has been seen, are they to be called "one established in the fruit"? Yes. While seeing the origin… while seeing cessation they are to be called "one on the way" — when cessation has been seen, are they to be called "one established in the fruit"? That should not be said…
A person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing suffering, is to be called "one on the way" — when suffering has been seen, should it not be said that "they are to be called ‘one established in the fruit’"? Yes. While seeing the path they are to be called "one on the way" — when the path has been seen, should it not be said that "they are to be called ‘one established in the fruit’"? That should not be said… While seeing the origin… while seeing cessation they are to be called "one on the way" — when cessation has been seen, should it not be said that "they are to be called ‘one established in the fruit’"? Yes. While seeing the path they are to be called "one on the way" — when the path has been seen, should it not be said that "they are to be called ‘one established in the fruit’"? That should not be said…
[Mark of the question of our own school] A person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry, while seeing suffering, is to be called "one on the way" — when suffering has been seen, should it not be said that "they are to be called ‘one established in the fruit’"? Yes. Is the seeing of suffering pointless? That should not be said… While seeing the origin… while seeing cessation they are to be called "one on the way" — when cessation has been seen, should it not be said that "they are to be called ‘one established in the fruit’"? Yes. Is the seeing of cessation pointless? That should not be said… ^5-344

[Mark of the question of the other school] When suffering has been seen, have the four truths been seen? Yes. Is the truth of suffering the four truths? That should not be said…
[Mark of the question of our own school] When the aggregate of material form has been seen as impermanent, have the five aggregates been seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the aggregate of material form the five aggregates? That should not be said…
[Mark of the question of our own school] When the eye base has been seen as impermanent, have the twelve sense bases been seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the eye base the twelve sense bases? That should not be said…
[Mark of the question of our own school] When the eye element has been seen as impermanent, have the eighteen elements been seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the eye element the eighteen elements? That should not be said…
[Mark of the question of our own school] When the eye faculty has been seen as impermanent, have the twenty-two faculties been seen as impermanent? Yes. Is the eye faculty the twenty-two faculties? That should not be said…
[Mark of the question of our own school] Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry by means of four kinds of knowledge? Yes. Are there four fruits of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry by means of eight kinds of knowledge? Yes. Are there eight fruits of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry by means of twelve kinds of knowledge? Yes. Are there twelve fruits of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry by means of forty-four kinds of knowledge? Yes. Are there forty-four fruits of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does one realize the fruit of stream-entry by means of seventy-seven kinds of knowledge? Yes. Are there seventy-seven fruits of stream-entry? That should not be said… ^5-345

Should it not be said that "the breakthrough is gradual"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Just as, monks, the great ocean slopes gradually, inclines gradually, shelves gradually, and does not drop off abruptly; in the same way, monks, in this Dhamma and discipline there is gradual training, gradual work, a gradual way of practice, and no abrupt penetration to final knowledge" [Cūḷava. 385; A. Ni. 8.20; Udā. 45, also in the Udāna]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the breakthrough is gradual.
Should it not be said that "the breakthrough is gradual"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Gradually, little by little, moment by moment, the wise one
should blow away their own impurities, as a smith does with silver" [Dha. Pa. 239, in the Dhammapada]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the breakthrough is gradual.
Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. But didn't the venerable elder Gavampati say this to the monks: "Friends, I heard this face to face from the Blessed One, I received it face to face: ‘Monks, whoever sees suffering also sees the origin of suffering, also sees the cessation of suffering, also sees the way of practice leading to the cessation of suffering; whoever sees the origin of suffering also sees suffering, also sees the cessation of suffering, also sees the way of practice leading to the cessation of suffering; whoever sees the cessation of suffering also sees suffering, also sees the origin of suffering, also sees the way of practice leading to the cessation of suffering; whoever sees the way of practice leading to the cessation of suffering also sees suffering, also sees the origin of suffering, also sees the cessation of suffering’" [S. Ni. 5.1100]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the breakthrough is gradual."
Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Together with their attainment of vision,
three things are abandoned:
identity view and doubt,
and whatever there may be of rules and rituals.
They are freed from the four lower realms,
and incapable of doing the six grave wrongs"?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the breakthrough is gradual."
Is the breakthrough gradual? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, at the time when the dust-free, stainless eye of the Dhamma arises in a noble disciple — ‘Whatever is subject to arising, all that is subject to cessation’ — then, monks, together with the arising of vision, three fetters are abandoned in the noble disciple: identity view, doubt, and clinging to rules and rituals"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the breakthrough is gradual."
The Discussion of Gradual Breakthrough is finished. ^5-346

#### The Second Chapter ^5-10-11-0

##### (19) 10. Discussion of Speech ^5-10-11-1-0

Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Does it strike a world-transcending ear and not a worldly one; do people understand it with world-transcending consciousness and not with worldly consciousness; do disciples understand it and not ordinary people? That should not be said…
But doesn't the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, strike the worldly ear? Yes. If the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, strikes the worldly ear, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending."
But don't people understand the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, with worldly consciousness? Yes. If people understand the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, with worldly consciousness, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending."
But don't ordinary people understand the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One? Yes. If ordinary people understand the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending." ^5-347

Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, nibbāna (final release), the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, the path of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one), the fruit of arahantship, a foundation of mindfulness, a right striving, a basis of psychic power, a faculty, a power, a factor of awakening? That should not be said…
Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Are there some who hear the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One? Yes. Is a world-transcending state cognizable by the ear; does it strike the ear; does it come within range of the ear? That should not be said…
But isn't it the case that a world-transcending state is not cognizable by the ear, does not strike the ear, and does not come within range of the ear? Yes. If a world-transcending state is not cognizable by the ear, does not strike the ear, and does not come within range of the ear, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending." ^5-348

Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Are there some who might feel greed for the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One? Yes. Is a world-transcending state a basis for greed, enticing, desirable, intoxicating, binding, infatuating? That should not be said…
But isn't it the case that a world-transcending state is not a basis for greed, not enticing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, not infatuating? Yes. If a world-transcending state is not a basis for greed, not enticing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, not infatuating, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending."
Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Are there some who might feel hatred towards the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One? Yes. Is a world-transcending state a basis for hatred, a basis for anger, a basis for aversion? That should not be said…
But isn't it the case that a world-transcending state is not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, not a basis for aversion? Yes. If a world-transcending state is not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, not a basis for aversion, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending."
Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Are there some who might be deluded about the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One? Yes. Is a world-transcending state a basis for delusion, something that causes lack of knowledge, that causes blindness, that brings wisdom to an end, that sides with distress, that does not lead to nibbāna? That should not be said…
But isn't it the case that a world-transcending state is not a basis for delusion, does not cause lack of knowledge, does not cause blindness, increases wisdom, sides with freedom from distress, and leads to nibbāna? Yes. If a world-transcending state is not a basis for delusion, does not cause lack of knowledge, does not cause blindness, increases wisdom, sides with freedom from distress, and leads to nibbāna, then surely you must not say: "The speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, is world-transcending." ^5-349

Is the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, world-transcending? Yes. Do all who hear the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, develop the path? That should not be said…
Do all who hear the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One, develop the path? Yes. Foolish ordinary people hear the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One — do foolish ordinary people develop the path? That should not be said… Does a killer of their mother develop the path… a killer of their father… a killer of a worthy one (arahant)… a shedder of a Buddha's blood… a splitter of the Community hears the speech of the Buddha, the Blessed One — does the splitter of the Community develop the path? That should not be said… ^5-350

Is it possible to point out both a heap of grain and a heap of gold with a golden stick? Yes. In just the same way, the Blessed One, with world-transcending speech, speaks of both worldly and world-transcending things.
Is it possible to point out both a heap of grain and a heap of gold with a stick of castor-oil wood? Yes. In just the same way, the Blessed One, with worldly speech, speaks of both worldly and world-transcending things. ^5-351

When the Buddha, the Blessed One, speaks of the worldly, is his speech worldly, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, is it world-transcending? Yes. When he speaks of the worldly, does it strike a worldly ear, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, does it strike a world-transcending ear; when he speaks of the worldly, do people understand it with worldly consciousness, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, do they understand it with world-transcending consciousness; when he speaks of the worldly, do ordinary people understand it, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, do disciples understand it? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "when the Buddha, the Blessed One, speaks of the worldly, his speech is worldly, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, it is world-transcending"? Yes. But doesn't the Blessed One speak of both worldly and world-transcending things? Yes. If the Blessed One speaks of both worldly and world-transcending things, then surely you must also say: "When the Buddha, the Blessed One, speaks of the worldly, his speech is worldly, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, it is world-transcending."
When the Buddha, the Blessed One, speaks of the worldly, is his speech worldly, and when he speaks of the world-transcending, is it world-transcending? Yes. When he speaks of the path, is it the path; when he speaks of what is not the path, is it not the path; when he speaks of the fruit, is it the fruit; when he speaks of what is not the fruit, is it not the fruit; when he speaks of nibbāna, is it nibbāna; when he speaks of what is not nibbāna, is it not nibbāna; when he speaks of the conditioned, is it conditioned; when he speaks of the unconditioned, is it unconditioned; when he speaks of material form, is it material form; when he speaks of what is not material form, is it not material form; when he speaks of feeling, is it feeling; when he speaks of what is not feeling, is it not feeling; when he speaks of perception, is it perception; when he speaks of what is not perception, is it not perception; when he speaks of mental formations, is it mental formations; when he speaks of what are not mental formations, is it not mental formations; when he speaks of consciousness, is it consciousness; when he speaks of what is not consciousness, is it not consciousness? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Speech is finished. ^5-352

#### The Second Chapter ^5-10-12-0

##### (20) 11. Discussion of Cessation ^5-10-12-1-0

Are there two cessations? Yes. Are there two cessations of suffering? That should not be said… Are there two cessations of suffering? Yes. Are there two truths of cessation? That should not be said… Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two truths of suffering? That should not be said… Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two truths of the origin? That should not be said… Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two truths of the path? That should not be said…
Are there two truths of cessation? Yes. Are there two protections… two shelters… two refuges… two final resorts… two imperishables… two deathless states… two nibbānas (final releases)? That should not be said…
Are there two nibbānas? Yes. Is there between the two nibbānas any difference of high and low, of inferior and superior, of better and worse, or any boundary, division, dividing line or gap? That should not be said…
Are there two cessations? Yes. But isn't it the case that people bring to cessation, through reflection, formations that have ceased without reflection? Yes. If people bring to cessation, through reflection, formations that have ceased without reflection, then surely you must not say: "There are two cessations."
Should it not be said that "there are two cessations"? Yes. But aren't formations that have ceased without reflection utterly broken up, and formations that have ceased through reflection also utterly broken up? Yes. If formations that have ceased without reflection are utterly broken up, and formations that have ceased through reflection are also utterly broken up, then surely you must also say: "There are two cessations."
Are there two cessations? Yes. Have formations that ceased through reflection too [variant: paṭisaṅkhāniruddhā (?)] ceased because of the noble path? Yes. Have formations that ceased without reflection ceased because of the noble path? That should not be said…
Are there two cessations? Yes. Do formations that ceased through reflection not arise again? Yes. Do formations that ceased without reflection not arise again? That should not be said… In that case it should not be said that "there are two cessations."
The Discussion of Cessation is finished.
The Second Chapter.
Here is its summary:
What others bring, lack of knowledge, uncertainty, being helped across by others;
verbal expression, uttering "suffering", the duration of mind, and hot embers;
gradual breakthrough, speech, and cessation. ^5-353

Does a disciple know the world with its many and various elements? Yes. ##### (24) 4. Discussion of Becoming Liberated ^5-11-4-1-0

Is it liberated while becoming liberated? Yes. Is it partly liberated and partly not liberated? That should not be said…
Is it partly liberated and partly not liberated? Yes. Is one partly a stream-enterer and partly not a stream-enterer; is one partly one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of stream-entry and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; partly one who has at most seven more lives, one who goes from family to family, one with a single seed, one endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, in the Dhamma… in the Community… endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, and partly not endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones? That should not be said…
Is it partly liberated and partly not liberated? Yes. Is one partly a once-returner and partly not a once-returner; is one partly one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of once-returning and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not dwell having touched it with the body? That should not be said…
Is it partly liberated and partly not liberated? Yes. Is one partly a non-returner and partly not a non-returner; is one partly one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of non-returning and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; partly one who attains final nibbāna (final release) in between, one who attains final nibbāna on landing, one who attains final nibbāna without exertion, one who attains final nibbāna with exertion, one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and partly not one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm? That should not be said…
Is it partly liberated and partly not liberated? Yes. Is one partly a worthy one (arahant) and partly not a worthy one; is one partly one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized arahantship (the state of a worthy one) and who dwells having entered upon it and dwells having touched it with the body, and partly one who does not dwell having touched it with the body; partly free from greed, free from hatred, free from delusion… partly one by whom what is to be realized has been realized, and partly one by whom what is to be realized has not been realized? That should not be said…
Is it liberated while becoming liberated? Yes. Is it liberated at the moment of arising, and becoming liberated at the moment of dissolution? That should not be said… ^5-366

Should it not be said that "it is liberated while becoming liberated"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "For one who knows thus, who sees thus, the mind becomes liberated from the taint of sensuality, the mind becomes liberated from the taint of existence, the mind becomes liberated from the taint of ignorance" [D. Ni. 1.248 and elsewhere]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should be said [variant: tena hi (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ.), tena hi na vattabbaṃ (Ka.)] that "it is liberated while becoming liberated."
Is it liberated while becoming liberated? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "When the mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, without blemish, free from impurities, pliable, workable, steady and attained to imperturbability, they direct the mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "it is liberated while becoming liberated."
Is there a mind that is becoming liberated? Yes. Is there a mind that is becoming impassioned, becoming corrupted, becoming deluded, becoming defiled? That should not be said… But isn't it both impassioned and not impassioned, both corrupted and not corrupted, both deluded and not deluded, both cut and not cut, both broken and not broken, both done and not done? Yes. If it is both impassioned and not impassioned, both corrupted and not corrupted, both deluded and not deluded, both cut and not cut, both broken and not broken, both done and not done, then surely you must not say: "There is a mind that is becoming liberated."
The Discussion of Becoming Liberated is finished. ^5-367

The eighth person has wisdom — do they have the faculty of wisdom? That should not be said…
A person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning… a person practising for the realization of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) has faith — do they have the faculty of faith… has wisdom — do they have the faculty of wisdom? That should not be said…
Does the eighth person not have the five faculties? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom — these, monks, are the five faculties. Monks, through the completion and fulfilment of these five faculties one is a worthy one (arahant). If they are weaker than that, one is practising for the realization of arahantship; if weaker still, one is a non-returner; if weaker still, one is practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning; if weaker still, one is a once-returner; if weaker still, one is practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning; if weaker still, one is a stream-enterer; if weaker still, one is practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry. Monks, one in whom these five faculties are completely and in every way absent, I call ‘an outsider, standing on the side of ordinary people’" [S. Ni. 5.488]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. Is the eighth person an outsider, standing on the side of ordinary people? That should not be said… In that case the eighth person has the five faculties.
The Discussion of the Faculties of the Eighth Person is finished. ^5-372

##### (27) 7. Discussion of the Divine Eye ^5-11-7-1-0

Does the physical eye, supported by a mental state, become the divine eye? Yes. Is the physical eye the divine eye, and the divine eye the physical eye? That should not be said…

Having belonged to the sense-desire realm, does it come to belong to the realm of form? Yes. Having belonged to the realm of form, does it come to belong to the formless realm? That should not be said…

Does the physical eye, supported by a mental state, become the divine eye? Yes. Are there only two eyes? That should not be said… Are there only two eyes? Yes. If the Blessed One has spoken of three eyes — the physical eye, the divine eye, the eye of wisdom — then surely you must not say: "There are only two eyes."
Are there only two eyes? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these three eyes. Which three? The physical eye, the divine eye, the eye of wisdom — these, monks, are the three eyes."
"The physical eye, the divine eye, and the unsurpassed eye of wisdom —
these three eyes were made known by the highest of persons.
"The arising of the physical eye is the path to the divine eye;

by gaining that eye one is freed from all suffering" [Itivu. 61, in the Itivuttaka]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "there are only two eyes."
The Discussion of the Divine Eye is finished. ^5-374

Is the knowledge of how beings fare according to their actions [variant: yathākammūpagatañāṇaṃ (Syā., Kaṃ.)] the divine eye? Yes. Does one both attend to how beings fare according to their actions and see visible forms with the divine eye? That should not be said…

##### (30) 10. Discussion of Restraint ^5-11-10-1-0

Is there restraint among the gods? Yes. Is there non-restraint among the gods? That should not be said…

Acknowledge the refutation. If virtue is restraint from non-restraint, and there is restraint among the gods, then surely you must also say: "There is non-restraint among the gods, restraint from which is virtue." What you say here — that "virtue is restraint from non-restraint, and there is restraint among the gods" should be said, but "there is non-restraint among the gods, restraint from which is virtue" should not be said — is wrong.
There is restraint among human beings — is there non-restraint there? Yes. There is restraint among the gods — is there non-restraint there? That should not be said…
There is restraint among the gods — is there no non-restraint there? Yes. There is restraint among human beings — is there no non-restraint there? That should not be said… ^5-379

Is there abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among the gods? Yes. Is there liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among the gods? That should not be said…
Is there no killing of living beings among the gods? Yes. Is there no abstention from killing living beings among the gods? That should not be said…
Is there no liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among the gods? Yes. Is there no abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among the gods? That should not be said…
There is abstention from killing living beings among human beings — is there killing of living beings there? Yes. There is abstention from killing living beings among the gods — is there killing of living beings there? That should not be said…
There is abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among human beings — is there liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, there? Yes. There is abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among the gods — is there liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, there? That should not be said…

There is abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among the gods — is there no liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, there? Yes. There is abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, among human beings — is there no liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, there? That should not be said…
Is there no restraint among the gods? Yes. Do all the gods kill living beings, take what is not given, engage in sexual misconduct, speak falsely, and indulge in liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness? That should not be said… In that case there is restraint among the gods.

#### The Third Chapter ^5-11-11-0

##### (31) 11. Discussion of Beings Without Perception ^5-11-11-1-0

Is there perception among beings without perception? Yes. Is it an existence with perception, a destination with perception, an abode of beings with perception, a round of rebirth with perception, a mode of birth with perception, an acquisition of individual existence with perception? That should not be said…
But isn't it an existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode of beings without perception, a round of rebirth without perception, a mode of birth without perception, an acquisition of individual existence without perception? Yes. If it is an existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode of beings without perception, a round of rebirth without perception, a mode of birth without perception, an acquisition of individual existence without perception, then surely you must not say: "There is perception among beings without perception."
Is there perception among beings without perception? Yes. Is it a five-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
But isn't it a single-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence? Yes. If it is a single-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence, then surely you must not say: "There is perception among beings without perception."
Is there perception among beings without perception? Yes. Do they do with that perception what perception has to do? That should not be said… ^5-381

There is perception among human beings — and is that an existence with perception, a destination with perception, an abode of beings with perception, a round of rebirth with perception, a mode of birth with perception, an acquisition of individual existence with perception? That should not be said…
There is perception among human beings — and is that a five-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence? Yes. There is perception among beings without perception — and is that a five-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
There is perception among human beings — do they do with that perception what perception has to do? Yes. There is perception among beings without perception — do they do with that perception what perception has to do? That should not be said…
There is perception among beings without perception — and is that an existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode of beings without perception, a round of rebirth without perception, a mode of birth without perception, an acquisition of individual existence without perception? Yes. There is perception among human beings — and is that an existence without perception, a destination without perception… an acquisition of individual existence without perception? That should not be said…
There is perception among beings without perception — and is that a single-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence? Yes. There is perception among human beings — and is that a single-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
There is perception among beings without perception, but do they not do with that perception what perception has to do? Yes. There is perception among human beings, but do they not do with that perception what perception has to do? That should not be said… ^5-382

Should it not be said that "there is perception among beings without perception"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are gods called beings without perception; and with the arising of perception those gods pass away from that body" [D. Ni. 1.68]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is perception among beings without perception.
Is there perception among beings without perception? At some times [variant: kañci (Syā.)] there is, at some times there is not. At some times are they beings with perception and at some times beings without perception; at some times is it an existence with perception and at some times an existence without perception; at some times a five-aggregate existence and at some times a single-aggregate existence? That should not be said…
Is there perception among beings without perception at some times, and at some times not? Yes. At what time is there, and at what time is there not? At the time of passing away and at the time of rebirth there is; at the time of remaining there is not. At the time of passing away and at the time of rebirth are they beings with perception, and at the time of remaining beings without perception; at the time of passing away and at the time of rebirth is it an existence with perception, and at the time of remaining an existence without perception; at the time of passing away and at the time of rebirth is it a five-aggregate existence, and at the time of remaining a single-aggregate existence? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Beings Without Perception is finished. ^5-383

#### The Third Chapter ^5-11-12-0

##### (32) 12. Discussion of the Base of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception ^5-11-12-1-0

In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said that "there is perception"? Yes. Is it an existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode of beings without perception, a round of rebirth without perception, a mode of birth without perception, an acquisition of individual existence without perception? That should not be said…
But isn't it an existence with perception, a destination with perception, an abode of beings with perception, a round of rebirth with perception, a mode of birth with perception, an acquisition of individual existence with perception? Yes. If it is an existence with perception, a destination with perception… an acquisition of individual existence with perception, then surely you must not say: "In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, it should not be said that ‘there is perception’."
In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said that "there is perception"? Yes. Is it a single-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
But isn't it a four-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence? Yes. If it is a four-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence, then surely you must not say: "In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, it should not be said that ‘there is perception’." ^5-384

Among beings without perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that an existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode of beings without perception, a round of rebirth without perception, a mode of birth without perception, an acquisition of individual existence without perception? Yes. In the base of neither perception nor non-perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that an existence without perception, a destination without perception, an abode of beings without perception, a round of rebirth without perception, a mode of birth without perception, an acquisition of individual existence without perception? That should not be said…
Among beings without perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that a single-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence? Yes. In the base of neither perception nor non-perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that a single-aggregate existence, destination, abode of beings, round of rebirth, mode of birth, acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
In the base of neither perception nor non-perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that an existence with perception, a destination with perception… an acquisition of individual existence with perception? Yes. Among beings without perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that an existence with perception, a destination with perception… an acquisition of individual existence with perception? That should not be said…
In the base of neither perception nor non-perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that a four-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence? Yes. Among beings without perception it should not be said that "there is perception" — and is that a four-aggregate existence, destination… acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said that "there is perception"? Yes. But isn't the base of neither perception nor non-perception a four-aggregate existence? Yes. If the base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence, then surely you must not say: "In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, it should not be said that ‘there is perception’." ^5-385

The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — in the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said that "there is perception"? Yes. The base of the infinity of space is a four-aggregate existence — in the base of the infinity of space, should it not be said that "there is perception"? That should not be said…
The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — in the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said that "there is perception"? Yes. The base of the infinity of consciousness… the base of nothingness is a four-aggregate existence — in the base of nothingness, should it not be said that "there is perception"? That should not be said…
The base of the infinity of space is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? Yes. The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? That should not be said…
The base of the infinity of consciousness… the base of nothingness is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? Yes. The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? That should not be said…
In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said either that "there is perception" or that "there is not"? Yes. But isn't the base of neither perception nor non-perception a four-aggregate existence? Yes. If the base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence, then surely you must not say: "In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, it should not be said either that ‘there is perception’ or that ‘there is not’."
The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — in the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said either that "there is perception" or that "there is not"? Yes. The base of the infinity of space… the base of the infinity of consciousness… the base of nothingness is a four-aggregate existence — in the base of nothingness, should it not be said either that "there is perception" or that "there is not"? That should not be said…
The base of the infinity of space is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? Yes. The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? That should not be said…
The base of the infinity of consciousness… the base of nothingness is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? Yes. The base of neither perception nor non-perception is a four-aggregate existence — is there perception there? That should not be said…
In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, should it not be said [variant: nevasaññānāsaññāyatane vattabbaṃ (?)] either that "there is perception" or that "there is not"? Yes. But isn't it the base of neither perception nor non-perception? Yes. If it is the base of neither perception nor non-perception, then surely you must also say: "In the base of neither perception nor non-perception, it should not be said either that ‘there is perception’ or that ‘there is not’."
On the grounds that it is "the base of neither perception nor non-perception", should it not be said in the base of neither perception nor non-perception either that "there is perception" or that "there is not"? Yes. On the grounds that it is "neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling", should it not be said of neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling [variant: adukkhamasukhā vedanā (Sī., Ka.)] either that it is "feeling" or that it is "not feeling"? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Base of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception is finished.
The Third Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The power is shared; noble; a mind with greed is liberated;
liberated while becoming liberated; there is a mind becoming liberated;
for the eighth person obsession by views is abandoned;
the eighth person does not have the five faculties; the eye,
the ear supported by a mental state; knowledge of faring according to action;
restraint among the gods; perception among beings without perception; and likewise the peak of existence. ^5-386

### The Fourth Chapter ^5-12-0

#### (33) 1. Discussion of "A Householder Can Be a Worthy One" ^5-12-1-0

Can a householder be a worthy one (arahant)? Yes. Does a worthy one have the fetter of household life? That should not be said… Does a worthy one not have the fetter of household life? Yes. If a worthy one does not have the fetter of household life, then surely you must not say: "A householder can be a worthy one."
Can a householder be a worthy one? Yes. But hasn't a worthy one's fetter of household life been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, so that it is no longer subject to arise in the future? Yes. If a worthy one's fetter of household life has been abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, done away with, so that it is no longer subject to arise in the future, then surely you must not say: "A householder can be a worthy one."
Can a householder be a worthy one? Yes. Is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering in this very life [M. Ni. 2.186]? There is not. If there is no householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering in this very life, then surely you must not say: "A householder can be a worthy one."
Can a householder be a worthy one? Yes. But didn't the wanderer Vacchagotta say this to the Blessed One: "Master Gotama, is there any householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering at the breakup of the body?" "Vaccha, there is no householder who, without abandoning the fetter of household life, makes an end of suffering at the breakup of the body." Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a householder can be a worthy one."
Can a householder be a worthy one? Yes. Would a worthy one engage in sexual intercourse, bring about sexual union, live in a bed crowded with children, enjoy sandalwood from Kāsi, wear garlands, scents and ointments, accept gold and silver, accept goats and sheep, accept chickens and pigs, accept elephants, cattle, horses and mares, accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants [variant: … kapiñjalaṃ (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)], wear a decorated headdress with a topknot [variant: pītavaṇṭavālamoḷikaṃ (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)], wear white clothes with long fringes, and remain a householder for their whole life? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "a householder can be a worthy one"? Yes. But didn't Yasa, the son of a good family, Uttiya the householder and Setu the young brahmin attain arahantship (the state of a worthy one) while still in the outward guise of a householder? Yes. If Yasa, the son of a good family, Uttiya the householder and Setu the young brahmin attained arahantship while still in the outward guise of a householder, then surely you must also say: "A householder can be a worthy one."
The Discussion of "A Householder Can Be a Worthy One" is finished. ^5-387

##### (34) 2. Discussion of Rebirth ^5-12-2-1-0

Is one a worthy one (arahant) at the very moment of rebirth? Yes. Does one become a stream-enterer at the very moment of rebirth? That should not be said…
Is one a worthy one at the very moment of rebirth? Yes. Does one become a once-returner at the very moment of rebirth? That should not be said…

##### (35) 3. Discussion of "Free of Taints" ^5-12-3-1-0

Are all things in a worthy one (arahant) free of taints? Yes. Are they the path, the fruit, nibbāna (final release), the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, the path of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one), the fruit of arahantship, a foundation of mindfulness, a right striving, a basis of psychic power, a faculty, a power, a factor of awakening? That should not be said…
Are all things in a worthy one free of taints? Yes. Is a worthy one's eye free of taints? That should not be said… Is a worthy one's eye free of taints? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… a factor of awakening? That should not be said…
Is a worthy one's ear… a worthy one's nose… a worthy one's tongue… a worthy one's body free of taints? That should not be said… Is a worthy one's body free of taints? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, nibbāna, the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… a factor of awakening? That should not be said…
Is a worthy one's body free of taints? Yes. Is a worthy one's body subject to being held up and held down, subject to cutting and breaking, something shared with crows, vultures and hawks? Yes. Is a state that is free of taints subject to being held up and held down, subject to cutting and breaking, something shared with crows, vultures and hawks? That should not be said…
Could poison affect a worthy one's body, could a weapon affect it, could fire affect it? Yes. Could poison affect a state that is free of taints, could a weapon affect it, could fire affect it? That should not be said…
Is it possible to bind a worthy one's body with shackles, to bind it with ropes, to bind it with chains, to confine it to a village, to confine it to a town, to confine it to a city, to confine it to a country, to bind it with the five bonds of which the neck is the fifth? Yes. Is it possible to bind a state that is free of taints with shackles, to bind it with ropes, to bind it with chains, to confine it to a village, town, city or country, to bind it with the five bonds of which the neck is the fifth? That should not be said… ^5-391

If a worthy one gives a robe to an ordinary person, does the robe, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints?
