That should not be said… Is that very same thing both free of taints and accompanied by taints? Yes. Does the path, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints? That should not be said… Does the fruit… a foundation of mindfulness… a right striving… a basis of psychic power… a faculty… a power… a factor of awakening, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints? That should not be said…
If a worthy one gives almsfood, gives lodging, gives medicines and requisites for the sick to an ordinary person, does it, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints? That should not be said… Does it, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints? Yes. Is that very same thing both free of taints and accompanied by taints? That should not be said… Is that very same thing both free of taints and accompanied by taints? Yes. Does the path, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints? That should not be said… Does the fruit… a foundation of mindfulness… a right striving… a basis of psychic power… a faculty… a power… a factor of awakening, having been free of taints, become accompanied by taints? That should not be said…
If an ordinary person gives a robe to a worthy one, does the robe, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? That should not be said… Does it, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? Yes. Is that very same thing both accompanied by taints and free of taints? That should not be said… Is that very same thing both accompanied by taints and free of taints? Yes. Does greed, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? That should not be said… Does hatred… delusion… lack of moral fear, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? That should not be said…
If an ordinary person gives almsfood, gives lodging, gives medicines and requisites for the sick to a worthy one, does it, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? That should not be said… Does it, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? Yes. Is that very same thing both accompanied by taints and free of taints? That should not be said… Is that very same thing both accompanied by taints and free of taints? Yes. Does greed, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? That should not be said… Does hatred… delusion… lack of moral fear, having been accompanied by taints, become free of taints? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "all things in a worthy one are free of taints"? Yes. But isn't a worthy one free of taints? Yes. If a worthy one is free of taints, then surely you must also say: "All things in a worthy one are free of taints."

##### (36) 4. Discussion of Being Endowed ^5-12-4-1-0

Is a worthy one (arahant) endowed with the four fruits? Yes. Should one endowed with the fruit of stream-entry be called "a stream-enterer"? Yes. Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Is that very non-returner a stream-enterer? That should not be said…

Is a worthy one who has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry endowed with it? Yes. Is a worthy one who has gone beyond the path of stream-entry, who has gone beyond identity view, doubt, clinging to rules and rituals, greed that leads to the lower realms, hatred that leads to the lower realms and delusion that leads to the lower realms, endowed with them? That should not be said…
Is a worthy one endowed with the fruit of once-returning? Yes. But hasn't a worthy one gone beyond the fruit of once-returning? Yes. If a worthy one has gone beyond the fruit of once-returning, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one is endowed with the fruit of once-returning."
Is a worthy one who has gone beyond the fruit of once-returning endowed with it? Yes. Is a worthy one who has gone beyond the path of once-returning, who has gone beyond gross sensual desire and gross ill will, endowed with them? That should not be said…
Is a worthy one endowed with the fruit of non-returning? Yes. But hasn't a worthy one gone beyond the fruit of non-returning? Yes. If a worthy one has gone beyond the fruit of non-returning, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one is endowed with the fruit of non-returning."
Is a worthy one who has gone beyond the fruit of non-returning endowed with it? Yes. Is a worthy one who has gone beyond the path of non-returning, who has gone beyond even subtle sensual desire and even subtle ill will, endowed with them? That should not be said…
Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. But hasn't a non-returner gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If a non-returner has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you must not say: "A non-returner is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry."
Is a non-returner who has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry endowed with it? Yes. Is a non-returner who has gone beyond the path of stream-entry, who has gone beyond identity view… delusion that leads to the lower realms, endowed with them? That should not be said…
Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of once-returning? Yes. But hasn't a non-returner gone beyond the fruit of once-returning? Yes. If a non-returner has gone beyond the fruit of once-returning, then surely you must not say: "A non-returner is endowed with the fruit of once-returning."
Is a non-returner who has gone beyond the fruit of once-returning endowed with it? Yes. Is a non-returner who has gone beyond the path of once-returning, who has gone beyond gross sensual desire and gross ill will, endowed with them? That should not be said…
Is a once-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. But hasn't a once-returner gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If a once-returner has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you must not say: "A once-returner is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry."
Is a once-returner who has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry endowed with it? Yes. Is a once-returner who has gone beyond the path of stream-entry, who has gone beyond identity view… delusion that leads to the lower realms, endowed with them? That should not be said… ^5-395

Should it not be said that "a worthy one is endowed with the four fruits"? Yes. But hasn't a worthy one obtained the four fruits, and not fallen away from them? Yes. If a worthy one has obtained the four fruits and has not fallen away from them, then surely you must also say: "A worthy one is endowed with the four fruits."
Should it not be said that "a non-returner is endowed with three fruits"? Yes. But hasn't a non-returner obtained three fruits, and not fallen away from them? Yes. If a non-returner has obtained three fruits and has not fallen away from them, then surely you must also say: "A non-returner is endowed with three fruits."
Should it not be said that "a once-returner is endowed with two fruits"? Yes. But hasn't a once-returner obtained two fruits, and not fallen away from them? Yes. If a once-returner has obtained two fruits and has not fallen away from them, then surely you must also say: "A once-returner is endowed with two fruits."
Since a worthy one has obtained the four fruits and has not fallen away from them, is a worthy one endowed with the four fruits? Yes. Since a worthy one has obtained the four paths and has not fallen away from them, is a worthy one endowed with the four paths? That should not be said…
Since a non-returner has obtained three fruits and has not fallen away from them, is a non-returner endowed with three fruits? Yes. Since a non-returner has obtained three paths and has not fallen away from them, is a non-returner endowed with three paths? That should not be said…
Since a once-returner has obtained two fruits and has not fallen away from them, is a once-returner endowed with two fruits? Yes. Since a once-returner has obtained two paths and has not fallen away from them, is a once-returner endowed with two paths? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Being Endowed is finished. ^5-396

#### The Fourth Chapter ^5-12-5-0

##### (37) 5. Discussion of Being Endowed with Equanimity ^5-12-5-1-0

Is a worthy one (arahant) endowed with six kinds of equanimity? Yes. Is a worthy one endowed with six contacts, six feelings, six perceptions… six kinds of wisdom? That should not be said…
Is a worthy one endowed with six kinds of equanimity? Yes. While seeing a visible form with the eye, does a worthy one hear a sound with the ear, smell a smell with the nose, taste a taste with the tongue, feel a touch with the body, know a mental object with the mind… while knowing a mental object with the mind, does a worthy one see a visible form with the eye, hear a sound with the ear, smell a smell with the nose, taste a taste with the tongue, feel a touch with the body? That should not be said…
Is a worthy one endowed with six kinds of equanimity? Yes. Is a worthy one constantly, continuously and without interruption endowed with and possessed of [variant: samāhito (Syā.)] six kinds of equanimity; are six kinds of equanimity present? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "a worthy one is endowed with six kinds of equanimity"? Yes. But isn't a worthy one equanimous in six ways? Yes. If a worthy one is equanimous in six ways, then surely you must also say: "A worthy one is endowed with six kinds of equanimity."…
The Discussion of Being Endowed with Equanimity is finished. ^5-397

#### The Fourth Chapter ^5-12-6-0

##### (38) 6. Discussion of "A Buddha by Awakening" ^5-12-6-1-0

Is one a Buddha by awakening? Yes. When awakening has ceased, gone and subsided, does one become not a Buddha? That should not be said…
Is one a Buddha by awakening? Yes. Is one a Buddha by past awakening? That should not be said… Is one a Buddha by past awakening? Yes. Does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? That should not be said…
Does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? Yes. With that awakening does one fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, develop the path? That should not be said…
Is one a Buddha by awakening? Yes. Is one a Buddha by future awakening? That should not be said…
Is one a Buddha by future awakening? Yes. Does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? That should not be said…
Does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? Yes. With that awakening does one fully understand suffering… develop the path? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by present awakening — does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? Yes. One is a Buddha by past awakening — does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by present awakening — with that awakening does one fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, develop the path? Yes. One is a Buddha by past awakening — with that awakening does one fully understand suffering… develop the path? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by present awakening — does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? Yes. One is a Buddha by future awakening — does one do with that awakening what awakening has to do? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by present awakening — with that awakening does one fully understand suffering… develop the path? Yes. One is a Buddha by future awakening — with that awakening does one fully understand suffering… develop the path? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by past awakening, but does one not do with that awakening what awakening has to do? Yes. One is a Buddha by present awakening, but does one not do with that awakening what awakening has to do? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by past awakening, but with that awakening does one not fully understand suffering… not develop the path? Yes. One is a Buddha by present awakening, but with that awakening does one not fully understand suffering… not develop the path? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by future awakening, but does one not do with that awakening what awakening has to do? Yes. One is a Buddha by present awakening, but does one not do with that awakening what awakening has to do? That should not be said…
One is a Buddha by future awakening, but with that awakening does one not fully understand suffering… not develop the path? Yes. One is a Buddha by present awakening, but with that awakening does one not fully understand suffering… not develop the path? That should not be said… ^5-398

Is one a Buddha by past awakening, a Buddha by future awakening, a Buddha by present awakening? Yes. Is one a Buddha by three awakenings? That should not be said…
Is one a Buddha by three awakenings? Yes. Is one constantly, continuously and without interruption endowed with and possessed of three awakenings; are three awakenings present? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "one is a Buddha by awakening"? Yes. But isn't one a Buddha through obtaining awakening? Yes. If one is a Buddha through obtaining awakening, then surely you must also say: "One is a Buddha by awakening."
Since one is a Buddha through obtaining awakening, is one a Buddha by awakening? Yes. Is one awakening through obtaining awakening? That should not be said…
The Discussion of "A Buddha by Awakening" is finished. ^5-399

#### The Fourth Chapter ^5-12-7-0

##### (39) 7. Discussion of the Marks ^5-12-7-1-0

Is one who is endowed with the marks a bodhisatta (a Buddha-to-be)? Yes. Is one who is endowed with some of the marks partly a bodhisatta? That should not be said…
Is one who is endowed with the marks a bodhisatta? Yes. Is one who is endowed with a third of the marks a third of a bodhisatta? That should not be said…
Is one who is endowed with the marks a bodhisatta? Yes. Is one who is endowed with half of the marks half a bodhisatta? That should not be said…
Is one who is endowed with the marks a bodhisatta? Yes. A future wheel-turning king (a universal monarch) is endowed with the marks — is a future wheel-turning king a bodhisatta? That should not be said…
A future wheel-turning king is endowed with the marks — is a future wheel-turning king a bodhisatta? Yes. Are the preparatory effort, past conduct, proclaiming of the Dhamma and teaching of the Dhamma of a future wheel-turning king such as the preparatory effort, past conduct, proclaiming of the Dhamma and teaching of the Dhamma of a bodhisatta are? That should not be said… ^5-400

Just as, when a bodhisatta is being born, gods receive him first and human beings afterwards [D. Ni. 2.27; M. Ni. 3.205 — the question is asked with reference to what is said there], in just the same way, when a future wheel-turning king is being born, do gods receive him first and human beings afterwards? That should not be said…
Just as, when a bodhisatta is being born, four young gods receive him and set him before his mother, saying: "Rejoice, O queen! A son of great power has been born to you," in just the same way, when a future wheel-turning king is being born, do four young gods receive him and set him before his mother, saying: "Rejoice, O queen! A son of great power has been born to you"? That should not be said…
Just as, when a bodhisatta is being born, two streams of water appear from the sky — one of cool water, one of warm — with which they bathe the bodhisatta and his mother, in just the same way, when a future wheel-turning king is being born, do two streams of water appear from the sky — one of cool water, one of warm — with which they bathe the future wheel-turning king and his mother? That should not be said…
Just as a bodhisatta, as soon as he is born, stands firmly on even feet, faces north and walks seven steps while a white parasol is held over him, surveys all the directions and speaks these lordly words: "I am the foremost in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the best in the world; this is my last birth; now there is no more renewed existence," in just the same way, does a future wheel-turning king, as soon as he is born, stand firmly on even feet, face north and walk seven steps while a white parasol is held over him, survey all the directions and speak these lordly words: "I am the foremost in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the best in the world; this is my last birth; now there is no more renewed existence"? That should not be said…
Just as, when a bodhisatta is being born, there appear a great light, a great radiance and a great quaking of the earth, in just the same way, when a future wheel-turning king is being born, do there appear a great light, a great radiance and a great quaking of the earth? That should not be said…
Just as a bodhisatta's natural body shines for an arm's span all around, in just the same way, does a future wheel-turning king's natural body shine for an arm's span all around? That should not be said…
Just as a bodhisatta has the great dreams, in just the same way, does a future wheel-turning king have the great dreams? That should not be said… ^5-401

Should it not be said that "one who is endowed with the marks is a bodhisatta"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these thirty-two marks of a great man, and for a great man endowed with them only two destinations are possible, and no other [variant: na aññā (Ka.)]. If he lives at home, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning king, a righteous king who rules by the Dhamma, ruler of the four quarters, victorious, who has brought stability to his country and who possesses the seven treasures. These are his seven treasures: the wheel treasure, the elephant treasure, the horse treasure, the jewel treasure, the woman treasure, the householder treasure, and the adviser treasure as the seventh. He has more than a thousand sons, brave, heroic in build, crushers of enemy armies. He lives having conquered this earth bounded by the ocean without rod and without weapon, by righteousness. But if he goes forth from home into homelessness, he becomes a worthy one (arahant), a Fully Awakened Buddha, one who draws back the veil from the world" [D. Ni. 3.200]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one who is endowed with the marks is a bodhisatta.
The Discussion of the Marks is finished. ^5-402

#### The Fourth Chapter ^5-12-8-0

##### (40) 8. Discussion of Entering the Fixed Course ^5-12-8-1-0

Under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, had the bodhisatta (the Buddha-to-be) entered the fixed course and lived the holy life (the life of spiritual training) [M. Ni. 2.282 — the question is asked on the basis of the Ghaṭikāra Discourse]? Yes. Was the bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? That should not be said…
Was the bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? Yes. Having been a disciple, does one become a Buddha? That should not be said…
Having been a disciple, does one become a Buddha? Yes. Is he one who learned by hearing from others? That should not be said…
Is he one who learned by hearing from others? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One self-awakened? Yes. If the Blessed One is self-awakened, then surely you must not say: "He is one who learned by hearing from others."
Under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, had the bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life? Yes. At the foot of the tree of awakening, did the Blessed One awaken to only three fruits of the ascetic life? That should not be said…
But didn't the Blessed One, at the foot of the tree of awakening, awaken to four fruits of the ascetic life? Yes. If the Blessed One, at the foot of the tree of awakening, awakened to four fruits of the ascetic life, then surely you must not say: "Under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, the bodhisatta had entered the fixed course and lived the holy life." ^5-403

Under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, had the bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life? Yes. Did the bodhisatta practise severe austerities? Yes. Would a person accomplished in vision practise severe austerities? That should not be said…
Did the bodhisatta practise another kind of austerity [variant: amaraṃ tapaṃ (S. Ni. 1.137)] and acknowledge another teacher? Yes. Would a person accomplished in vision acknowledge another teacher? That should not be said…
The venerable Ānanda entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One — is the venerable Ānanda a disciple of the Blessed One? Yes. The bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa — was the bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? That should not be said…
Citta the householder and Hatthaka of Āḷavī entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One — are Citta the householder and Hatthaka of Āḷavī disciples of the Blessed One? Yes. The bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa — was the bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? That should not be said…
The bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, but was he not a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? Yes. The venerable Ānanda entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One, but is he not a disciple of the Blessed One? That should not be said…
The bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, but was he not a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? Yes. Citta the householder and Hatthaka of Āḷavī entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One, but are they not disciples of the Blessed One? That should not be said…
The bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, but was he not a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa? Yes. Having passed beyond a birth, does a disciple become one who is not a disciple? That should not be said… ^5-404

Should it not be said that "under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, the bodhisatta had entered the fixed course and lived the holy life"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Ānanda, I lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa for the sake of full awakening in the future"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, the bodhisatta had entered the fixed course and lived the holy life."
Under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, had the bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"I am the one who has overcome all, who knows all,
untainted by any thing at all;
having given up all, liberated by the destruction of craving,
having known it directly by myself, whom should I point to as my teacher?
"I have no teacher, no one equal to me is found;
in the world with its gods, there is no one to rival me.
"For I am the worthy one (arahant) in the world, I am the unsurpassed teacher;
I alone am a Fully Awakened Buddha, I have become cool and quenched.
"To set rolling the wheel of the Dhamma, I am going to the city of Kāsi;
in a world that has become blind [variant: andhabhūtasmiṃ (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)], I shall beat [variant: āhaññiṃ (Ka.)] the drum of the deathless" [variant: dudrabhinti (Ka.)].
"To judge by what you claim, friend, you must be the Endless Conqueror?"
"Those like me are conquerors indeed, who have reached the destruction of the taints;
I have conquered bad states, therefore, Upaka, I am a conqueror" [Mahāva. 11; M. Ni. 1.285; 2.341]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, the bodhisatta had entered the fixed course and lived the holy life."
Under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, had the bodhisatta entered the fixed course and lived the holy life? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "‘This is the noble truth of suffering’ — thus, monks, in regard to things not heard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘This noble truth of suffering is to be fully understood’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been fully understood’ — thus, monks, in regard to things not heard before, there arose in me vision… there arose light. ‘This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering’ — thus, monks… ‘this noble truth of the origin of suffering [variant: dukkhasamudayo (Syā., Kaṃ.)] is to be abandoned’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been abandoned’ — thus, monks… ‘this is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering [variant: dukkhanirodho (Syā., Kaṃ.)]’ — thus, monks… ‘this noble truth of the cessation of suffering is to be realized’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been realized’ — thus, monks… ‘this is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering’ — thus, monks… ‘this noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering is to be developed’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been developed’ — thus, monks, in regard to things not heard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light" [Mahāva. 15; S. Ni. 5.1081; Paṭi. Ma. 2.30]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "under the teaching of the Blessed One Kassapa, the bodhisatta had entered the fixed course and lived the holy life."
The Discussion of Entering the Fixed Course is finished. ^5-405

Is a person practising for the realization of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) endowed with three fruits? Yes. Is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Should one endowed with the fruit of stream-entry be called a stream-enterer? Yes. Is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Is a person practising for the realization of arahantship who has gone beyond the fruit of once-returning endowed with it? Yes. Is a person practising for the realization of arahantship who has gone beyond the fruit of non-returning endowed with it? Yes. Is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. But hasn't a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you must not say: "A person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry."
Is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning who has gone beyond the fruit of stream-entry endowed with it? Yes. Is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning who has gone beyond the path of stream-entry, who has gone beyond identity view… delusion that leads to the lower realms, endowed with them? That should not be said… ^5-410

Should it not be said that "a person practising for the realization of arahantship is endowed with three fruits"? Yes. But hasn't a person practising for the realization of arahantship obtained three fruits, and not fallen away from them? Yes. If a person practising for the realization of arahantship has obtained three fruits and has not fallen away from them, then surely you must also say: "A person practising for the realization of arahantship is endowed with three fruits."
Should it not be said that "a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is endowed with two fruits"? Yes. But hasn't a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning obtained two fruits, and not fallen away from them? Yes. If a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has obtained two fruits and has not fallen away from them, then surely you must also say: "A person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning is endowed with two fruits."
Should it not be said that "a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry"? Yes. But hasn't a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning obtained the fruit of stream-entry, and not fallen away from it? Yes. If a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has obtained the fruit of stream-entry and has not fallen away from it, then surely you must also say: "A person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry." ^5-411

Since a person practising for the realization of arahantship has obtained three fruits and has not fallen away from them, is a person practising for the realization of arahantship endowed with three fruits? Yes. Since a person practising for the realization of arahantship has obtained four paths and has not fallen away from them, is a person practising for the realization of arahantship endowed with four paths? That should not be said…
Since a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has obtained two fruits and has not fallen away from them, is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with two fruits? Yes. Since a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning has obtained three paths and has not fallen away from them, is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning endowed with three paths? That should not be said…
Since a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has obtained the fruit of stream-entry and has not fallen away from it, is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. Since a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning has obtained two paths and has not fallen away from them, is a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning endowed with two paths? That should not be said…
Another Discussion of Being Endowed is finished. ^5-412

#### The Fourth Chapter ^5-12-10-0

##### (42) 10. Discussion of the Abandoning of All Fetters ^5-12-10-1-0

Is arahantship (the state of a worthy one) the abandoning of all fetters? Yes. Are all fetters abandoned by the path of arahantship? That should not be said…
Are all fetters abandoned by the path of arahantship? Yes. Does one abandon identity view, doubt and clinging to rules and rituals by the path of arahantship? That should not be said…
Does one abandon identity view, doubt and clinging to rules and rituals by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the abandoning of the three fetters to be the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the abandoning of the three fetters to be the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you must not say: "All fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship." ^5-413

Are all fetters abandoned by the path of arahantship? Yes. Does one abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will by the path of arahantship? That should not be said… ^5-414

Does one abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the weakening of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of once-returning? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the weakening of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of once-returning, then surely you must not say: "All fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship."
Are all fetters abandoned by the path of arahantship? Yes. Does one abandon even subtle sensual desire and even subtle ill will by the path of arahantship? That should not be said… ^5-415

Does one abandon even subtle sensual desire and even subtle ill will by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the abandoning without remainder of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of non-returning? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the abandoning without remainder of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of non-returning, then surely you must not say: "All fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship."
Are all fetters abandoned by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the abandoning without remainder of greed for the realm of form, greed for the formless realm, conceit, restlessness and ignorance to be arahantship? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the abandoning without remainder of greed for the realm of form, greed for the formless realm, conceit, restlessness and ignorance to be arahantship, then surely you must not say: "All fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship." ^5-416

Should it not be said that "arahantship is the abandoning of all fetters"? Yes. But hasn't a worthy one (arahant) abandoned all fetters? Yes. If a worthy one has abandoned all fetters, then surely you must also say: "Arahantship is the abandoning of all fetters."
The Discussion of the Abandoning of All Fetters is finished.
The Fourth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
A householder can be a worthy one; a worthy one at the very moment of rebirth; all things in a worthy one are free of taints; a worthy one is endowed with the four fruits; likewise with six kinds of equanimity; a Buddha by awakening; one endowed with the marks; the bodhisatta had entered the fixed course and lived the holy life; one on the way is endowed with the fruit; the abandoning of all fetters is arahantship. ^5-417

### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-0

#### (43) 1. Discussion of Liberation ^5-13-1-0

Is the knowledge of liberation liberated? Yes. Is any knowledge of liberation whatsoever, all of it, liberated? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation liberated? Yes. Is reviewing knowledge liberated? That should not be said…
Is the knowledge of liberation liberated? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person at the point of change of lineage (gotrabhū) liberated? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry liberated? Yes. Is it the knowledge of a stream-enterer, the knowledge of one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of stream-entry? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning liberated? Yes. Is it the knowledge of a once-returner, the knowledge of one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of once-returning? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning liberated? Yes. Is it the knowledge of a non-returner, the knowledge of one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized the fruit of non-returning? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) liberated? Yes. Is it the knowledge of a worthy one (arahant), the knowledge of one who has attained, obtained, reached and realized arahantship? That should not be said… ^5-418

Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of stream-entry liberated? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry liberated? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of once-returning liberated? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning liberated? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of non-returning liberated? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning liberated? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of arahantship liberated? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of arahantship liberated? That should not be said… ^5-419

Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of stream-entry liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of once-returning liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of non-returning liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of the fruit of non-returning liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? That should not be said… Is the knowledge of liberation of a person possessing the fruit of arahantship liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? Yes. Is the knowledge of liberation of a person practising for the realization of arahantship liberated, and is it the knowledge of one who has attained the fruit? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Liberation is finished. ^5-420

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-2-0

##### (44) 2. Discussion of the Knowledge of One Beyond Training ^5-13-2-1-0

Does a trainee (one still in training) have the knowledge of one beyond training? Yes. Does a trainee know and see the state beyond training, and dwell having entered upon it as something seen, known and realized, and dwell having touched it with the body? That should not be said… But doesn't a trainee not know and not see the state beyond training, and not dwell having entered upon it — it being unseen, unknown and unrealized — and not dwell having touched it with the body? Yes. If a trainee does not know and does not see the state beyond training, and does not dwell having entered upon it — it being unseen, unknown and unrealized — and does not dwell having touched it with the body, then surely you must not say: "A trainee has the knowledge of one beyond training."
One beyond training has the knowledge of one beyond training — does one beyond training know and see the state beyond training, and dwell having entered upon it as something seen, known and realized, and dwell having touched it with the body? Yes. A trainee has the knowledge of one beyond training — does a trainee know and see the state beyond training, and dwell having entered upon it as something seen, known and realized, and dwell having touched it with the body? That should not be said… ^5-421

A trainee has the knowledge of one beyond training — does a trainee not know and not see the state beyond training, and not dwell having entered upon it — it being unseen, unknown and unrealized — and not dwell having touched it with the body? Yes. One beyond training has the knowledge of one beyond training — does one beyond training not know and not see the state beyond training, and not dwell having entered upon it — it being unseen, unknown and unrealized — and not dwell having touched it with the body? That should not be said…
Does a trainee have the knowledge of one beyond training? Yes. Does a person at the point of change of lineage (gotrabhū) have knowledge of the path of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry have knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning… of the fruit of non-returning… of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) have knowledge of arahantship? That should not be said… ^5-422

Should it not be said that "a trainee has the knowledge of one beyond training"? Yes. But doesn't the venerable Ānanda, a trainee, know: "The Blessed One is great," and know: "The elder Sāriputta and the elder Mahāmoggallāna are great"? Yes. If the venerable Ānanda, a trainee, knows: "The Blessed One is great," and knows: "The elder Sāriputta and the elder Mahāmoggallāna are great," then surely you must also say: "A trainee has the knowledge of one beyond training."
The Discussion of the Knowledge of One Beyond Training is finished. ^5-423

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-3-0

##### (45) 3. Discussion of Distortion ^5-13-3-1-0

Is the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa (a meditation device) [variant: pathavīkasiṇasamāpattiṃ (Sī., Ka.)] a distorted knowledge? Yes. Is it the distortion of taking the impermanent as permanent? That should not be said… Of taking the painful as pleasant… of taking what is not self as self… is it the distortion of taking the unattractive as attractive? That should not be said…
Is the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa a distorted knowledge? Yes. Is it unwholesome? That should not be said… But isn't it wholesome? Yes. If it is wholesome, then surely you must not say: "The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge."
Taking the impermanent as permanent is a distortion — and is it unwholesome? Yes. The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge — and is it unwholesome? That should not be said… Taking the painful as pleasant… taking what is not self as self… taking the unattractive as attractive is a distortion — and is it unwholesome? Yes. The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge — and is it unwholesome? That should not be said… ^5-424

The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge — and is it unwholesome? Yes. Taking the impermanent as permanent is a distortion — and is it wholesome? That should not be said… The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge — and is it unwholesome? Yes. Taking the painful as pleasant… taking what is not self as self… taking the unattractive as attractive is a distortion — and is it wholesome? That should not be said… ^5-425

Is the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa a distorted knowledge? Yes. Might a worthy one (arahant) enter the attainment of the earth kasiṇa? Yes. If a worthy one might enter the attainment of the earth kasiṇa, then surely you must not say: "The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge."
The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge — might a worthy one enter the attainment of the earth kasiṇa? Yes. Does a worthy one have distortion? That should not be said…
Does a worthy one have distortion? Yes. Does a worthy one have distortion of perception, distortion of mind, distortion of view? That should not be said…
Does a worthy one not have distortion of perception, distortion of mind, distortion of view? Yes. If a worthy one does not have distortion of perception, distortion of mind, distortion of view, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one has distortion." ^5-426

Should it not be said that the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge? Yes. For one entering the attainment of the earth kasiṇa, is everything earth? That should not be said. In that case the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge.
Is the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa a distorted knowledge? Yes. But doesn't earth exist, and isn't there someone who enters upon earth as earth? Yes. If earth exists, and there is someone who enters upon earth as earth, then surely you must not say: "The knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge."
Earth exists — for one who enters upon earth as earth, is there distortion? Yes. Nibbāna (final release) exists — for one who enters upon nibbāna as nibbāna, is there distortion? That should not be said… In that case it should not be said that "the knowledge of one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa is a distorted knowledge."
The Discussion of Distortion is finished. ^5-427

##### (46) 4. Discussion of the Fixed Course ^5-13-4-1-0

Does one whose course is not fixed have knowledge for going into the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is fixed have knowledge for going into what is not the fixed course? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is fixed not have knowledge for going into what is not the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is not fixed not have knowledge for going into the fixed course? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is not fixed have knowledge for going into the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is fixed have knowledge for going into the fixed course? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is fixed not have knowledge for going into the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is not fixed not have knowledge for going into the fixed course? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is not fixed have knowledge for going into the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is not fixed have knowledge for going into what is not the fixed course? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is not fixed not have knowledge for going into what is not the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is not fixed not have knowledge for going into the fixed course? That should not be said… ^5-428

Does one whose course is not fixed have knowledge for going into the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is not fixed have, for going into the fixed course, the fixed course? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is not fixed have knowledge for going into the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is not fixed have, for going into the fixed course, the foundations of mindfulness… the right strivings… the bases of psychic power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of awakening? That should not be said…

If one whose course is not fixed does not have, for going into the fixed course, the fixed course, then surely you must not say: "One whose course is not fixed has knowledge for going into the fixed course."

But doesn't the Blessed One know: "This person will enter the fixed course of rightness; this person is capable of breaking through to the Dhamma"? Yes. If the Blessed One knows: "This person will enter the fixed course of rightness; this person is capable of breaking through to the Dhamma," then surely you must also say: "One whose course is not fixed has knowledge for going into the fixed course."

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-5-0

##### (47) 5. Discussion of Analytical Knowledge ^5-13-5-1-0

Is all knowledge analytical knowledge? Yes. Is conventional knowledge analytical knowledge? That should not be said… Is conventional knowledge analytical knowledge? Yes. Have all who know convention attained analytical knowledge? That should not be said… Is all knowledge analytical knowledge? Yes. Is knowledge encompassing minds (knowledge of the minds of others) analytical knowledge? That should not be said… Is knowledge encompassing minds analytical knowledge? Yes. Have all who know the minds of others attained analytical knowledge? That should not be said…
Is all knowledge analytical knowledge? Yes. Is all wisdom analytical knowledge? That should not be said… Is all wisdom analytical knowledge? Yes. One who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa (a meditation device) has wisdom — is that wisdom analytical knowledge? That should not be said… The water kasiṇa… the fire kasiṇa… the air kasiṇa… the blue kasiṇa… the yellow kasiṇa… the red kasiṇa… the white kasiṇa… the base of the infinity of space… the base of the infinity of consciousness… the base of nothingness… one who has entered the base of neither perception nor non-perception… one giving a gift… one giving a robe… one giving almsfood… one giving lodging… one giving medicines and requisites for the sick has wisdom — is that wisdom analytical knowledge? That should not be said… ^5-432

Should it not be said that "all knowledge is analytical knowledge"? Yes. There is world-transcending wisdom — is that wisdom not analytical knowledge? That should not be said… In that case all knowledge is analytical knowledge.
The Discussion of Analytical Knowledge is finished. ^5-433

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-6-0

##### (48) 6. Discussion of Conventional Knowledge ^5-13-6-1-0

Should it not be said that "conventional knowledge has truth alone as its object and no other object"? Yes. But doesn't one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa (a meditation device) have knowledge, and isn't the earth kasiṇa within conventional truth? Yes. If one who has entered the attainment of the earth kasiṇa has knowledge, and the earth kasiṇa is within conventional truth, then surely you must also say: "Conventional knowledge has truth alone as its object and no other object."
Should it not be said that "conventional knowledge has truth alone as its object and no other object"? Yes… But doesn't one who has entered the water kasiṇa… the fire kasiṇa… one giving medicines and requisites for the sick have knowledge, and aren't medicines and requisites for the sick within conventional truth? Yes. If one giving medicines and requisites for the sick has knowledge, and medicines and requisites for the sick are within conventional truth, then surely you must also say: "Conventional knowledge has truth alone as its object and no other object." ^5-434

Does conventional knowledge have truth alone as its object and no other object? Yes. With that knowledge does one fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, develop the path? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Conventional Knowledge is finished. ^5-435

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-7-0

##### (49) 7. Discussion of Mind as Object ^5-13-7-1-0

Does knowledge encompassing minds (knowledge of the minds of others) have mind alone as its object and no other object? Yes. But isn't there someone who understands a mind with greed as "a mind with greed"? Yes. If there is someone who understands a mind with greed as "a mind with greed", then surely you must not say: "Knowledge encompassing minds has mind alone as its object and no other object."
But isn't there someone who understands a mind free from greed… a mind with hatred… a mind free from hatred… a mind with delusion… a mind free from delusion… a contracted mind… a scattered mind… an exalted mind… an unexalted mind… a surpassable mind… an unsurpassable mind… a concentrated mind… an unconcentrated mind… a liberated mind… an unliberated mind as "an unliberated mind"? Yes. If there is someone who understands an unliberated mind as "an unliberated mind", then surely you must not say: "Knowledge encompassing minds has mind alone as its object and no other object." ^5-436

Should knowledge that has contact as its object be called "knowledge encompassing minds"? Yes. If knowledge that has contact as its object should be called knowledge encompassing minds, then surely you must not say: "Knowledge encompassing minds has mind alone as its object and no other object." Knowledge that has feeling as its object… perception as its object… intention as its object… mind as its object… faith as its object… energy as its object… mindfulness as its object… concentration as its object… wisdom as its object… greed as its object… hatred as its object… delusion as its object… knowledge that has lack of moral fear as its object — should it be called "knowledge encompassing minds"? Yes. If knowledge that has lack of moral fear as its object should be called knowledge encompassing minds, then surely you must not say: "Knowledge encompassing minds has mind alone as its object and no other object."
Should knowledge that has contact as its object not be called "knowledge encompassing minds"? Yes. Is it knowledge encompassing contact? That should not be said… Should knowledge that has feeling as its object… perception as its object… knowledge that has lack of moral fear as its object not be called "knowledge encompassing minds"? Yes. Is it knowledge encompassing lack of moral fear? That should not be said… ^5-437

Should it not be said that "knowledge encompassing minds has mind alone as its object and no other object"? Yes. But isn't it knowledge encompassing minds? Yes. If it is knowledge encompassing minds, then surely you must also say: "Knowledge encompassing minds has mind alone as its object and no other object."
The Discussion of Mind as Object is finished. ^5-438

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-8-0

##### (50) 8. Discussion of Knowledge of the Future ^5-13-8-1-0

Is there knowledge of the future? Yes. Does one know the future by its root, know it by its cause, know it by its source, know it by its origination, know it by its production, know it by its arising, know it by its nutriment, know it by its object, know it by its condition, know it by its origin? That should not be said…
Is there knowledge of the future? Yes. Does one know the future as a root condition, know it as an object condition, know it as a predominance condition, know it as a proximity condition, know it as an immediate-proximity condition? That should not be said…
Is there knowledge of the future? Yes. Does a person at the point of change of lineage (gotrabhū) have knowledge of the path of stream-entry? That should not be said… Does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry have knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry? That should not be said…
Does a person practising for the realization of the fruit of once-returning… of the fruit of non-returning… of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) have knowledge of arahantship? That should not be said… ^5-439

Should it not be said that "there is knowledge of the future"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Ānanda, three dangers will befall Pāṭaliputta: from fire, from water, or from internal dissension" [Mahāva. 286; D. Ni. 2.152; Udā. 76]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is knowledge of the future.
The Discussion of Knowledge of the Future is finished. ^5-440

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-9-0

##### (51) 9. Discussion of the Present ^5-13-9-1-0

Is there knowledge of the present [variant: paccuppanne (Sī., Syā.)]? Yes. Does one know that knowledge by that same knowledge? That should not be said… Does one know that knowledge by that same knowledge? Yes. Does one know that knowledge as "knowledge" by that same knowledge? That should not be said… Does one know that knowledge as "knowledge" by that same knowledge? Yes. Is that knowledge the object of that same knowledge? That should not be said…
Is that knowledge the object of that same knowledge? Yes. Does one touch that contact by that same contact, feel that feeling by that same feeling, perceive that perception by that same perception, intend that intention by that same intention, think that mind by that same mind, think that thinking by that same thinking, examine that examining by that same examining, delight in that joy by that same joy, remember that mindfulness by that same mindfulness, understand that wisdom by that same wisdom, cut that sword with that same sword, hew that axe with that same axe, hew that hatchet with that same hatchet, hew that adze with that same adze, sew that needle with that same needle, touch that fingertip with that same fingertip, touch that tip of the nose with that same tip of the nose, touch that head with that same head, wash that excrement with that same excrement, wash that urine with that same urine, wash that spittle with that same spittle, wash that pus with that same pus, wash that blood with that same blood? That should not be said… ^5-441

Should it not be said that "there is knowledge of the present"? Yes. But when all formations (conditioned things) are seen as impermanent, isn't that knowledge too seen as impermanent? Yes. If, when all formations are seen as impermanent, that knowledge too is seen as impermanent, then surely you must also say: "There is knowledge of the present."
The Discussion of Knowledge of the Present [variant: paccuppannakathā (Sī.)] is finished. ^5-442

#### The Fifth Chapter ^5-13-10-0

##### (52) 10. Discussion of Knowledge of the Fruit ^5-13-10-1-0

Does a disciple have knowledge of the fruit? Yes. Does a disciple make known what has been accomplished as regards the fruit? That should not be said…
Does a disciple have knowledge of the fruit? Yes. Does a disciple have knowledge of the higher and lower state of fruits, the higher and lower state of faculties, the higher and lower state of persons? That should not be said…
Does a disciple have knowledge of the fruit? Yes. Does a disciple make the designation of the aggregates, the designation of the sense bases, the designation of the elements, the designation of the truths, the designation of the faculties, the designation of persons? That should not be said…
Does a disciple have knowledge of the fruit? Yes. Is a disciple a conqueror, a teacher, a Fully Awakened Buddha, all-knowing, all-seeing, the lord of the Dhamma, the final authority on the Dhamma? That should not be said…
Does a disciple have knowledge of the fruit? Yes. Is a disciple the one who brings into being the path not arisen before, who produces the path not produced before, who declares the path not declared before, the knower of the path, the finder of the path, the one skilled in the path? That should not be said… ^5-443

Should it not be said that "a disciple has knowledge of the fruit"? Yes. Is a disciple without knowledge? That should not be said… In that case a disciple has knowledge of the fruit…
