The Fifth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The knowledge of liberation is liberated; a trainee has the knowledge of one beyond training; distorted knowledge; one whose course is not fixed has knowledge for going into the fixed course; all knowledge is analytical knowledge; conventional knowledge; knowledge encompassing minds; knowledge of the future; knowledge of the present; a disciple has knowledge of the fruit.
The Great Set of Fifty.
Here is its summary too:
The finding of a being, what others bring, the power, a householder can be a worthy one, and liberation as the fifth. ^5-444

### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-0

#### (53) 1. Discussion of the Fixed Course ^5-14-1-0

Is the fixed course unconditioned? Yes. Is it nibbāna (final release), the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the final resort, the imperishable, the deathless? That should not be said…
Is the fixed course unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said…
Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections, two shelters, two refuges, two final resorts, two imperishables, two deathless states, two nibbānas? That should not be said…
Are there two nibbānas? Yes. Is there between the two nibbānas any difference of high and low, of inferior and superior, of better and worse, or any boundary, division, dividing line or gap? That should not be said…
Is the fixed course unconditioned? Yes. Are there some who enter the fixed course, obtain it, make it arise, make it fully arise, raise it up, fully raise it up, produce it, fully produce it, generate it, fully generate it? Yes. Are there some who enter the unconditioned, obtain it, make it arise, make it fully arise, raise it up, fully raise it up, produce it, fully produce it, generate it, fully generate it? That should not be said… ^5-445

Is the fixed course unconditioned? Yes. Is the path unconditioned? That should not be said…
Is the path conditioned? Yes. Is the fixed course conditioned? That should not be said…
Is the fixed course of stream-entry unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of stream-entry unconditioned? That should not be said…
Is the path of stream-entry conditioned? Yes. Is the fixed course of stream-entry conditioned? That should not be said…
Is the fixed course of once-returning… the fixed course of non-returning… the fixed course of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of arahantship unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the path of arahantship conditioned? Yes. Is the fixed course of arahantship conditioned? That should not be said…
Is the fixed course of stream-entry unconditioned… is the fixed course of arahantship unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there five unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there five unconditioned things? Yes. Are there five protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
Is the fixed course unconditioned? Yes. Is the fixed course of wrongness unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the fixed course of wrongness conditioned? Yes. Is the fixed course of rightness conditioned? That should not be said… ^5-446

Should it not be said that "the fixed course is unconditioned"? Yes. When the fixed course has arisen and ceased, does one become one whose course is not fixed? That should not be said… In that case the fixed course is unconditioned. When the fixed course of wrongness has arisen and ceased, does one become one whose course is not fixed? That should not be said… In that case the fixed course of wrongness is unconditioned.
The Discussion of the Fixed Course is finished. ^5-447

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-2-0

##### (54) 2. Discussion of Dependent Arising ^5-14-2-1-0

Is dependent arising unconditioned? Yes. Is it nibbāna (final release), the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the final resort, the imperishable, the deathless? That should not be said… Is dependent arising unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections, two shelters, two refuges, two final resorts, two imperishables, two deathless states, two nibbānas? That should not be said… Are there two nibbānas? Yes. Is there between the two nibbānas any difference of high and low, of inferior and superior, of better and worse, or any boundary, division, dividing line or gap? That should not be said… ^5-448

Is dependent arising unconditioned? Yes. Is ignorance unconditioned? That should not be said… Is ignorance conditioned? Yes. Is dependent arising conditioned? That should not be said… Is dependent arising unconditioned? Yes. Are the formations that have ignorance as their condition unconditioned? That should not be said… Are the formations that have ignorance as their condition conditioned? Yes. Is dependent arising conditioned? That should not be said… Is dependent arising unconditioned? Yes. Is the consciousness that has formations as its condition unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the consciousness that has formations as its condition conditioned? Yes. Is dependent arising conditioned? That should not be said… Is dependent arising unconditioned? Yes. Is the name-and-form (mind and body) that has consciousness as its condition unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the name-and-form that has consciousness as its condition conditioned? Yes. Is dependent arising conditioned? That should not be said… Is dependent arising unconditioned? Yes. Are the ageing and death that have birth as their condition unconditioned? That should not be said… Are the ageing and death that have birth as their condition conditioned? Yes. Is dependent arising conditioned? That should not be said… ^5-449

Should it not be said that "dependent arising is unconditioned"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, with birth as condition there is ageing and death. Whether Tathāgatas (Buddhas) arise or do not arise, that element stands firm — the stability of things, the fixed order of things, specific conditionality. The Tathāgata awakens to it and breaks through to it. Having awakened to it and broken through to it, he explains it, teaches it, makes it known, establishes it, discloses it, analyses it and makes it plain. And he says: ‘See!’ — with birth as condition, monks, there is ageing and death. With existence as condition, monks, there is birth… with ignorance as condition, monks, there are formations. Whether Tathāgatas arise or do not arise, that element stands firm… and he says: ‘See!’ — with ignorance as condition, monks, there are formations. So, monks, the reality in this, the non-falsity, the not-otherwiseness, the specific conditionality — this, monks, is called dependent arising" [S. Ni. 2.20]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case dependent arising is unconditioned. ^5-450

The stability of things, the fixed order of things in "with ignorance as condition there are formations" — is that unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
The stability of things, the fixed order of things in "with ignorance as condition there are formations" — is that unconditioned; the stability of things, the fixed order of things in "with formations as condition there is consciousness" — is that unconditioned; and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there three unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there three unconditioned things? Yes. Are there three protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
The stability of things, the fixed order of things in "with ignorance as condition there are formations" — is that unconditioned; the stability of things, the fixed order of things in "with formations as condition there is consciousness" — is that unconditioned… the stability of things, the fixed order of things in "with birth as condition there is ageing and death" — is that unconditioned; and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there twelve unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there twelve unconditioned things? Yes. Are there twelve protections, twelve shelters… or any gap? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Dependent Arising is finished. ^5-451

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-3-0

##### (55) 3. Discussion of the Truths ^5-14-3-1-0

Are the four truths unconditioned? Yes. Are there four protections, four shelters, four refuges, four final resorts, four imperishables, four deathless states, four nibbānas (final releases)? That should not be said… Are there four nibbānas? Yes. Is there among the four nibbānas any difference of high and low, of inferior and superior, of better and worse, or any boundary, division, dividing line or gap? That should not be said…
Is the truth of suffering unconditioned? Yes. Is suffering unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of suffering unconditioned? Yes. Are bodily suffering, mental suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? Yes. Is the origin unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of the origin unconditioned? Yes. Are craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence and craving for non-existence unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of the path unconditioned? Yes. Is the path unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of the path unconditioned? Yes. Is right view… right concentration unconditioned? That should not be said…
Is suffering conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of suffering conditioned? That should not be said… Are bodily suffering, mental suffering, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief and despair conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of suffering conditioned? That should not be said… Is the origin conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the origin conditioned? That should not be said… Are craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence and craving for non-existence conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the origin conditioned? That should not be said… Is the path conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the path conditioned? That should not be said… Is right view… right concentration conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the path conditioned? That should not be said… ^5-452

Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, and is cessation unconditioned? Yes. Is the truth of suffering unconditioned, and is suffering unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, and is cessation unconditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the origin unconditioned, and is the origin unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, and is cessation unconditioned? Yes. Is the truth of the path unconditioned, and is the path unconditioned? That should not be said…
Is the truth of suffering unconditioned, while suffering is conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, while cessation is conditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of the origin unconditioned, while the origin is conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, while cessation is conditioned? That should not be said… Is the truth of the path unconditioned, while the path is conditioned? Yes. Is the truth of cessation unconditioned, while cessation is conditioned? That should not be said… ^5-453

Should it not be said that "the four truths are unconditioned"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are real, not unreal, not otherwise. Which four? ‘This is suffering,’ monks — this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise… ‘This is the origin of suffering’… ‘This is the cessation of suffering’… ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering’ — this is real, this is not unreal, this is not otherwise. These, monks, are the four things that are real, not unreal, not otherwise" [S. Ni. 5.1090]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the four truths are unconditioned.
The Discussion of the Truths is finished. ^5-454

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-4-0

##### (56) 4. Discussion of the Formless States ^5-14-4-1-0

Is the base of the infinity of space unconditioned? Yes. Is it nibbāna (final release), the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the final resort, the imperishable, the deathless? That should not be said… Is the base of the infinity of space unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
Is the base of the infinity of space unconditioned? Yes. Is the base of the infinity of space an existence, a destination, an abode of beings, a round of rebirth, a mode of birth, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individual existence? Yes. Is the unconditioned an existence, a destination, an abode of beings, a round of rebirth, a mode of birth, a station of consciousness, an acquisition of individual existence? That should not be said…
Is there action that leads to rebirth in the base of the infinity of space? Yes. Is there action that leads to rebirth in the unconditioned? That should not be said… Are there beings reborn in the base of the infinity of space? Yes. Are there beings reborn in the unconditioned? That should not be said…
In the base of the infinity of space, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away and are they reborn? Yes. In the unconditioned, are beings born, do they age, die, pass away and are they reborn? That should not be said… In the base of the infinity of space, are there feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness? Yes. In the unconditioned, are there feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness? That should not be said… Is the base of the infinity of space a four-aggregate existence? Yes. Is the unconditioned a four-aggregate existence? That should not be said… ^5-455

Should it not be said that "the four formless states are unconditioned"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the four formless states to be imperturbable? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the four formless states to be imperturbable, then surely you must also say: "The four formless states are unconditioned."
The Discussion of the Formless States is finished. ^5-456

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-5-0

##### (57) 5. Discussion of the Attainment of Cessation ^5-14-5-1-0

Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned? Yes. Is it nibbāna (final release), the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the final resort, the imperishable, the deathless? That should not be said… Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
Is the attainment of cessation unconditioned? Yes. Are there some who enter cessation, obtain it, make it arise, make it fully arise, raise it up, fully raise it up, produce it, fully produce it, generate it, fully generate it? Yes. Are there some who enter the unconditioned, obtain it, make it arise, make it fully arise, raise it up, fully raise it up, produce it, fully produce it, generate it, fully generate it? That should not be said… ^5-457

Is a cleansing, an emergence from cessation, discerned? Yes. Is a cleansing, an emergence from the unconditioned, discerned? That should not be said… For one entering cessation, does the verbal formation cease first, then the bodily formation, then the mental formation? Yes. For one entering the unconditioned, does the verbal formation cease first, then the bodily formation, then the mental formation? That should not be said… For one emerging from cessation, does the mental formation arise first, then the bodily formation, then the verbal formation? Yes. For one emerging from the unconditioned, does the mental formation arise first, then the bodily formation, then the verbal formation? That should not be said…
Do three contacts touch one who has emerged from cessation — the contact of emptiness, the signless contact, the desireless contact? Yes. Do three contacts touch one who has emerged from the unconditioned — the contact of emptiness, the signless contact, the desireless contact? That should not be said…
For one who has emerged from cessation, does the mind incline towards seclusion, slope towards seclusion, lean towards seclusion? Yes. For one who has emerged from the unconditioned, does the mind incline towards seclusion, slope towards seclusion, lean towards seclusion? That should not be said… ^5-458

Should it not be said that "the attainment of cessation is unconditioned"? Yes. Is it conditioned? That should not be said… In that case the attainment of cessation is unconditioned.
The Discussion of the Attainment of Cessation is finished. ^5-459

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-6-0

##### (58) 6. Discussion of Space ^5-14-6-1-0

Is space unconditioned? Yes. Is it nibbāna (final release), the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the final resort, the imperishable, the deathless? That should not be said… Is space unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
Is space unconditioned? Yes. Are there some who make what is not space into space? Yes. Are there some who make the conditioned into the unconditioned? That should not be said… Are there some who make space into what is not space? Yes. Are there some who make the unconditioned into the conditioned? That should not be said…
In space do birds go, do the moon and sun go, do the stars go, do people perform feats of psychic power, move their arms, move their hands, throw clods, throw sticks, project psychic power [variant: sattiṃ (?)], shoot arrows? Yes. In the unconditioned do birds go, do the moon and sun go, do the stars go, do people perform feats of psychic power, move their arms, move their hands, throw clods, throw sticks, project psychic power, shoot arrows? That should not be said… ^5-460

Do people build houses and build storerooms by enclosing space? Yes. Do people build houses and build storerooms by enclosing the unconditioned? That should not be said…
When a well is being dug, does what is not space become space? Yes. Does the conditioned become unconditioned? That should not be said…
When an empty well is being filled, when an empty storeroom is being filled, when an empty pot is being filled, does space disappear? Yes. Does the unconditioned disappear? That should not be said… ^5-461

Should it not be said that "space is unconditioned"? Yes. Is space conditioned? That should not be said… In that case space is unconditioned.
The Discussion of Space is finished. ^5-462

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-7-0

##### (59) 7. Discussion of "Space Is Visible" ^5-14-7-1-0

Is space visible? Yes. Is it a visible form, the visible-form base, the visible-form element, blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by the eye; does it strike the eye, does it come within range of the eye? That should not be said…
Is space visible? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on space? That should not be said…
Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on space? Yes. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on space" — is there really [variant: atthi (?)] such a discourse? There is not. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" [M. Ni. 1.400; 3.421; S. Ni. 4.60] — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms," then surely you must not say: "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on space." ^5-463

Should it not be said that "space is visible"? Yes. But doesn't one see the gap between two trees, the gap between two posts, a keyhole, a window opening? Yes. If one sees the gap between two trees, the gap between two posts, a keyhole, a window opening, then surely you must also say: "Space is visible."
The Discussion of "Space Is Visible" is finished. ^5-464

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-8-0

##### (60) 8. Discussion of "The Earth Element Is Visible" and So On ^5-14-8-1-0

Is the earth element visible? Yes. Is it a visible form, the visible-form base, the visible-form element, blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by the eye; does it strike the eye, does it come within range of the eye? That should not be said…
Is the earth element visible? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on the earth element? That should not be said…
Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on the earth element? Yes. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on the earth element" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms," then surely you must not say: "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on the earth element." ^5-465

Should it not be said that "the earth element is visible"? Yes. But doesn't one see the ground, rocks, mountains? Yes. If one sees [variant: passasi (Sī., Syā., Ka.), so also below] the ground, rocks, mountains, then surely you must also say: "The earth element is visible."…
Should it not be said that "the water element is visible"? Yes. But doesn't one see water? Yes. If one sees water, then surely you must also say: "The water element is visible."…
Should it not be said that the fire element is visible? Yes. But doesn't one see a fire burning? Yes. If one sees a fire burning, then surely you must also say: "The fire element is visible."…
Should it not be said that "the air element is visible"? Yes. But doesn't one see trees being shaken by the wind? Yes. If one sees trees being shaken by the wind, then surely you must also say: "The air element is visible."…
The Discussion of "The Earth Element Is Visible" and So On is finished. ^5-466

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-9-0

##### (61) 9. Discussion of "The Eye Faculty Is Visible" and So On ^5-14-9-1-0

Is the eye faculty visible? Yes. Is it a visible form, the visible-form base, the visible-form element… does it come within range of the eye? That should not be said…
Is the eye faculty visible? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on the eye faculty? That should not be said…
Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on the eye faculty? Yes. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on the eye faculty" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms," then surely you must not say: "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on the eye faculty." ^5-467

Should it not be said that "the five faculties are visible"? Yes. But doesn't one see the eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body? Yes. If one sees the eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, then surely you must also say: "The five faculties are visible."…
The Discussion of "The Eye Faculty Is Visible" and So On is finished. ^5-468

#### The Sixth Chapter ^5-14-10-0

##### (62) 10. Discussion of "Bodily Action Is Visible" ^5-14-10-1-0

Is bodily action visible? Yes. Is it a visible form, the visible-form base, the visible-form element, blue, yellow, red, white, cognizable by the eye; does it strike the eye, does it come within range of the eye? That should not be said…
Is bodily action visible? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on bodily action? That should not be said…
Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on bodily action? Yes. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on bodily action" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms," then surely you must not say: "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on bodily action." ^5-469

Should it not be said that "bodily action is visible"? Yes. But doesn't one see someone going forward, going back, looking ahead, looking around, bending a limb, stretching a limb? Yes. If one sees someone going forward, going back, looking ahead, looking around, bending a limb, stretching a limb, then surely you must also say: "Bodily action is visible."
The Discussion of "Bodily Action Is Visible" is finished.
The Sixth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The fixed course is unconditioned; dependent arising is unconditioned; the four truths are unconditioned; the four formless states are unconditioned; the attainment of cessation is unconditioned; space is unconditioned; space is visible; the four great elements; the five faculties; and likewise bodily action. ^5-470

### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-0

#### (63) 1. Discussion of Inclusion ^5-15-1-0

Are there no states that are included by any states [variant: saṅgahītāti (Pī.)]? Yes. But aren't there some states that are counted together with some states, come under the same heading as them, and are included with them? Yes. If there are some states that are counted together with some states, come under the same heading as them, and are included with them, then surely you must not say: "There are no states that are included by any states."
Into the count of which aggregate [variant: katamaṃ khandhagaṇanaṃ (Sī., Pī., Ka.)] does the eye base go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of material form. If the eye base goes into the count of the aggregate of material form, then surely you must also say: "The eye base is included by the aggregate of material form." Into the count of which aggregate does the ear base… the nose base… the tongue base… the body base go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of material form. If the body base goes into the count of the aggregate of material form, then surely you must also say: "The body base is included by the aggregate of material form."
Into the count of which aggregate does the visible-form base… the sound base… the smell base… the taste base… the touch base go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of material form. If the touch base goes into the count of the aggregate of material form, then surely you must also say: "The touch base is included by the aggregate of material form."
Into the count of which aggregate does pleasant feeling go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of feeling. If pleasant feeling goes into the count of the aggregate of feeling, then surely you must also say: "Pleasant feeling is included by the aggregate of feeling." Into the count of which aggregate does painful feeling… neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of feeling. If neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling goes into the count of the aggregate of feeling, then surely you must also say: "Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is included by the aggregate of feeling."
Into the count of which aggregate does perception born of eye-contact go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of perception. If perception born of eye-contact goes into the count of the aggregate of perception, then surely you must also say: "Perception born of eye-contact is included by the aggregate of perception." Into the count of which aggregate does perception born of ear-contact… perception born of mind-contact go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of perception. If perception born of mind-contact goes into the count of the aggregate of perception, then surely you must also say: "Perception born of mind-contact is included by the aggregate of perception."
Into the count of which aggregate does intention born of eye-contact… intention born of mind-contact go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of mental formations. If intention born of mind-contact goes into the count of the aggregate of mental formations, then surely you must also say: "Intention born of mind-contact is included by the aggregate of mental formations."
Into the count of which aggregate does eye-consciousness… mind-consciousness go? It goes into the count of the aggregate of consciousness. If mind-consciousness goes into the count of the aggregate of consciousness, then surely you must also say: "Mind-consciousness is included by the aggregate of consciousness." ^5-471

Just as two oxen are held together by a rope or by a yoke-tie, almsfood is held in a sling-bag, and a dog is held by a leash — are those states held together by those states in just the same way [the statement of our own school (see the commentary)]? If two oxen are held together by a rope or by a yoke-tie, almsfood is held in a sling-bag, and a dog is held by a leash, then surely you must also say: "There are some states that are included by some states" [the statement of our own school (see the commentary)].
The Discussion of Inclusion is finished. ^5-472

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-2-0

##### (64) 2. Discussion of Association ^5-15-2-1-0

Are there no states that are associated with any states? Yes. But aren't there some states that are accompanied by some states, arisen together with them, mixed with them, that arise together with them, cease together with them, have the same base and have the same object? Yes. If there are some states that are accompanied by some states, arisen together with them, mixed with them, that arise together with them, cease together with them, have the same base and have the same object, then surely you must not say: "There are no states that are associated with any states."
Has the aggregate of feeling arisen together with the aggregate of perception? Yes. If the aggregate of feeling has arisen together with the aggregate of perception, then surely you must also say: "The aggregate of feeling is associated with the aggregate of perception."
Has the aggregate of feeling arisen together with the aggregate of mental formations… with the aggregate of consciousness? Yes. If the aggregate of feeling has arisen together with the aggregate of consciousness, then surely you must also say: "The aggregate of feeling is associated with the aggregate of consciousness."
Has the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of mental formations… the aggregate of consciousness arisen together with the aggregate of feeling… with the aggregate of perception… with the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. If the aggregate of consciousness has arisen together with the aggregate of mental formations, then surely you must also say: "The aggregate of consciousness is associated with the aggregate of mental formations." ^5-473

Just as oil pervades and permeates sesame seed, and juice pervades and permeates sugar cane, do those states in just the same way pervade and permeate those states? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Association is finished. ^5-474

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-3-0

##### (65) 3. Discussion of Mental Factors ^5-15-3-1-0

Is there no mental factor (a state belonging to the mind)? Yes. But aren't there some states that are accompanied by the mind, arisen together with it, mixed with it, associated with it, that arise together with it, cease together with it, have the same base and have the same object? Yes. If there are some states that are accompanied by the mind, arisen together with it, mixed with it, associated with it, that arise together with it, cease together with it, have the same base and have the same object, then surely you must not say: "There is no mental factor."
Has contact arisen together with the mind? Yes. If contact has arisen together with the mind, then surely you must also say: "Contact is a mental factor." Has feeling… perception… intention… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom… greed… hatred… delusion… lack of moral fear arisen together with the mind? Yes. If lack of moral fear has arisen together with the mind, then surely you must also say: "Lack of moral fear is a mental factor." ^5-475

On the grounds that they have arisen together with the mind, are they mental factors? Yes. On the grounds that they have arisen together with contact, are they contact factors [variant: phassikāti (Pī., Aṭṭha.)]? Yes. On the grounds that they have arisen together with the mind, are they mental factors? Yes. On the grounds that they have arisen together with feeling… perception… intention… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom… greed… hatred… delusion… lack of moral fear, are they lack-of-moral-fear factors [variant: anottappikāti (?)]? Yes. ^5-476

Is there no mental factor? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"This mind, and the states that are mental factors,
are known as not self by one who has clearly understood;
having known both of these, the inferior and the superior,
the one with right vision has understood what is subject to breaking up"?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is a mental factor.
Is there no mental factor? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, Kevaṭṭa, a monk declares the mind of other beings, of other persons, declares their mental factors, declares their thinking, declares their examining: ‘Such is your mind, thus is your mind, so is your thought’" [D. Ni. 1.485]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is a mental factor.
The Discussion of Mental Factors is finished. ^5-477

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-4-0

##### (66) 4. Discussion of the Gift ^5-15-4-1-0

Is a gift a mental factor? Yes. Can a mental factor be given to others? That should not be said… Can a mental factor be given to others? Yes. Can contact be given to others? That should not be said… Can feeling… perception… intention… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom be given to others? That should not be said… ^5-478

Should it not be said that a gift is a mental factor? Yes. Is a gift something whose fruit is undesirable, unlovely, disagreeable and unsatisfying, with suffering as its outcome and suffering as its result? That should not be said… But isn't a gift something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? Yes. If a gift is something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result, then surely you must also say: "A gift is a mental factor."
The Blessed One said that a gift has a desirable fruit — is a robe a gift [this is like the question of the other school stated below; the commentary should be consulted]? Yes. Is a robe something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? That should not be said… The Blessed One said that a gift has a desirable fruit — are almsfood, lodging, and medicines and requisites for the sick a gift? Yes. Are medicines and requisites for the sick something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? That should not be said… ^5-479

Should it not be said that "a gift is a mental factor"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Faith, a sense of shame and the wholesome gift —
these are things followed by good people;
for this, they say, is the divine path;
by this one goes to the world of the gods" [A. Ni. 8.32]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case a gift is a mental factor.
Should it not be said that "a gift is a mental factor"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these five gifts, great gifts, recognized as foremost, recognized as of long standing, recognized as traditional, ancient, unadulterated, never adulterated before, which are not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, and which are not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. Which five? Here, monks, a noble disciple, having abandoned the killing of living beings, abstains from killing living beings. Monks, by abstaining from killing living beings, a noble disciple gives fearlessness, gives freedom from hostility, gives freedom from ill will [variant: abyāpajjhaṃ (Syā., Ka.)] to immeasurable beings. Having given fearlessness, freedom from hostility and freedom from ill will to immeasurable beings, they come to share in immeasurable fearlessness, freedom from hostility and freedom from ill will. This, monks, is the first gift, a great gift, recognized as foremost, recognized as of long standing, recognized as traditional, ancient, unadulterated, never adulterated before, which is not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, and which is not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. Again, monks, a noble disciple, having abandoned taking what is not given… having abandoned sexual misconduct… having abandoned false speech… having abandoned liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, abstains from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness. Monks, by abstaining from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness, a noble disciple gives fearlessness, gives freedom from hostility, gives freedom from ill will to immeasurable beings. Having given fearlessness, freedom from hostility and freedom from ill will to immeasurable beings, they come to share in immeasurable fearlessness, freedom from hostility and freedom from ill will. This, monks, is the fifth gift, a great gift, recognized as foremost, recognized as of long standing, recognized as traditional, ancient, unadulterated, never adulterated before, which is not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, and which is not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins. These, monks, are the five gifts, great gifts, recognized as foremost, recognized as of long standing, recognized as traditional, ancient, unadulterated, never adulterated before, which are not being adulterated and will not be adulterated, and which are not rejected by wise ascetics and brahmins" [A. Ni. 8.39]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case a gift is a mental factor. ^5-480

Should it not be said that "the thing to be given is a gift"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here someone gives food, gives drink, gives clothing, gives a vehicle, gives garlands, gives scent, gives ointment, gives a bed, gives a dwelling, gives lamps" [S. Ni. 3.362-391, slightly different]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the thing to be given is a gift. ^5-481

Is the thing to be given a gift? Yes. Is the thing to be given something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? That should not be said… The Blessed One said that a gift has a desirable fruit — is a robe a gift? Yes. Is a robe something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? That should not be said… The Blessed One said that a gift has a desirable fruit — is almsfood a gift… is lodging a gift… are medicines and requisites for the sick a gift? Yes. Are medicines and requisites for the sick something whose fruit is desirable, lovely, agreeable and wholly satisfying, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result? That should not be said… In that case it should not be said that "the thing to be given is a gift."
The Discussion of the Gift is finished. ^5-482

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-5-0

##### (67) 5. Discussion of Merit Arising from Use ^5-15-5-1-0

Does merit arising from use (of what was given) grow? Yes. Does contact arising from use grow, does feeling grow, does perception grow, does intention grow, does the mind grow, does faith grow, does energy grow, does mindfulness grow, does concentration grow, does wisdom grow? That should not be said…
Does merit arising from use grow? Yes. Does it grow like a creeper, grow like a vine, grow like a tree, grow like grass, grow like a clump of reeds? That should not be said… ^5-483

Does merit arising from use grow? Yes. When a giver has given a gift and does not bring it to mind, is there merit? Yes. Is there merit for one who does not turn the mind to it [variant: anāvaṭṭantassa (Sī., Pī., Ka.), anāvajjhantassa (Syā.)]… for one without concern… for one who does not bring it to mind… for one who does not attend to it… for one who does not intend… for one who does not wish… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But isn't there merit for one who turns the mind to it… for one with concern… for one who brings it to mind… for one who attends to it… for one who intends… for one who wishes… for one who aspires? Yes. If there is merit for one who turns the mind to it… for one with concern… for one who brings it to mind… for one who attends to it… for one who intends… for one who wishes… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "Merit arising from use grows." ^5-484

Does merit arising from use grow? Yes. When a giver has given a gift and thinks thoughts of sensual desire, thinks thoughts of ill will, thinks thoughts of harming, is there merit? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said… Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? The sky, monks, and the earth — this is the first thing that is very far apart. The near shore of the ocean, monks, and the far shore — this is the second thing that is very far apart. Where the sun rises, monks, and where it sets — this is the third thing that is very far apart. The Dhamma of the good, monks, and the Dhamma of the bad — this is the fourth thing that is very far apart. These, monks, are the four things that are very far apart.
"The sky is far, and the earth is far;
the far shore of the ocean, they say, is far;
and where the sun rises,
and where the maker of light sets.
"Even farther apart than that, they say,
are the Dhamma of the good and the Dhamma of the bad;
the company of the good does not fade away;
for as long as it lasts, it stays just the same.
"For the company of the bad soon passes [variant: khippaṃhaveti (many editions)];
therefore the Dhamma of the good is far from the bad" [A. Ni. 4.47]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face." ^5-485

Should it not be said that "merit arising from use grows"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Those who plant groves, who plant woods, those people who build bridges,
who give a place for drinking water and a well, who give a shelter —
"for them, by day and by night, merit always grows;
established in the Dhamma, endowed with virtue, those people are bound for heaven" [S. Ni. 1.47]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case merit arising from use grows.
Should it not be said that "merit arising from use grows"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nutriments of happiness, heavenly, ripening in happiness, leading to heaven, which lead to what is desirable, lovely and agreeable, to welfare and to happiness. Which four? Monks, when a monk, while using someone's robe, enters and dwells in a boundless concentration of mind, boundless is that person's stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nutriment of happiness, heavenly, ripening in happiness, leading to heaven, which leads to what is desirable, lovely and agreeable, to welfare and to happiness. Monks, when a monk, while using someone's almsfood… while using someone's lodging… while using someone's medicines and requisites for the sick, enters and dwells in a boundless concentration of mind, boundless is that person's stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nutriment of happiness, heavenly, ripening in happiness, leading to heaven, which leads to what is desirable, lovely and agreeable, to welfare and to happiness. These, monks, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nutriments of happiness, heavenly, ripening in happiness, leading to heaven, which lead to what is desirable, lovely and agreeable, to welfare and to happiness" [A. Ni. 4.51]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case merit arising from use grows. ^5-486

Does merit arising from use grow? Yes. When a giver gives a gift, and the recipient, having received it, does not use it but throws it away or gives it away, is there merit? Yes. If, when a giver gives a gift, and the recipient, having received it, does not use it but throws it away or gives it away, there is merit, then surely you must not say: "Merit arising from use grows."
Does merit arising from use grow? Yes. When a giver gives a gift, and after the recipient has received it, kings take it away, or thieves take it away, or fire burns it, or water carries it away, or unloved heirs take it away, is there merit? Yes. If, when a giver gives a gift, and after the recipient has received it, kings take it away, or thieves take it away, or fire burns it, or water carries it away, or unloved heirs take it away, there is merit, then surely you must not say: "Merit arising from use grows."
The Discussion of Merit Arising from Use is finished. ^5-487

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-6-0

##### (68) 6. Discussion of "What Is Given from Here" ^5-15-6-1-0

Do they sustain themselves there on what is given from here? Yes. People give a robe here — do they use that robe there? That should not be said… People give almsfood here, give lodging here, give medicines and requisites for the sick here, give food to chew here, give meals here, give drink here — do they consume that drink there? That should not be said…
Do they sustain themselves there on what is given from here? Yes. Is one person the doer for another; is pleasure and pain made by another; does one person act and another experience? That should not be said… ^5-488

Should it not be said that "they sustain themselves there on what is given from here"? Yes. But don't ghosts rejoice in someone who gives a gift for their benefit, gain confidence in their minds, give rise to joy and obtain gladness? Yes. If ghosts rejoice in someone who gives a gift for their benefit, gain confidence in their minds, give rise to joy and obtain gladness, then surely you must also say: "They sustain themselves there on what is given from here." ^5-489

Should it not be said that "they sustain themselves there on what is given from here"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"As rain that has fallen on high ground flows down to the low,
just so what is given from here benefits the ghosts.
"As rivers when full fill up the ocean,
just so what is given from here benefits the ghosts.
"For there is no farming there, and no cattle-keeping is found there;
there is no trade like that, no buying and selling with gold [variant: kayakkayaṃ (Sī., Pī.)];
on what is given from here the ghosts, the departed, sustain themselves there" [Khu. Pā. 7.6; Pe. Va. 19]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case they sustain themselves there on what is given from here. ^5-490

Should it not be said that "they sustain themselves there on what is given from here"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, seeing these five reasons, mothers and fathers wish for a son to be born in their family. Which five? He, whom we have supported, will support us; he will do our work; the family line will last long; he will take over the inheritance; or else he will give offerings on behalf of the departed who have died — seeing these five reasons, monks, mothers and fathers wish for a son to be born in their family."
"Seeing five reasons, the wise wish for a son:
he, whom we have supported, will support us; he will do our work;
"the family line will last long; he will take over the inheritance;
or else he will give offerings on behalf of the departed.
"Seeing these reasons, the wise wish for a son;
therefore the peaceful and good, grateful and thankful,
"support their mother and father, remembering what was done for them before;
they do their work for them, as for those who helped them before.
"Following their advice, supporting those who supported him, not letting the family line decline,
having faith and endowed with virtue — such a son is worthy of praise" [A. Ni. 5.31]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case they sustain themselves there on what is given from here.
The Discussion of "What Is Given from Here" is finished. ^5-491

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-7-0

##### (69) 7. Discussion of "The Earth Is a Result of Action" ^5-15-7-1-0

Is the earth a result of action? Yes. Is it to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant; is it associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with intention, associated with mind; does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind [variant: āvajjanā (Syā., Kaṃ.)], concern, bringing to mind, attention, intention, wish and aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful, not to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant, not associated with pleasant feeling, not associated with painful feeling, not associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, not associated with contact, not associated with feeling, not associated with perception, not associated with intention, not associated with mind, that it is without an object, and that it has no turning of the mind, concern, bringing to mind, attention, intention, wish or aspiration? Yes. If it is not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… without an object, and has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "The earth is a result of action."
Contact is a result of action — is contact to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant, associated with pleasant feeling, painful… associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with intention, associated with mind; does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. The earth is a result of action — is the earth to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant, associated with pleasant feeling, painful… associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with intention, associated with mind; does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind, concern, bringing to mind, attention, intention, wish and aspiration? That should not be said… The earth is a result of action — is the earth not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… without an object; does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Contact is a result of action — is contact not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… without an object; does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said…
Is the earth a result of action? Yes. Is the earth subject to being held up and held down, subject to cutting and breaking? Yes. Is a result of action subject to being held up and held down, subject to cutting and breaking? That should not be said…
Can the earth be bought, sold, pledged, collected and gathered? Yes. Can a result of action be bought, sold, pledged, collected and gathered? That should not be said… ^5-492

Is the earth shared with others? Yes. Is a result of action shared with others? That should not be said…
Is a result of action shared with others? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"A treasure not shared with others, which thieves cannot carry off —
let a mortal make merit, if they would live in good conduct" [Khu. Pā. 8.9, in the Khuddakapāṭha, slightly different]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a result of action is shared with others."
Is the earth a result of action? Yes. Does the earth take shape first, and do beings arise afterwards? Yes. Does the result arise first, and do they afterwards perform action in order to obtain the result? That should not be said…
Is the earth a result of the action of all beings? Yes. Do all beings make use of the earth? That should not be said… Do all beings make use of the earth? Yes. Are there some who attain final nibbāna (final release) without having made use of the earth? Yes. Are there some who attain final nibbāna without having used up the result of their action? That should not be said…
Is the earth a result of the action of a wheel-turning king (a universal monarch)? Yes. Do other beings make use of the earth? Yes. Do other beings make use of the result of a wheel-turning king's action? That should not be said… Do other beings make use of the result of a wheel-turning king's action? Yes. Do other beings make use of a wheel-turning king's contact, feeling, perception, intention, mind, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom? That should not be said… ^5-493

Should it not be said that "the earth is a result of action"? Yes. But isn't there action that leads to sovereignty, action that leads to lordship? Yes. If there is action that leads to sovereignty, action that leads to lordship, then surely you must also say: "The earth is a result of action."
The Discussion of "The Earth Is a Result of Action" is finished. ^5-494

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-8-0

##### (70) 8. Discussion of "Ageing and Death Are a Result" ^5-15-8-1-0

Are ageing and death a result? Yes. Are they to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful, to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant; are they associated with pleasant feeling, associated with painful feeling, associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, associated with contact, associated with feeling, associated with perception, associated with intention, associated with mind; do they have an object; do they have turning of the mind, concern, bringing to mind, attention, intention, wish and aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that they are not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… that they are without an object, and that they have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. If they are not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… without an object, and have no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "Ageing and death are a result."
Contact is a result — is contact to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful… does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Ageing and death are a result — are ageing and death to be felt as pleasant, to be felt as painful… do they have an object; do they have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said…
Ageing and death are a result — are ageing and death not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… without an object; do they have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Contact is a result — is contact not to be felt as pleasant, not to be felt as painful… without an object; does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… ^5-495

The ageing and death of unwholesome states — is it a result of unwholesome states? Yes. The ageing and death of wholesome states — is it a result of wholesome states? That should not be said…
The ageing and death of wholesome states — should it not be called "a result of wholesome states"? Yes. The ageing and death of unwholesome states — should it not be called "a result of unwholesome states"? That should not be said…
The ageing and death of wholesome states — is it a result of unwholesome states? Yes. The ageing and death of unwholesome states — is it a result of wholesome states? That should not be said…
The ageing and death of unwholesome states — should it not be called "a result of wholesome states"? Yes. The ageing and death of wholesome states — should it not be called "a result of unwholesome states"? That should not be said…
The ageing and death of wholesome and unwholesome states — is it a result of unwholesome states? Yes. The ageing and death of wholesome and unwholesome states — is it a result of wholesome states? That should not be said…
The ageing and death of wholesome and unwholesome states — should it not be called "a result of wholesome states"? Yes. The ageing and death of wholesome and unwholesome states — should it not be called "a result of unwholesome states"? That should not be said… ^5-496

Should it not be said that "ageing and death are a result"? Yes. But isn't there action that leads to ugliness, action that leads to a short life? Yes. If there is action that leads to ugliness, action that leads to a short life, then surely you must also say: "Ageing and death are a result."
The Discussion of "Ageing and Death Are a Result" is finished. ^5-497

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-9-0

##### (71) 9. Discussion of the Result of the Noble States ^5-15-9-1-0

Is there no result of the noble states? Yes. But isn't the ascetic life of great fruit, and brahminhood (the state of a true brahmin) of great fruit? Yes. If the ascetic life is of great fruit, and brahminhood is of great fruit, then surely you must not say: "There is no result of the noble states."
Is there no result of the noble states? Yes. But isn't there the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If there is the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you must not say: "There is no result of the noble states." But isn't there the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship (the state of a worthy one)? Yes. If there is the fruit of arahantship, then surely you must not say: "There is no result of the noble states."
Is the fruit of stream-entry not a result? Yes. Is the fruit of giving not a result? That should not be said… Is the fruit of stream-entry not a result? Yes. Is the fruit of virtue… the fruit of meditative development not a result? That should not be said…
Is the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship not a result? Yes. Is the fruit of giving not a result? That should not be said… Is the fruit of arahantship not a result? Yes. Is the fruit of virtue… the fruit of meditative development not a result? That should not be said… Is the fruit of giving a result? Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry a result? That should not be said…
Is the fruit of giving a result? Yes. Is the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship a result? That should not be said… Is the fruit of virtue… the fruit of meditative development a result? Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry a result? That should not be said… Is the fruit of meditative development a result? Yes. Is the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship a result? That should not be said… ^5-498

Does what is wholesome and belongs to the sense-desire realm have a result? Yes. Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have a result? That should not be said… Does what is wholesome and belongs to the realm of form… what is wholesome and belongs to the formless realm have a result? Yes. Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have a result? That should not be said…
Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have no result? Yes. Does what is wholesome and belongs to the sense-desire realm have no result? That should not be said… Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have no result? Yes. Does what is wholesome and belongs to the realm of form… what is wholesome and belongs to the formless realm have no result? That should not be said… ^5-499

Does what is wholesome and belongs to the sense-desire realm have a result and lead to building up? Yes. Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have a result and lead to building up? That should not be said… Does what is wholesome and belongs to the realm of form… what is wholesome and belongs to the formless realm have a result and lead to building up? Yes. Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have a result and lead to building up? That should not be said…
Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have a result and lead to dismantling? Yes. Does what is wholesome and belongs to the sense-desire realm have a result and lead to dismantling? That should not be said… Does what is wholesome and world-transcending have a result and lead to dismantling? Yes. Does what is wholesome and belongs to the realm of form… what is wholesome and belongs to the formless realm have a result and lead to dismantling? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Result of the Noble States is finished. ^5-500

#### The Seventh Chapter ^5-15-10-0

##### (72) 10. Discussion of "A Result Is a State That Produces Results" ^5-15-10-1-0

Is a result a state that produces results? Yes. Is the result of that result a state that produces results? That should not be said… Is the result of that result a state that produces results? Yes. Then for each one in turn is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the cycle of rebirth, no complete nibbāna (final release) without clinging? That should not be said…
Is a result a state that produces results? Yes. Are "result" and "a state that produces results", "a state that produces results" and "result" — are these the same, one in meaning, equal, alike in every part, of the same kind? That should not be said…
Is a result a state that produces results? Yes. Are the result and the state that produces results, the state that produces results and the result, accompanied by each other, arisen together, mixed, associated, arising together, ceasing together, with the same base and the same object? That should not be said…
Is a result a state that produces results? Yes. Is that very unwholesome thing the result of the unwholesome, and that very wholesome thing the result of the wholesome? That should not be said…
Is a result a state that produces results? Yes. With the very same mind with which one kills a living being, does one burn in hell; with the very same mind with which one gives a gift, does one rejoice in heaven? That should not be said… ^5-501

Should it not be said that "a result is a state that produces results"? Yes. But aren't the four non-material aggregates that are results conditions for one another? Yes. If the four non-material aggregates that are results are conditions for one another, then surely you must also say: "A result is a state that produces results."
The Discussion of "A Result Is a State That Produces Results" is finished.
The Seventh Chapter.
Here is its summary:
Inclusion, association, mental factors, the gift is a mental factor, merit arising from use grows, they sustain themselves there on what is given from here, the earth is a result of action, ageing and death are a result, there is no result of the noble states, a result is a state that produces results. ^5-502

### The Eighth Chapter ^5-16-0

#### (73) 1. Discussion of the Six Destinations ^5-16-1-0

Are there six destinations? Yes. But didn't the Blessed One speak of five destinations — hell, the animal realm, the realm of ghosts, human beings and gods [M. Ni. 1.153]? Yes. If the Blessed One spoke of five destinations — hell, the animal realm, the realm of ghosts, human beings and gods — then surely you must not say: "There are six destinations."
Are there six destinations? Yes. But aren't the Kālakañcika titans (asuras) [variant: kālakañjikā (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ.), kāḷakañjakā (Pī.)] of the same appearance, the same enjoyments, the same food and the same life span as the ghosts, and don't they marry and intermarry with the ghosts? Yes. If the Kālakañcika titans are of the same appearance, the same enjoyments, the same food and the same life span as the ghosts, and marry and intermarry with the ghosts, then surely you must not say: "There are six destinations."
Are there six destinations? Yes. Are the five sense bases alone sensual pleasures? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. Which five? Visible forms cognizable by the eye… touches cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire and enticing — these, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. Yet, monks, these are not sensual pleasures; in the discipline of the noble one they are called strands of sensual pleasure":
"A person's sensual pleasure is greedy intention;
the beautiful things in the world are not sensual pleasures;
a person's sensual pleasure is greedy intention;
the beautiful things stay just as they are in the world;
but the wise remove the desire for them" [A. Ni. 6.63, in the Nibbedhika Discourse]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the five sense bases alone are sensual pleasures."
