Since the body is material form, is bodily action material form? Yes. Since the eye base is material form, is eye-consciousness material form? That should not be said… Since the body is material form, is bodily action material form? Yes. Since the ear base is material form, is ear-consciousness material form? That should not be said… Since the body is material form, is bodily action material form? Yes. Since the nose base is material form, is nose-consciousness material form? That should not be said… Since the body is material form, is bodily action material form? Yes. Since the tongue base is material form, is tongue-consciousness material form? That should not be said… Since the body is material form, is bodily action material form? Yes. Since the body base is material form, is body-consciousness material form? That should not be said… ^5-538

Is material form action? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, I say that intention is action; having intended, one performs action by body, by speech and by mind" [A. Ni. 6.63, in the Nibbedhika Discourse]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "material form is action."
Is material form action? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Ānanda [variant: hānanda (S. Ni. 2.25)], when there is the body, internal pleasure and pain arise because of bodily intention; Ānanda [variant: hānanda (S. Ni. 2.25)], when there is speech, internal pleasure and pain arise because of verbal intention; Ānanda [variant: hānanda (S. Ni. 2.25)], when there is the mind, internal pleasure and pain arise because of mental intention" [S. Ni. 2.25; A. Ni. 4.171]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "material form is action."
Is material form action? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, threefold bodily intention is unwholesome bodily action, with suffering as its outcome and suffering as its result; monks, fourfold verbal intention is unwholesome verbal action, with suffering as its outcome and suffering as its result; monks, threefold mental intention is unwholesome mental action, with suffering as its outcome and suffering as its result; monks, threefold bodily intention is wholesome bodily action, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result; monks, fourfold verbal intention is wholesome verbal action, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result; monks, threefold mental intention is wholesome mental action, with happiness as its outcome and happiness as its result" [A. Ni. 10.217, but slightly different]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "material form is action."
Is material form action? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Ānanda, if the misguided man Samiddhi, when asked this by the wanderer Pāṭaliputta [variant: potaliputtassa (M. Ni. 3.300)], had answered thus: ‘Friend Pāṭaliputta, having done an intentional action by body, speech or mind that is to be felt as pleasant, one feels pleasure; friend Pāṭaliputta, having done an intentional action by body, speech or mind that is to be felt as painful, one feels pain; friend Pāṭaliputta, having done an intentional action by body, speech or mind that is to be felt as neither painful nor pleasant, one feels what is neither painful nor pleasant’ — answering thus, Ānanda, the misguided man Samiddhi would have answered the wanderer Pāṭaliputta rightly" [M. Ni. 3.300]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "material form is action."
The Discussion of "Material Form Is Action" is finished. ^5-539

#### The Eighth Chapter ^5-16-10-0

##### (82) 10. Discussion of the Life Faculty ^5-16-10-1-0

Is there no material life faculty? Yes. Is there no life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of material states? That should not be said… Is there life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of material states? Yes. If there is life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of material states, then surely you must not say: "There is no material life faculty."
There is life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of non-material states — is there a non-material life faculty? Yes. There is life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of material states — is there a material life faculty? That should not be said… There is life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of material states — is there no material life faculty? Yes. There is life, persistence, maintenance, sustenance, activity, continuance and protection of non-material states — is there no non-material life faculty? That should not be said…
Is the life of non-material states the non-material life faculty? Yes. Is the life of material states the material life faculty? That should not be said… Should the life of material states not be called "the material life faculty"? Yes. Should the life of non-material states not be called "the non-material life faculty"? That should not be said… ^5-540

Is the life of material states the non-material life faculty? Yes. Is the life of non-material states the material life faculty? That should not be said…
Should the life of non-material states not be called "the material life faculty"? Yes. Should the life of material states not be called "the non-material life faculty"? That should not be said…
Is the life of material and non-material states the non-material life faculty? Yes. Is the life of material and non-material states the material life faculty? That should not be said…
Should the life of material and non-material states not be called "the material life faculty"? Yes. Should the life of material and non-material states not be called "the non-material life faculty"? That should not be said… Is there no material life faculty? Yes. Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have no life faculty? That should not be said… ^5-541

Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have a life faculty? Yes. If one who has entered the attainment of cessation has a life faculty, then surely you must not say: "There is no material life faculty."
Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have a life faculty? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of mental formations. Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have the aggregate of mental formations? That should not be said…
Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have the aggregate of feeling… the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of consciousness? That should not be said…
Does one who has entered the attainment of cessation have the aggregate of feeling… the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of consciousness? Yes. Then has that one not entered the attainment of cessation? That should not be said… ^5-542

Is there no material life faculty? Yes. Do the beings without perception have no life faculty? That should not be said…
Do the beings without perception have a life faculty? Yes. If the beings without perception have a life faculty, then surely you must not say: "There is no material life faculty." Do the beings without perception have a life faculty? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of mental formations. Do the beings without perception have the aggregate of mental formations? That should not be said…
Do the beings without perception have the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Do the beings without perception have the aggregate of feeling… the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of consciousness? That should not be said…
Do the beings without perception have the aggregate of feeling… the aggregate of perception… the aggregate of consciousness? Yes. Is it a five-aggregate existence? That should not be said… ^5-543

When the rebirth-seeking mind breaks up, does the life faculty produced by the rebirth-seeking mind break up partly? Yes. When the rebirth-seeking mind breaks up, does contact produced by the rebirth-seeking mind break up partly? That should not be said…
When the rebirth-seeking mind breaks up, does contact produced by the rebirth-seeking mind break up without remainder? Yes. When the rebirth-seeking mind breaks up, does the life faculty produced by the rebirth-seeking mind break up without remainder? That should not be said… ^5-544

Are there two life faculties? Yes. Does one live with two lives and die with two deaths? Yes [variant: na hevaṃ vattabbe (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)].
The Discussion of the Life Faculty is finished. ^5-545

#### The Eighth Chapter ^5-16-11-0

##### (83) 11. Discussion of "Because of Action" ^5-16-11-1-0

Does a worthy one (arahant) fall away from arahantship (the state of a worthy one) because of action? Yes. Does a stream-enterer fall away from the fruit of stream-entry because of action? That should not be said… Does a worthy one fall away from arahantship because of action? Yes. Does a once-returner… a non-returner fall away from the fruit of non-returning because of action? That should not be said…
Does a stream-enterer not fall away from the fruit of stream-entry because of action? Yes. Does a worthy one not fall away from arahantship because of action? That should not be said… Does a once-returner… a non-returner not fall away from the fruit of non-returning because of action? Yes. Does a worthy one not fall away from arahantship because of action? That should not be said…
Does a worthy one fall away from arahantship because of action? Yes. Because of the action of killing living beings? That should not be said… Because of the action of taking what is not given… because of the action of sexual misconduct… because of the action of false speech… because of the action of divisive speech… because of the action of harsh speech… because of the action of idle chatter… because of the action of killing one's mother [variant: mātughātakakammassa (Syā.), mātughātikammassa (Ka.), and likewise in the words for killing one's father and killing a worthy one]… because of the action of killing one's father… because of the action of killing a worthy one… because of the action of shedding a Buddha's blood… because of the action of splitting the Community? That should not be said…
Because of which action? Well, because they slander worthy ones. Does a worthy one fall away from arahantship because of the action of slandering worthy ones? Yes. Do all those who slander worthy ones realize arahantship? That should not be said…
The Discussion of "Because of Action" is finished.
The Eighth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
Six destinations, intermediate existence, the five strands of sensual pleasure alone are the sense-desire realm, the five sense bases alone are sensual pleasures, material states are the realm of form, non-material states are the formless realm, an individual existence with six sense bases in the realm of form, there is material form in the formless realms, material form is action, material life, falling away because of action. ^5-546

### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-0

#### (84) 1. Discussion of Seeing the Benefit ^5-17-1-0

Is there abandoning of the fetters for one who sees the benefit? Yes. But aren't the fetters abandoned by one who attends to formations (conditioned things) as impermanent? Yes. If the fetters are abandoned by one who attends to formations as impermanent, then surely you must not say: "There is abandoning of the fetters for one who sees the benefit."
But aren't the fetters abandoned by one who attends to formations as painful… as a disease… as a boil… as a dart… as misery… as an affliction… as alien… as disintegrating… as a calamity… as a disaster… as a terror… as a menace… as unsteady… as perishable… as not lasting… as no protection… as no shelter… as no refuge… as having become no refuge… as vacant… as hollow… as empty… as not self… as dangerous… as subject to change? Yes. If the fetters are abandoned by one who attends to formations as subject to change, then surely you must not say: "There is abandoning of the fetters for one who sees the benefit."
Does one attend to formations as impermanent and also see the benefit in nibbāna (final release)? That should not be said… Does one attend to formations as impermanent and also see the benefit in nibbāna? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… Does one attend to formations as painful… as subject to change and also see the benefit in nibbāna? That should not be said… Does one attend to formations as subject to change and also see the benefit in nibbāna? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… ^5-547

Should it not be said that "there is abandoning of the fetters for one who sees the benefit"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating happiness in nibbāna, perceiving happiness, experiencing happiness, constantly, continuously and without interruption resolving on it with the mind and plunging into it with wisdom" [A. Ni. 7.19]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is abandoning of the fetters for one who sees the benefit.
The Discussion of Seeing the Benefit is finished. ^5-548

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-2-0

##### (85) 2. Discussion of the Deathless as Object ^5-17-2-1-0

Does a fetter have the deathless as its object? Yes. Is the deathless subject to the fetters, subject to the knots, subject to the floods, subject to the bonds, subject to the hindrances, seized upon, subject to clinging, subject to defilement? That should not be said… But isn't the deathless not subject to the fetters, not subject to the knots… not subject to defilement? Yes. If the deathless is not subject to the fetters… not subject to defilement, then surely you must not say: "A fetter has the deathless as its object."
Does greed arise with regard to the deathless? Yes. Is the deathless a basis for greed, enticing, desirable, intoxicating, binding, infatuating? That should not be said… But isn't the deathless not a basis for greed, not enticing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, not infatuating? Yes. If the deathless is not a basis for greed, not enticing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, not infatuating, then surely you must not say: "Greed arises with regard to the deathless."
Does hatred arise with regard to the deathless? Yes. Is the deathless a basis for hatred, a basis for anger, a basis for aversion? That should not be said… But isn't the deathless not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, not a basis for aversion? Yes. If the deathless is not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, not a basis for aversion, then surely you must not say: "Hatred arises with regard to the deathless."
Does delusion arise with regard to the deathless? Yes. Is the deathless a basis for delusion, something that causes lack of knowledge, causes blindness, brings wisdom to an end, sides with distress and does not lead to nibbāna? That should not be said… But isn't the deathless not a basis for delusion, something that does not cause lack of knowledge, does not cause blindness, that increases wisdom, does not side with distress and leads to nibbāna? Yes. If the deathless is not a basis for delusion, does not cause lack of knowledge… leads to nibbāna, then surely you must not say: "Delusion arises with regard to the deathless." ^5-549

Fetters arise with regard to material form — is material form subject to the fetters, subject to the knots… subject to defilement? Yes. Fetters arise with regard to the deathless — is the deathless subject to the fetters… subject to defilement? That should not be said…
Greed arises with regard to material form — is material form a basis for greed, enticing, desirable, intoxicating, binding, infatuating? Yes. Greed arises with regard to the deathless — is the deathless a basis for greed… infatuating? That should not be said…
Hatred arises with regard to material form — is material form a basis for hatred, a basis for anger, a basis for aversion? Yes. Hatred arises with regard to the deathless — is the deathless a basis for hatred, a basis for anger, a basis for aversion? That should not be said…
Delusion arises with regard to material form — is material form a basis for delusion, something that causes lack of knowledge… does not lead to nibbāna? Yes. Delusion arises with regard to the deathless — is the deathless a basis for delusion, something that causes lack of knowledge… does not lead to nibbāna? That should not be said…
Fetters arise with regard to the deathless — is the deathless not subject to the fetters, not subject to the knots, not subject to the floods, not subject to the bonds, not subject to the hindrances, not seized upon, not subject to clinging, not subject to defilement? Yes. Fetters arise with regard to material form — is material form not subject to the fetters, not subject to the knots… not subject to defilement? That should not be said…
Greed arises with regard to the deathless — is the deathless not a basis for greed, not enticing, not desirable, not intoxicating, not binding, not infatuating? Yes. Greed arises with regard to material form — is material form not a basis for greed… not infatuating? That should not be said…
Hatred arises with regard to the deathless — is the deathless not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, not a basis for aversion? Yes. Hatred arises with regard to material form — is material form not a basis for hatred, not a basis for anger, not a basis for aversion? That should not be said…
Delusion arises with regard to the deathless — is the deathless not a basis for delusion, something that does not cause lack of knowledge… leads to nibbāna? Yes. Delusion arises with regard to material form — is material form not a basis for delusion, something that does not cause lack of knowledge… leads to nibbāna? That should not be said… ^5-550

Should it not be said that "a fetter has the deathless as its object"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "They perceive nibbāna as nibbāna; having perceived nibbāna as nibbāna, they conceive nibbāna, they conceive in nibbāna, they conceive from nibbāna, they conceive ‘nibbāna is mine’, they delight in nibbāna" [M. Ni. 1.6]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case a fetter has the deathless as its object.
The Discussion of the Deathless as Object is finished. ^5-551

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-3-0

##### (86) 3. Discussion of "Material Form Has an Object" ^5-17-3-1-0

Does material form have an object? Yes. Does it have turning of the mind, concern, bringing to mind, attention, intention, wish and aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it has no turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? Yes. If it has no turning of the mind, concern… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "Material form has an object."
Contact has an object — does it have turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? Yes. Material form has an object — does it have turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? That should not be said…
Feeling… perception, intention, mind, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom, greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, sluggishness, restlessness, shamelessness… lack of moral fear has an object — does it have turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? Yes. Material form has an object — does it have turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? That should not be said…
Material form has an object — does it have no turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? Yes. Contact has an object — does it have no turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? That should not be said…
Material form has an object — does it have no turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? Yes. Feeling… lack of moral fear has an object — does it have no turning of the mind, concern… aspiration? That should not be said… ^5-552

Should it not be said that "material form has an object"? Yes. But isn't material form dependent on conditions? Yes. If material form is dependent on conditions, then surely you must also say: "Material form has an object."
The Discussion of "Material Form Has an Object" is finished. ^5-553

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-4-0

##### (87) 4. Discussion of "The Underlying Tendencies Are Without an Object" ^5-17-4-1-0

Are the underlying tendencies without an object? Yes. Are they material form, nibbāna (final release), the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed without an object? Yes. Are sensual greed, obsession by sensual greed, the fetter of sensual greed, the flood of sensuality, the bond of sensuality and the hindrance of sensual desire without an object? That should not be said… Do sensual greed, obsession by sensual greed, the fetter of sensual greed, the flood of sensuality, the bond of sensuality and the hindrance of sensual desire have an object? Yes. Does the underlying tendency to sensual greed have an object? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed without an object? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of mental formations. Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object? That should not be said… Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of consciousness without an object? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object? Yes. Is sensual greed, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object? That should not be said… Does sensual greed, included in the aggregate of mental formations, have an object? Yes. Does the underlying tendency to sensual greed, included in the aggregate of mental formations, have an object? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object, while sensual greed, included in the aggregate of mental formations, has an object? Yes. Is the aggregate of mental formations partly with an object and partly without an object? That should not be said… Is the aggregate of mental formations partly with an object and partly without an object? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of consciousness partly with an object and partly without an object? That should not be said… ^5-554

Are the underlying tendency to aversion, the underlying tendency to conceit, the underlying tendency to views, the underlying tendency to doubt, the underlying tendency to greed for existence and the underlying tendency to ignorance without an object? Yes. Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the bond of ignorance, the underlying tendency to ignorance, obsession by ignorance, the fetter of ignorance and the hindrance of ignorance without an object? That should not be said… Do ignorance, the flood of ignorance… the hindrance of ignorance have an object? Yes. Does the underlying tendency to ignorance have an object? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to ignorance without an object? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of mental formations. Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object? That should not be said… Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of consciousness without an object? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to ignorance, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object? Yes. Is ignorance, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object? That should not be said… Does ignorance, included in the aggregate of mental formations, have an object? Yes. Does the underlying tendency to ignorance, included in the aggregate of mental formations, have an object? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to ignorance, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object, while ignorance, included in the aggregate of mental formations, has an object? Yes. Is the aggregate of mental formations partly with an object and partly without an object? That should not be said… Is the aggregate of mental formations partly with an object and partly without an object? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of consciousness partly with an object and partly without an object? That should not be said… ^5-555

Should it not be said that "the underlying tendencies are without an object"? Yes. When a wholesome or indeterminate mind is occurring in an ordinary person, should that person be called "one with underlying tendencies"? Yes. Do those underlying tendencies have an object? That should not be said… In that case the underlying tendencies are without an object. When a wholesome or indeterminate mind is occurring in an ordinary person, should that person be called "one who has greed"? Yes. Does that greed have an object? That should not be said… In that case greed is without an object.
The Discussion of "The Underlying Tendencies Are Without an Object" is finished. ^5-556

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-5-0

##### (88) 5. Discussion of "Knowledge Is Without an Object" ^5-17-5-1-0

Is knowledge without an object? Yes. Is it material form, nibbāna (final release), the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said… Is knowledge without an object? Yes. Are wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, right view and the investigation-of-states factor of awakening without an object? That should not be said… Do wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, right view and the investigation-of-states factor of awakening have an object? Yes. Does knowledge have an object? That should not be said…
Is knowledge without an object? Yes. In which aggregate is it included? It is included in the aggregate of mental formations. Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object? That should not be said… Is the aggregate of mental formations without an object? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of consciousness without an object? That should not be said… Is knowledge, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object? Yes. Is wisdom, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object? That should not be said… Does wisdom, included in the aggregate of mental formations, have an object? Yes. Does knowledge, included in the aggregate of mental formations, have an object? That should not be said…
Is knowledge, included in the aggregate of mental formations, without an object, while wisdom, included in the aggregate of mental formations, has an object? Yes. Is the aggregate of mental formations partly with an object and partly without an object? That should not be said… Is the aggregate of mental formations partly with an object and partly without an object? Yes. Are the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception and the aggregate of consciousness partly with an object and partly without an object? That should not be said… ^5-557

Should it not be said that "knowledge is without an object"? Yes. Should a worthy one (arahant) possessing eye-consciousness be called "one who has knowledge"? Yes. Does that knowledge have an object? That should not be said… In that case knowledge is without an object. Should a worthy one possessing eye-consciousness be called "one who has wisdom"? Yes. Does that wisdom have an object? That should not be said… In that case wisdom is without an object.
The Discussion of "Knowledge Is Without an Object" is finished. ^5-558

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-6-0

##### (89) 6. Discussion of Past and Future Objects ^5-17-6-1-0

Is a mind that has a past object without an object? Yes. But doesn't it have a past object? Yes. If it has a past object, then surely you must not say: "A mind that has a past object is without an object." "A mind that has a past object is without an object" — that is wrong. Or else, if it is without an object, then surely you must not say: "It has a past object." "It is without an object and has a past object" — that is wrong.
Is a mind that has a past object without an object? Yes. But isn't there turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the past? Yes. If there is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the past, then surely you must not say: "A mind that has a past object is without an object." ^5-559

Is a mind that has a future object without an object? Yes. But doesn't it have a future object? Yes. If it has a future object, then surely you must not say: "A mind that has a future object is without an object." "A mind that has a future object is without an object" — that is wrong. Or else, if it is without an object, then surely you must not say: "It has a future object." "It is without an object and has a future object" — that is wrong.
Is a mind that has a future object without an object? Yes. But isn't there turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the future? Yes. If there is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the future, then surely you must not say: "A mind that has a future object is without an object."
There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the present — does a mind that has a present object have an object? Yes. There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the past — does a mind that has a past object have an object? That should not be said… There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the present — does a mind that has a present object have an object? Yes. There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the future — does a mind that has a future object have an object? That should not be said…
There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the past — is a mind that has a past object without an object? Yes. There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the present — is a mind that has a present object without an object? That should not be said…
There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the future — is a mind that has a future object without an object? Yes. There is turning of the mind… aspiration with regard to the present — is a mind that has a present object without an object? That should not be said… ^5-560

Should it not be said that "a mind that has a past or future object is without an object"? Yes. But isn't it the case that the past and the future do not exist? Yes. If the past and the future do not exist, then surely you must also say: "A mind that has a past or future object is without an object."…
The Discussion of Past and Future Objects is finished. ^5-561

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-7-0

##### (90) 7. Discussion of "Accompanied by Thinking" ^5-17-7-1-0

Is every mind accompanied by thinking? Yes. Is every mind accompanied by examining, accompanied by joy, accompanied by pleasure, accompanied by pain, accompanied by gladness, accompanied by sadness, accompanied by equanimity, accompanied by faith, accompanied by energy, accompanied by mindfulness, accompanied by concentration, accompanied by wisdom, accompanied by greed, accompanied by hatred… accompanied by lack of moral fear? That should not be said…
Is every mind accompanied by thinking? Yes. But isn't there concentration without thinking, with examining only? Yes. If there is concentration without thinking, with examining only, then surely you must not say: "Every mind is accompanied by thinking."
Is every mind accompanied by thinking? Yes. But isn't there concentration without thinking and without examining? Yes. If there is concentration without thinking and without examining, then surely you must not say: "Every mind is accompanied by thinking." Is every mind accompanied by thinking? Yes. But didn't the Blessed One speak of three kinds of concentration — concentration with thinking and examining, concentration without thinking, with examining only, and concentration without thinking and without examining [D. Ni. 3.305, 353]? Yes. If the Blessed One spoke of three kinds of concentration — concentration with thinking and examining, concentration without thinking, with examining only, and concentration without thinking and without examining — then surely you must not say: "Every mind is accompanied by thinking."
The Discussion of "Accompanied by Thinking" is finished. ^5-562

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-8-0

##### (91) 8. Discussion of the Sound of the Outflow of Thinking ^5-17-8-1-0

For one who is thinking and examining, is the outflow of thinking sound in every case? Yes. For one who is contacting, is the outflow of contact sound in every case; for one who is feeling, is the outflow of feeling sound in every case; for one who is perceiving, is the outflow of perception sound in every case; for one who is intending, is the outflow of intention sound in every case; for one who is thinking things over, is the outflow of mind sound in every case; for one who is remembering, is the outflow of mindfulness sound in every case; for one who is understanding, is the outflow of wisdom sound in every case? That should not be said…
For one who is thinking and examining, is the outflow of thinking sound in every case? Yes. Is the sound that is the outflow of thinking cognizable by the ear; does it strike the ear, does it come within range of the ear? That should not be said… But isn't the sound that is the outflow of thinking not cognizable by the ear; does it not strike the ear, does it not come within range of the ear? Yes. If the sound that is the outflow of thinking is not cognizable by the ear, does not strike the ear and does not come within range of the ear, then surely you must not say: "For one who is thinking and examining, the outflow of thinking is sound in every case."
The Discussion of the Sound of the Outflow of Thinking is finished. ^5-563

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-9-0

##### (92) 9. Discussion of "Speech Is Not in Accordance with the Mind" ^5-17-9-1-0

Is speech not in accordance with the mind? Yes. Is there speech for one without contact, speech for one without feeling, speech for one without perception, speech for one without intention, speech for one without mind? That should not be said… But isn't there speech for one with contact, speech for one with feeling, speech for one with perception, speech for one with intention, speech for one with mind? Yes. If there is speech for one with contact… speech for one with mind, then surely you must not say: "Speech is not in accordance with the mind."
Is speech not in accordance with the mind? Yes. Is there speech for one who does not turn the mind to it [variant: anāvaṭṭantassa (Pī.), anāvajjantassa (Sī., Syā., Ka.); see Kathā. 484]… speech for one without concern… speech for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But isn't there speech for one who turns the mind to it, speech for one with concern… speech for one who aspires? Yes. If there is speech for one who turns the mind to it, speech for one with concern, speech for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "Speech is not in accordance with the mind."
Is speech not in accordance with the mind? Yes. But isn't speech produced by the mind, arisen together with the mind and having the same arising as the mind? Yes. If speech is produced by the mind, arisen together with the mind and has the same arising as the mind, then surely you must not say: "Speech is not in accordance with the mind."
Is speech not in accordance with the mind? Yes. Does one speak without wishing to speak, talk without wishing to talk, address others without wishing to address them, converse without wishing to converse? That should not be said… But doesn't one speak when wishing to speak, talk when wishing to talk, address others when wishing to address them, converse when wishing to converse? Yes. If one speaks when wishing to speak, talks when wishing to talk, addresses others when wishing to address them, converses when wishing to converse, then surely you must not say: "Speech is not in accordance with the mind." ^5-564

Should it not be said that "speech is not in accordance with the mind"? Yes. But isn't there someone who, thinking "I will say one thing", says another; thinking "I will talk about one thing", talks about another; thinking "I will address one thing", addresses another; thinking "I will converse about one thing", converses about another? Yes. If there is someone who, thinking "I will say one thing", says another… thinking "I will converse about one thing", converses about another, then surely you must also say: "Speech is not in accordance with the mind."
The Discussion of "Speech Is Not in Accordance with the Mind" is finished. ^5-565

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-10-0

##### (93) 10. Discussion of "Bodily Action Is Not in Accordance with the Mind" ^5-17-10-1-0

Is bodily action not in accordance with the mind? Yes. Is there bodily action for one without contact… bodily action for one without mind? That should not be said… But isn't there bodily action for one with contact… bodily action for one with mind? Yes. If there is bodily action for one with contact… bodily action for one with mind, then surely you must not say: "Bodily action is not in accordance with the mind."
Is bodily action not in accordance with the mind? Yes. Is there bodily action for one who does not turn the mind to it… bodily action for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But isn't there bodily action for one who turns the mind to it… bodily action for one who aspires? Yes. If there is bodily action for one who turns the mind to it… bodily action for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "Bodily action is not in accordance with the mind."
Is bodily action not in accordance with the mind? Yes. But isn't bodily action produced by the mind, arisen together with the mind and having the same arising as the mind? Yes. If bodily action is produced by the mind, arisen together with the mind and has the same arising as the mind, then surely you must not say: "Bodily action is not in accordance with the mind."
Is bodily action not in accordance with the mind? Yes. Does one go forward without wishing to go forward, go back without wishing to go back, look ahead without wishing to look ahead, look around without wishing to look around, bend a limb without wishing to bend it, stretch a limb without wishing to stretch it? That should not be said… But doesn't one go forward when wishing to go forward, go back when wishing to go back, look ahead when wishing to look ahead, look around when wishing to look around, bend a limb when wishing to bend it, stretch a limb when wishing to stretch it? Yes. If one goes forward when wishing to go forward… stretches a limb when wishing to stretch it, then surely you must not say: "Bodily action is not in accordance with the mind." ^5-566

Should it not be said that "bodily action is not in accordance with the mind"? Yes. But isn't there someone who, thinking "I will go to one place", goes to another… thinking "I will stretch one limb", stretches another? Yes. If there is someone who, thinking "I will go to one place", goes to another… thinking "I will stretch one limb", stretches another, then surely you must also say: "Bodily action is not in accordance with the mind."
The Discussion of "Bodily Action Is Not in Accordance with the Mind" is finished. ^5-567

#### The Ninth Chapter ^5-17-11-0

##### (94) 11. Discussion of Being Endowed with the Past and the Future ^5-17-11-1-0

Is one endowed with the past? Yes. But hasn't the past ceased, gone, changed, vanished, completely vanished? Yes. If the past has ceased, gone, changed, vanished, completely vanished, then surely you must not say: "One is endowed with the past."
Is one endowed with the future? Yes. But isn't the future unborn, not come to be, not arisen, not produced, not fully produced, not manifested? Yes. If the future is unborn, not come to be, not arisen, not produced, not fully produced, not manifested, then surely you must not say: "One is endowed with the future." ^5-568

Is one endowed with the past aggregate of material form, endowed with the future aggregate of material form, endowed with the present aggregate of material form? Yes. Is one endowed with three aggregates of material form? That should not be said… Is one endowed with the five past aggregates, endowed with the five future aggregates, endowed with the five present aggregates? Yes. Is one endowed with fifteen aggregates? That should not be said…
Is one endowed with the past eye base, endowed with the future eye base, endowed with the present eye base? Yes. Is one endowed with three eye bases? That should not be said… Is one endowed with the twelve past sense bases, endowed with the twelve future sense bases, endowed with the twelve present sense bases? Yes. Is one endowed with thirty-six sense bases? That should not be said…
Is one endowed with the past eye element, endowed with the future eye element, endowed with the present eye element? Yes. Is one endowed with three eye elements? That should not be said… Is one endowed with the eighteen past elements, endowed with the eighteen future elements, endowed with the eighteen present elements? Yes. Is one endowed with fifty-four elements? That should not be said…
Is one endowed with the past eye faculty, endowed with the future eye faculty, endowed with the present eye faculty? Yes. Is one endowed with three eye faculties? That should not be said… Is one endowed with the twenty-two past faculties, endowed with the twenty-two future faculties, endowed with the twenty-two present faculties? Yes. Is one endowed with sixty-six faculties? That should not be said… ^5-569

Should it not be said that "one is endowed with the past and the future"? Yes. But isn't there one who meditates on the eight liberations, who obtains the four meditative absorptions (jhāna) at will, who obtains the nine attainments of the successive abodes? Yes. If there is one who meditates on the eight liberations, who obtains the four meditative absorptions at will, who obtains the nine attainments of the successive abodes, then surely you must also say: "One is endowed with the past and the future."
The Discussion of Being Endowed with the Past and the Future is finished.
The Ninth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The abandoning of the fetters for one who sees the benefit, a fetter has the deathless as its object, material form has an object, the underlying tendencies are without an object, likewise knowledge, a mind with a past or future object, every mind is accompanied by thinking, for one who is thinking and examining the outflow of thinking is sound in every case, speech is not in accordance with the mind, likewise bodily action, endowed with the past and the future. ^5-570

### The Tenth Chapter ^5-18-0

#### (95) 1. Discussion of Cessation ^5-18-1-0

While the five rebirth-seeking aggregates have not yet ceased, do five functional aggregates arise? Yes. Is there a coming together of ten aggregates; do ten aggregates come face to face? That should not be said… Is there a coming together of ten aggregates; do ten aggregates come face to face? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said…
While the five rebirth-seeking aggregates have not yet ceased, do four functional aggregates arise? Yes. Is there a coming together of nine aggregates; do nine aggregates come face to face? That should not be said… Is there a coming together of nine aggregates; do nine aggregates come face to face? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said…
While the five rebirth-seeking aggregates have not yet ceased, does functional knowledge arise? Yes. Is there a coming together of six aggregates; do six aggregates come face to face? That should not be said… Is there a coming together of six aggregates; do six aggregates come face to face? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… ^5-571

When the five rebirth-seeking aggregates have ceased, does the path arise? Yes. Does one who has died develop the path; does one who has passed away develop the path? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Cessation is finished. ^5-572

#### The Tenth Chapter ^5-18-2-0

##### (96) 2. Discussion of "Material Form Is the Path" ^5-18-2-1-0

Is the material form of one possessing the path the path? Yes. Does it have an object, and does it have turning of the mind, concern, bringing to mind, attention, intention, wish and aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it is without an object and has no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. If it is without an object and has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "The material form of one possessing the path is the path."
Is right speech the path? Yes. Does it have an object, and does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it is without an object and has no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. If it is without an object and has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "Right speech is the path."
Is right action… right livelihood the path? Yes. Does it have an object, and does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it is without an object and has no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. If it is without an object and has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "Right livelihood is the path." ^5-573

Right view is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right speech is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… Right view is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right action… right livelihood is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… Right intention… right effort… right mindfulness…
Right concentration is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right speech is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… Right concentration is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right action… right livelihood is the path and has an object — does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said…
Right speech is the path and is without an object — does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right view is the path and is without an object — does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… Right speech is the path and is without an object — does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… right concentration is the path and is without an object — does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said…
Right action… right livelihood is the path and is without an object — does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Right view… right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… right concentration is the path and is without an object — does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… ^5-574

Should it not be said that "the material form of one possessing the path is the path"? Yes. But aren't right speech, right action and right livelihood the path? Yes. If right speech, right action and right livelihood are the path, then surely you must also say: "The material form of one possessing the path is the path."
The Discussion of "Material Form Is the Path" is finished. ^5-575

#### The Tenth Chapter ^5-18-3-0

##### (97) 3. Discussion of the Path for One Possessing the Five Kinds of Consciousness ^5-18-3-1-0

Is there development of the path for one possessing the five kinds of consciousness? Yes. But don't the five kinds of consciousness have a base that has already arisen and an object that has already arisen? Yes. If the five kinds of consciousness have a base that has already arisen and an object that has already arisen, then surely you must not say: "There is development of the path for one possessing the five kinds of consciousness."
But isn't it the case that the five kinds of consciousness have a base that arose before them and an object that arose before them, an internal base and an external object, a base that is intact and an object that is intact, different bases and different objects; that they do not experience one another's range and domain; that they do not arise without bringing to mind, do not arise without attention, do not arise in uninterrupted succession, do not arise at one and the same time, neither before nor after, do not arise immediately after one another — aren't the five kinds of consciousness without concern? Yes. If the five kinds of consciousness are without concern, then surely you must not say: "There is development of the path for one possessing the five kinds of consciousness." ^5-576

Is there development of the path for one possessing eye-consciousness? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise with regard to emptiness? That should not be said… Does eye-consciousness arise with regard to emptiness? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on emptiness? That should not be said… Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on emptiness? Yes. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on emptiness" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms," then surely you must not say: "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on emptiness." ^5-577

Is there development of the path for one possessing eye-consciousness? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise with regard to the past and the future? That should not be said… Is there development of the path for one possessing eye-consciousness? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise with regard to contact… with regard to feeling… with regard to perception… with regard to intention… with regard to the mind… with regard to the eye… with regard to the body… with regard to sound… with regard to touch? That should not be said…
There is development of the path for one possessing mind-consciousness — does mind-consciousness arise with regard to emptiness? Yes. There is development of the path for one possessing eye-consciousness — does eye-consciousness arise with regard to emptiness? That should not be said… There is development of the path for one possessing mind-consciousness — does mind-consciousness arise with regard to the past and the future? Yes. There is development of the path for one possessing eye-consciousness — does eye-consciousness arise with regard to the past and the future? That should not be said… There is development of the path for one possessing mind-consciousness — does mind-consciousness arise with regard to contact… with regard to feeling… with regard to touch? Yes. There is development of the path for one possessing eye-consciousness — does eye-consciousness arise with regard to contact… with regard to feeling… with regard to touch? That should not be said… ^5-578

Should it not be said that "there is development of the path for one possessing the five kinds of consciousness"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, monks, a monk, having seen a visible form with the eye, does not grasp at its signs or its features… having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled a smell with the nose… having tasted a taste with the tongue… having touched a touch with the body, does not grasp at its signs or its features" [M. Ni. 1.349; A. Ni. 4.37]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is development of the path for one possessing the five kinds of consciousness.
The Discussion of the Path for One Possessing the Five Kinds of Consciousness is finished. ^5-579

Mind-consciousness is wholesome as well as unwholesome — does mind-consciousness arise with regard to emptiness? Yes. That should not be said… Mind-consciousness is with concern — does mind-consciousness arise with regard to the past and the future? Yes. #### The Tenth Chapter ^5-18-6-0

Is one possessing the path endowed with two kinds of virtue? Yes. Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly and world-transcending contact… endowed with worldly and world-transcending wisdom? That should not be said… Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly virtue? Yes. Is one possessing the path an ordinary person? That should not be said… ^5-587

Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly right speech? Yes. Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly right view? That should not be said… Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly right speech? Yes. Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly right intention… worldly right effort… worldly right mindfulness… worldly right concentration? That should not be said… Is one possessing the path endowed with worldly right action… worldly right livelihood? Yes. Is virtue not a mental factor (a state belonging to the mind)? Yes. Is it material form… nibbāna (final release)… the eye base… the body base… the visible-form base… the touch base? Is feeling… perception… intention… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom not a mental factor? That should not be said…
Is contact a mental factor? Yes. Is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said… Is feeling… perception… intention… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom a mental factor? Yes. Is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said… ^5-590

That should not be said… Energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom has a desirable fruit — is wisdom a mental factor? Yes. Virtue has a desirable fruit — is virtue a mental factor? That should not be said…

Is right view a mental factor? Yes. Is right speech a mental factor? That should not be said… Is right view a mental factor? Yes. Is right action… right livelihood a mental factor? That should not be said… Is right concentration a mental factor? Yes. Is right action… right livelihood a mental factor? That should not be said… ^5-593

#### The Tenth Chapter ^5-18-9-0

##### (103) 9. Discussion of Virtue Due to Undertaking ^5-18-9-1-0

Does virtue that is due to undertaking grow? Yes. Does contact that is due to undertaking grow, does feeling grow, does perception grow, does intention grow, does the mind grow, does faith grow, does energy grow, does mindfulness grow, does concentration grow, does wisdom grow? That should not be said…
Does virtue that is due to undertaking grow? Yes. Does it grow like a creeper, grow like a vine, grow like a tree, grow like grass, grow like a clump of reeds? That should not be said… ^5-598

Does virtue that is due to undertaking grow? Yes. When one has undertaken virtue and thinks thoughts of sensual desire, thinks thoughts of ill will, thinks thoughts of harming, does virtue grow? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said…
Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? The sky, monks, and the earth — this is the first thing that is very far apart… therefore the Dhamma of the good is far from the bad"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face." ^5-599

##### (104) 10. Discussion of "Expression Is Virtue" ^5-18-10-1-0

Is expression (through body or speech) virtue? Yes. Is it abstention from killing living beings? That should not be said… Is it abstention from taking what is not given? That should not be said… Is it abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness? That should not be said…
Is paying respect virtue, rising to greet someone virtue, raising the joined palms virtue, courteous conduct virtue, offering a seat virtue, offering a bed virtue, offering water for the feet virtue, offering a foot-scraper virtue, rubbing someone's back when bathing virtue? Yes. Is it abstention from killing living beings? That should not be said… Is it abstention from liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness? That should not be said… ^5-601

Should it not be said that "expression is virtue"? Yes. Is it lack of virtue? That should not be said… In that case expression is virtue.
The Discussion of "Expression Is Virtue" is finished. ^5-602

Is non-expression lack of virtue? Yes. Is it killing living beings? That should not be said… Is it taking what is not given? That should not be said… Is it sexual misconduct? That should not be said… Is it false speech? That should not be said… Is it liquor, wine and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness? That should not be said…
When one has undertaken an evil action and gives a gift, do both merit and demerit grow? That should not be said… Do both merit and demerit grow? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said…
Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face." ^5-603

Should it not be said that "non-expression is lack of virtue"? Yes. But wasn't that one someone who had undertaken an evil action? Yes. If that one had undertaken an evil action, then surely you must also say: "Non-expression is lack of virtue."

The Tenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
While the five rebirth-seeking aggregates have not yet ceased, five functional aggregates arise; the material form of one possessing the path is the path; there is development of the path for one possessing the five kinds of consciousness; the five kinds of consciousness are wholesome as well as unwholesome; the five kinds of consciousness are with concern; one possessing the path is endowed with two kinds of virtue; virtue is not a mental factor; virtue does not move along with the mind; virtue due to undertaking grows; expression is virtue; non-expression is lack of virtue.
The Second Set of Fifty.
Here is its summary:
The fixed course, inclusion, destinations, seeing the benefit, and cessation [variant: niyāma saṅgahagatānisaṃsatā atthi pañcavokārabhavo nirodho maggasamaṅgissa pañcavokārabhavoti (Sī., Syā., Ka.), niyāma saṅgaha gatānisaṃsatā atthi pañcavokārabhavo maggasamaṅgissa no pañcavokārabhavo (Pī.)]. ^5-604

### The Eleventh Chapter ^5-19-0

#### (106-108) 1-3. The Three Discussions of the Underlying Tendencies ^5-19-1-0

Are the underlying tendencies indeterminate? Yes. Are they results that are indeterminate, functional states that are indeterminate, material form, nibbāna (final release), the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed indeterminate? Yes. Are sensual greed, obsession by sensual greed, the fetter of sensual greed, the flood of sensuality, the bond of sensuality and the hindrance of sensual desire indeterminate? That should not be said… Are sensual greed, obsession by sensual greed… the hindrance of sensual desire unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to aversion indeterminate? Yes. Are aversion, obsession by aversion and the fetter of aversion indeterminate? That should not be said… Are aversion, obsession by aversion and the fetter of aversion unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to aversion unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to conceit indeterminate? Yes. Are conceit, obsession by conceit and the fetter of conceit indeterminate? That should not be said… Are conceit, obsession by conceit and the fetter of conceit unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to conceit unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to views indeterminate? Yes. Are wrong view, the flood of views, the bond of views, obsession by views and the fetter of views indeterminate? That should not be said… Are wrong view, the flood of views, the bond of views, obsession by views and the fetter of views unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to views unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to doubt indeterminate? Yes. Are doubt, obsession by doubt, the fetter of doubt and the hindrance of doubt indeterminate? That should not be said… Are doubt, obsession by doubt, the fetter of doubt and the hindrance of doubt unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to doubt unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to greed for existence indeterminate? Yes. Are greed for existence, obsession by greed for existence and the fetter of greed for existence indeterminate? That should not be said… Are greed for existence, obsession by greed for existence and the fetter of greed for existence unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to greed for existence unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to ignorance indeterminate? Yes. Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the bond of ignorance, obsession by ignorance, the fetter of ignorance and the hindrance of ignorance indeterminate? That should not be said… Are ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the bond of ignorance, obsession by ignorance, the fetter of ignorance and the hindrance of ignorance unwholesome? Yes. Is the underlying tendency to ignorance unwholesome? That should not be said… ^5-605

Should it not be said that "the underlying tendencies are indeterminate"? Yes. When a wholesome or indeterminate mind is occurring in an ordinary person, should that person be called "one with underlying tendencies"? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states come face to face? That should not be said… In that case the underlying tendencies are indeterminate. When a wholesome or indeterminate mind is occurring in an ordinary person, should that person be called "one who has greed"? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome states come face to face? That should not be said… In that case greed is indeterminate. ^5-606

Are the underlying tendencies without roots (root causes)? Yes. Are they material form, nibbāna, the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed without roots? Yes. Are sensual greed, obsession by sensual greed, the fetter of sensual greed and the hindrance of sensual desire without roots? ##### (112) 7. Discussion of the Strength of Psychic Power ^5-19-5-1-0

Could one endowed with the strength of psychic power live on for an aeon (world-age)? Yes. Is that life span made by psychic power, that destination made by psychic power, that acquisition of individual existence made by psychic power? That should not be said…

The Eleventh Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The underlying tendencies are indeterminate, without roots, dissociated from the mind; when lack of knowledge has gone, one has knowledge; knowledge is dissociated from the mind; knowledge occurs in the sound [variant: yattha saddo (Sī.), yathāsaddaṃ (?)]; one endowed with the strength of psychic power could live on for an aeon; the continuity of mind is concentration; the stability of things; impermanence. ^5-629

The ear base… the nose base… the tongue base… is the body base a result? Yes. Is it to be felt as pleasant… does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it is not to be felt as pleasant… that it is without an object, and that it has no turning of the mind… or aspiration? Yes. If it is not to be felt as pleasant… without an object, and has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "The body base is a result."
Contact is a result — is contact to be felt as pleasant… does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. The body base is a result — is the body base to be felt as pleasant… does it have an object; does it have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… The body base is a result — is the body base not to be felt as pleasant… without an object; does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. Contact is a result — is contact not to be felt as pleasant… without an object; does it have no turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… ^5-639

Should it not be said that "the six sense bases are a result"? Yes. But haven't the six sense bases arisen because action was done? Yes. If the six sense bases have arisen because action was done, then surely you must also say: "The six sense bases are a result."
The Discussion of the Six Sense Bases is finished. ^5-640

#### The Twelfth Chapter ^5-20-5-0

##### (120) 5. Discussion of the One Who Has at Most Seven More Lives ^5-20-5-1-0

Is a person who has at most seven more lives fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. Have they deprived their mother of life… deprived their father of life… deprived a worthy one (arahant) of life… with a corrupt mind shed the blood of the Tathāgata (the Buddha)… split the Community? That should not be said…
Is a person who has at most seven more lives fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. Are they incapable of breaking through to the Dhamma in the meantime? That should not be said… Are they incapable of breaking through to the Dhamma in the meantime? Yes. Have they deprived their mother of life… deprived their father of life… deprived a worthy one of life… with a corrupt mind shed the blood of the Tathāgata… split the Community? That should not be said… ^5-641

Is a person who has at most seven more lives fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. Is there a fixed course by which a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives? That should not be said… Are there foundations of mindfulness… right strivings… bases of psychic power… faculties… powers… factors of awakening by which a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives? That should not be said… ^5-642

Is there no fixed course by which a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. If there is no fixed course by which a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives, then surely you must not say: "A person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives."
Are there no foundations of mindfulness… factors of awakening by which a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. If there are no factors of awakening by which a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives, then surely you must not say: "A person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives." ^5-643

Is a person who has at most seven more lives fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. By the fixed course of once-returning? That should not be said… By the fixed course of non-returning? That should not be said… By the fixed course of arahantship (the state of a worthy one)? That should not be said…
By which fixed course? By the fixed course of stream-entry. Is a person who has at most seven more lives fixed in having at most seven more lives? Yes. Are all those who enter the fixed course of stream-entry fixed in having at most seven more lives? That should not be said… ^5-644

Should it not be said that "a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives"? Yes. But isn't that person one who has at most seven more lives? Yes. If that person is one who has at most seven more lives, then surely you must also say: "A person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives."
The Discussion of the One Who Has at Most Seven More Lives is finished. ^5-645

#### The Twelfth Chapter ^5-20-6-0

##### (121) 6. Discussion of the One Who Goes from Family to Family ^5-20-6-1-0

Should it not be said that "a person who goes from family to family is fixed in going from family to family"? Yes. But isn't that person one who goes from family to family? Yes. If that person is one who goes from family to family, then surely you must also say: "A person who goes from family to family is fixed in going from family to family."
The Discussion of the One Who Goes from Family to Family is finished. ^5-646

#### The Twelfth Chapter ^5-20-7-0

##### (122) 7. Discussion of the One with a Single Seed ^5-20-7-1-0

Should it not be said that "a person with a single seed is fixed in having a single seed"? Yes. But isn't that person one with a single seed? Yes. If that person is one with a single seed, then surely you must also say: "A person with a single seed is fixed in having a single seed."
The Discussion of the One with a Single Seed is finished. ^5-647

#### The Twelfth Chapter ^5-20-8-0

##### (123) 8. Discussion of Depriving of Life ^5-20-8-1-0

Would a person accomplished in right view intentionally deprive a living being of life? Yes. Would a person accomplished in right view intentionally deprive their mother of life… deprive their father of life… deprive a worthy one (arahant) of life… with a corrupt mind shed the blood of the Tathāgata (the Buddha)… split the Community? That should not be said…
Would a person accomplished in right view intentionally deprive a living being of life? Yes. Is a person accomplished in right view without respect for the Teacher? That should not be said… for the Dhamma… for the Community… without respect for the training? That should not be said…
But isn't a person accomplished in right view respectful toward the Teacher? Yes. If a person accomplished in right view is respectful toward the Teacher, then surely you must not say: "A person accomplished in right view would intentionally deprive a living being of life." But isn't a person accomplished in right view respectful toward the Dhamma… the Community… the training? Yes. If a person accomplished in right view is respectful toward the training, then surely you must not say: "A person accomplished in right view would intentionally deprive a living being of life." ^5-648

Is a person accomplished in right view without respect for the Teacher? Yes. Would a person accomplished in right view defecate on a shrine of the Buddha, urinate on it, spit on it, or pass a shrine of the Buddha disrespectfully, keeping it on their left [variant: asabyākato (Sī., Ka.)]? That should not be said…
Would a person accomplished in right view intentionally deprive a living being of life? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Just as, monks, the great ocean, being of a stable nature, does not go beyond its shore, so too, monks, whatever training rule I have laid down for my disciples, my disciples do not transgress it even for the sake of their life" [Cūḷava. 385; A. Ni. 8.20; Udā. 45]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a person accomplished in right view would intentionally deprive a living being of life."
The Discussion of Depriving of Life is finished. ^5-649

#### The Twelfth Chapter ^5-20-9-0

##### (124) 9. Discussion of Bad Destinations ^5-20-9-1-0

Has a person accomplished in right view abandoned bad destinations? Yes. Would a person accomplished in right view feel greed for visible forms of the lower realms? Yes. If a person accomplished in right view would feel greed for visible forms of the lower realms, then surely you must not say: "A person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations."
Has a person accomplished in right view abandoned bad destinations? Yes. Would a person accomplished in right view feel greed for sounds of the lower realms… smells… tastes… touches… engage in sexual intercourse with a non-human female, a female animal or a nāga maiden (a serpent being), accept goats and sheep, accept chickens and pigs, accept elephants, cattle, horses and mares… accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants [variant: … kapiñjalaṃ (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)]? Yes. If a person accomplished in right view would accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants, then surely you must not say: "A person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations." ^5-650

A person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations — would a person accomplished in right view feel greed for visible forms of the lower realms? Yes. A worthy one (arahant) has abandoned bad destinations — would a worthy one feel greed for visible forms of the lower realms? That should not be said… A person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations — would a person accomplished in right view feel greed for sounds of the lower realms… smells… tastes… touches… accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants? Yes. A worthy one has abandoned bad destinations — would a worthy one accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants? That should not be said…
A worthy one has abandoned bad destinations, but would a worthy one not feel greed for visible forms of the lower realms? Yes. A person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations, but would a person accomplished in right view not feel greed for visible forms of the lower realms? That should not be said… A worthy one has abandoned bad destinations, but would a worthy one not feel greed for sounds of the lower realms… smells… tastes… touches… not engage in sexual intercourse with a non-human female, a female animal or a nāga maiden, not accept goats and sheep, not accept chickens and pigs, not accept elephants, cattle, horses and mares… not accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants? Yes. A person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations, but would a person accomplished in right view not accept partridges, quails, peacocks and pheasants? That should not be said… ^5-651

[Following the commentary, this is the mark of the question of the other school. Yet this question seems to belong to our own school, and the earlier ones in this Discussion of Bad Destinations seem as if they should be taken as the other school's] Should it not be said that "a person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations"? Yes. Would a person accomplished in right view be reborn in hell… be reborn in the animal realm… be reborn in the realm of ghosts? That should not be said. In that case a person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations.
The Discussion of Bad Destinations is finished. ^5-652

#### The Twelfth Chapter ^5-20-10-0

##### (125) 10. Discussion of the One in Their Seventh Existence ^5-20-10-1-0

Should it not be said that "a person in their seventh existence has abandoned bad destinations"? Yes. Would a person in their seventh existence be reborn in hell, be reborn in the animal realm, be reborn in the realm of ghosts? That should not be said. In that case a person in their seventh existence has abandoned bad destinations.
The Discussion of the One in Their Seventh Existence is finished.
The Twelfth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
Restraint is action, and likewise non-restraint; all action has a result; sound is a result; the six sense bases are a result; a person who has at most seven more lives is fixed in having at most seven more lives; a person who goes from family to family is fixed in going from family to family; a person with a single seed is fixed in having a single seed; a person accomplished in right view would intentionally deprive a living being of life; a person accomplished in right view has abandoned bad destinations; and likewise one in their seventh existence. ^5-653

### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-0

#### (126) 1. Discussion of the One Who Remains for an Aeon ^5-21-1-0

Would one who remains for an aeon (world-age) remain for a whole aeon? Yes. Does the aeon come into being, and does a Buddha arise in the world? That should not be said… Would one who remains for an aeon remain for a whole aeon? Yes. Does the aeon come into being, and is the Community split? That should not be said… Would one who remains for an aeon remain for a whole aeon? Yes. Does the aeon come into being, and does one who remains for an aeon do the action that makes one remain for an aeon? That should not be said… Would one who remains for an aeon remain for a whole aeon? Yes. Does the aeon come into being, and does the person who remains for an aeon die? That should not be said… ^5-654

Would one who remains for an aeon remain for a whole aeon? Yes. Would they remain for a past aeon, remain for a future aeon? That should not be said… Would one who remains for an aeon remain for a whole aeon? Yes. Would they remain for two aeons… remain for three aeons… remain for four aeons? That should not be said… ^5-655

Would one who remains for an aeon remain for a whole aeon? Yes. When the aeon is burning up, where does the one who remains for an aeon go? They go to another world system. Do they go having died, or do they go through the air? They go having died. Is the action that makes one remain for an aeon one that ripens in some later existence? That should not be said… [“They go through the air” (?) — for this is just the other school's assertion, as in the ninth line of Kathā. 621-623] Do they go through the air? Yes [“They go through the air” (?) — for this is just the other school's assertion, as in the ninth line of Kathā. 621-623]. Does one who remains for an aeon have psychic power? That should not be said… Does one who remains for an aeon have psychic power? Yes. Has the one who remains for an aeon developed the basis of psychic power consisting of desire, developed the basis of psychic power consisting of energy, developed the basis of psychic power consisting of mind, developed the basis of psychic power consisting of investigation? That should not be said… ^5-656

Should it not be said that "one who remains for an aeon would remain for a whole aeon"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Bound for the lower realms, bound for hell, remaining there for an aeon, is the splitter of the Community;
