delighting in faction, standing in what is not the Dhamma, he falls away from security from bondage;
having split a Community that was in harmony [variant: bhinditvā (Sī., Ka.)], he is tormented in hell for an aeon" [Cūḷava. 354; A. Ni. 10.39; Itivu. 18]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one who remains for an aeon would remain for a whole aeon.
The Discussion of the One Who Remains for an Aeon is finished. ^5-657

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-2-0

##### (127) 2. Discussion of Obtaining the Wholesome ^5-21-2-1-0

Would one who remains for an aeon (world-age) not obtain a wholesome mind? Yes. Would one who remains for an aeon give a gift? Yes. If one who remains for an aeon would give a gift, then surely you must not say: "One who remains for an aeon would not obtain a wholesome mind."
Would one who remains for an aeon not obtain a wholesome mind? Yes. Would one who remains for an aeon give robes… give almsfood… give lodgings… give medicines and requisites for the sick… give food to chew… give meals… give drink… pay homage to a shrine… offer a garland at a shrine… offer scents… offer ointments… walk around a shrine keeping it on their right [variant: padakkhiṇaṃ (Pī.)]? Yes. If one who remains for an aeon would walk around a shrine keeping it on their right, then surely you must not say: "One who remains for an aeon would not obtain a wholesome mind."… ^5-658

Would one who remains for an aeon obtain a wholesome mind? Yes. Would they obtain a wholesome mind for emerging from there? Yes. Would they obtain a wholesome mind belonging to the realm of form… belonging to the formless realm… a world-transcending wholesome mind? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Obtaining the Wholesome is finished. ^5-659

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-3-0

##### (128) 3. Discussion of the One Engaged in a Deed with Immediate Result ^5-21-3-1-0

Would a person engaged in a deed with immediate result enter the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Would they enter both the fixed course of wrongness and the fixed course of rightness? That should not be said… Would a person engaged in a deed with immediate result enter the fixed course of rightness? Yes. But hasn't that action been undertaken, remorse been aroused and regret been produced? Yes. If that action has been undertaken, remorse has been aroused and regret has been produced, then surely you must not say: "A person engaged in a deed with immediate result would enter the fixed course of rightness." ^5-660

Is a person engaged in a deed with immediate result incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Have they deprived their mother of life… deprived their father of life… deprived a worthy one (arahant) of life… with a corrupt mind shed the blood of the Tathāgata (the Buddha)… split the Community? That should not be said…
Is a person engaged in a deed with immediate result, having withdrawn from that action, dispelled the remorse and removed the regret [variant: paṭivinodetvā (Sī., Pī., Ka.)], incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness? Yes. Have they deprived their mother of life… deprived their father of life… split the Community? That should not be said…
Is a person engaged in a deed with immediate result, having withdrawn from that action, dispelled the remorse and removed the regret, incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness? Yes. But hasn't that action been withdrawn from, the remorse dispelled and the regret removed? Yes. If that action has been withdrawn from, the remorse dispelled and the regret removed, then surely you must not say: "A person engaged in a deed with immediate result, having withdrawn from that action, dispelled the remorse and removed the regret, is incapable of entering the fixed course of rightness." ^5-661

Would a person engaged in a deed with immediate result enter the fixed course of rightness? Yes. But wasn't that person engaged in that action? Yes. If that person was engaged in that action, then surely you must not say: "A person engaged in a deed with immediate result would enter the fixed course of rightness."
The Discussion of the One Engaged in a Deed with Immediate Result is finished. ^5-662

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-4-0

##### (129) 4. Discussion of the Fixed Course for One Whose Course Is Fixed ^5-21-4-1-0

Does one whose course is fixed enter the fixed course? Yes. Does one whose course is fixed in wrongness enter the fixed course of rightness, and does one whose course is fixed in rightness enter the fixed course of wrongness? That should not be said…
Does one whose course is fixed enter the fixed course? Yes. Having first developed the path, does one afterwards enter the fixed course? That should not be said… Having first developed the path of stream-entry, does one afterwards enter the fixed course of stream-entry? That should not be said… Having first developed the path of once-returning… of non-returning… of arahantship (the state of a worthy one), does one afterwards enter the fixed course of arahantship? That should not be said…
Having first developed a foundation of mindfulness… a right striving… a basis of psychic power… a faculty… a power… a factor of awakening, does one afterwards enter the fixed course? That should not be said… ^5-663

Should it not be said that "one whose course is fixed enters the fixed course"? Yes. Is it possible for the bodhisatta (a Buddha-to-be) not to break through to the Dhamma in that birth? That should not be said. In that case one whose course is fixed enters the fixed course.
The Discussion of the Fixed Course for One Whose Course Is Fixed is finished. ^5-664

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-5-0

##### (130) 5. Discussion of the One Who Is Hindered ^5-21-5-1-0

Does one who is hindered abandon a hindrance? Yes. Does one who is impassioned abandon greed, one who is corrupted abandon hatred, one who is deluded abandon delusion, one who is defiled abandon the defilements? That should not be said… Does one abandon greed by means of greed, hatred by means of hatred, delusion by means of delusion, the defilements by means of the defilements? That should not be said…
Is greed associated with the mind, and is the path associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… Is greed unwholesome, and is the path wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said… ^5-665

Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? The sky, monks, and the earth — this is the first thing that is very far apart… therefore the Dhamma of the good is far from the bad"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome… come face to face."
Does one who is hindered abandon a hindrance? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "When the mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, without blemish, free from impurities, pliable, workable, steady and attained to imperturbability, they direct the mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "one who is hindered abandons a hindrance."… ^5-666

Should it not be said that "one who is hindered abandons a hindrance"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "For one who knows thus, who sees thus, the mind becomes liberated from the taint of sensuality… the mind becomes liberated from the taint of ignorance"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one who is hindered abandons a hindrance.
The Discussion of the One Who Is Hindered is finished. ^5-667

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-6-0

##### (131) 6. Discussion of the One Face to Face ^5-21-6-1-0

Does one who is face to face with a fetter abandon that fetter? Yes. Does one who is impassioned abandon greed, one who is corrupted abandon hatred, one who is deluded abandon delusion, one who is defiled abandon the defilements? That should not be said… Does one abandon greed by means of greed, hatred by means of hatred, delusion by means of delusion, the defilements by means of the defilements? That should not be said…
Is greed associated with the mind, and is the path associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… Is greed unwholesome, and is the path wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said… ^5-668

Do wholesome and unwholesome… come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? The sky, monks, and the earth — this is the first thing that is very far apart… therefore the Dhamma of the good is far from the bad"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome… come face to face."
Does one who is face to face with a fetter abandon that fetter? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "When the mind is thus concentrated… they direct the mind to the knowledge of the destruction of the taints"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "one who is face to face with a fetter abandons that fetter." ^5-669

Should it not be said that "one who is face to face with a fetter abandons that fetter"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "For one who knows thus, who sees thus, the mind becomes liberated from the taint of sensuality… the mind becomes liberated from the taint of ignorance"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one who is face to face with a fetter abandons that fetter.
The Discussion of the One Face to Face is finished. ^5-670

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-7-0

##### (132) 7. Discussion of "One in a Meditative Attainment Relishes It" ^5-21-7-1-0

Does one in a meditative attainment relish it, and does the longing for meditative absorption (jhāna) have meditative absorption as its object? Yes. Is that meditative absorption the object of that same meditative absorption? That should not be said… Is that meditative absorption the object of that same meditative absorption? Yes. Does one contact that contact by that same contact, feel that feeling by that same feeling, perceive that perception by that same perception, intend that intention by that same intention, think that mind by that same mind, think that thought by that same thinking, examine that examining by that same examining, delight in that joy by that same joy, remember that mindfulness by that same mindfulness, understand that wisdom by that same wisdom? That should not be said…
Is the longing for meditative absorption associated with the mind, and is meditative absorption associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said…
Is the longing for meditative absorption unwholesome, and is meditative absorption wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said… ^5-671

Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? The sky, monks, and the earth — this is the first thing that is very far apart… therefore the Dhamma of the good is far from the bad"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face." ^5-672

Should it not be said that "one in a meditative attainment relishes it, and the longing for meditative absorption has meditative absorption as its object"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, monks, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first meditative absorption; they relish it, desire it and find satisfaction in it. With the stilling of thinking and examining… the second meditative absorption… the third meditative absorption… they enter and dwell in the fourth meditative absorption; they relish it, desire it and find satisfaction in it" [A. Ni. 4.123]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one in a meditative attainment relishes it, and the longing for meditative absorption has meditative absorption as its object.
The Discussion of "One in a Meditative Attainment Relishes It" is finished. ^5-673

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-8-0

##### (133) 8. Discussion of Greed for the Unpleasant ^5-21-8-1-0

Is there greed for the unpleasant? Yes. Do beings delight in pain; are there some who wish for pain, long for it, seek it, search for it, look for it, and remain holding on to pain? That should not be said… But don't beings delight in pleasure; aren't there some who wish for pleasure, long for it, seek it, search for it, look for it, and remain holding on to pleasure? Yes. If beings delight in pleasure, and there are some who wish for pleasure, long for it, seek it, search for it, look for it, and remain holding on to pleasure, then surely you must not say: "There is greed for the unpleasant."
Is there greed for the unpleasant? Yes. Does the underlying tendency to greed lie latent in painful feeling, and does the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent in pleasant feeling? That should not be said… But doesn't the underlying tendency to greed lie latent in pleasant feeling, and the underlying tendency to aversion lie latent in painful feeling? Yes. If the underlying tendency to greed lies latent in pleasant feeling, and the underlying tendency to aversion lies latent in painful feeling, then surely you must not say: "There is greed for the unpleasant." ^5-674

Should it not be said that "there is greed for the unpleasant"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Being thus caught up in favouring and opposing, whatever feeling they feel — pleasant, painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — they delight in that feeling, welcome it and remain holding on to it" [M. Ni. 3.409, in the Greater Discourse on the Destruction of Craving]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is greed for the unpleasant.
The Discussion of Greed for the Unpleasant is finished. ^5-675

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-9-0

##### (134) 9. Discussion of "Craving for Mental Objects Is Indeterminate" ^5-21-9-1-0

Is craving for mental objects indeterminate? Yes. Is it a result that is indeterminate, a functional state that is indeterminate, material form, nibbāna (final release), the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said…
Is craving for mental objects indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for visible forms indeterminate? That should not be said… Is craving for mental objects indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for sounds… craving for smells… craving for tastes… craving for touches indeterminate? That should not be said…
Is craving for visible forms unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental objects unwholesome? That should not be said… Is craving for sounds… craving for touches unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental objects unwholesome? That should not be said… ^5-676

Is craving for mental objects indeterminate? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared craving to be unwholesome? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared craving to be unwholesome, then surely you must not say: "Craving for mental objects is indeterminate."
Is craving for mental objects indeterminate? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared greed to be unwholesome, and isn't craving for mental objects greed? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared greed to be unwholesome, and craving for mental objects is greed, then surely you must not say: "Craving for mental objects is indeterminate." ^5-677

Is craving for mental objects, being greed, indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for visible forms, being greed, indeterminate? That should not be said… Is craving for mental objects, being greed, indeterminate? Yes. Is craving for sounds… craving for touches, being greed, indeterminate? That should not be said…
Is craving for visible forms, being greed, unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental objects, being greed, unwholesome? That should not be said… Is craving for sounds… craving for touches, being greed, unwholesome? Yes. Is craving for mental objects, being greed, unwholesome? That should not be said… ^5-678

Is craving for mental objects indeterminate? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "This craving, which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and greed, and delights now here, now there — namely, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence" [Mahāva. 14; D. Ni. 2.400]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "craving for mental objects is indeterminate." ^5-679

Should it not be said that "craving for mental objects is indeterminate"? Yes. But isn't it craving for mental objects? Yes. If it is craving for mental objects, then surely you must also say: "Craving for mental objects is indeterminate."
The Discussion of "Craving for Mental Objects Is Indeterminate" is finished. ^5-680

#### The Thirteenth Chapter ^5-21-10-0

##### (135) 10. Discussion of "Craving for Mental Objects Is Not the Origin of Suffering" ^5-21-10-1-0

Is craving for mental objects not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for visible forms not the origin of suffering? That should not be said… Is craving for mental objects not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for sounds… craving for smells… craving for tastes… craving for touches not the origin of suffering? That should not be said…
Is craving for visible forms the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental objects the origin of suffering? That should not be said… Is craving for sounds… craving for smells… craving for tastes… craving for touches the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental objects the origin of suffering? That should not be said… ^5-681

Is craving for mental objects not the origin of suffering? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared craving to be the origin of suffering? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared craving to be the origin of suffering, then surely you must not say: "Craving for mental objects is not the origin of suffering." Is craving for mental objects not the origin of suffering? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared greed to be the origin of suffering, and isn't craving for mental objects greed? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared greed to be the origin of suffering, and craving for mental objects is greed, then surely you must not say: "Craving for mental objects is not the origin of suffering." ^5-682

Is craving for mental objects greed, and yet not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for visible forms greed, and yet not the origin of suffering? That should not be said… Is craving for mental objects greed, and yet not the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for sounds… craving for smells… craving for tastes… craving for touches greed, and yet not the origin of suffering? That should not be said…
Is craving for visible forms, being greed, the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental objects, being greed, the origin of suffering? That should not be said… Is craving for sounds… craving for touches, being greed, the origin of suffering? Yes. Is craving for mental objects, being greed, the origin of suffering? That should not be said… ^5-683

Is craving for mental objects not the origin of suffering? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "This craving, which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and greed, and delights now here, now there — namely, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "craving for mental objects is not the origin of suffering." ^5-684

Should it not be said that "craving for mental objects is not the origin of suffering"? Yes. But isn't it craving for mental objects? Yes. If it is craving for mental objects, then surely you must also say: "Craving for mental objects is not the origin of suffering."
The Discussion of "Craving for Mental Objects Is Not the Origin of Suffering" is finished.
The Thirteenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
One who remains for an aeon would remain for a whole aeon; one who remains for an aeon would not obtain a wholesome mind; a person engaged in a deed with immediate result would enter the fixed course of rightness; one whose course is fixed enters the fixed course; one who is hindered abandons a hindrance; one who is face to face abandons a fetter; the longing for meditative absorption; greed for the unpleasant; craving for mental objects is indeterminate; craving for mental objects is not the origin of suffering. ^5-685

### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-0

#### (136) 1. Discussion of the Linking of the Wholesome and the Unwholesome ^5-22-1-0

Does an unwholesome root link up with a wholesome root? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the wholesome? That should not be said…
An unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the wholesome"? Yes. Does the wholesome arise for one who does not turn the mind to it [variant: anāvaṭṭantassa (Sī., Pī., Ka.), anāvajjantassa (Syā., Kaṃ.)]… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't the wholesome arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If the wholesome arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "An unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root." ^5-686

Does an unwholesome root link up with a wholesome root? Yes. Does an unwholesome root arise for one who attends unwisely? Yes. Does the wholesome arise for one who attends unwisely? That should not be said… But doesn't the wholesome arise for one who attends wisely? Yes. If the wholesome arises for one who attends wisely, then surely you must not say: "An unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root."
Does an unwholesome root link up with a wholesome root? Yes. Does the perception of renunciation arise immediately after the perception of sensual desire, the perception of non-ill will immediately after the perception of ill will, the perception of harmlessness immediately after the perception of harming, loving-kindness immediately after ill will, compassion immediately after harming, sympathetic joy immediately after discontent, equanimity immediately after aversion? That should not be said… ^5-687

Does a wholesome root link up with an unwholesome root? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the wholesome the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome? That should not be said…
A wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the wholesome is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the unwholesome"? Yes. Does the unwholesome arise for one who does not turn the mind to it… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't the unwholesome arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If the unwholesome arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "A wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root." ^5-688

Does a wholesome root link up with an unwholesome root? Yes. Does the wholesome arise for one who attends wisely? Yes. Does the unwholesome arise for one who attends wisely? That should not be said… But doesn't the unwholesome arise for one who attends unwisely? Yes. If the unwholesome arises for one who attends unwisely, then surely you must not say: "A wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root."
Does a wholesome root link up with an unwholesome root? Yes. Does the perception of sensual desire arise immediately after the perception of renunciation, the perception of ill will immediately after the perception of non-ill will, the perception of harming immediately after the perception of harmlessness, ill will immediately after loving-kindness, harming immediately after compassion, discontent immediately after sympathetic joy, aversion immediately after equanimity? That should not be said… ^5-689

Should it not be said that "an unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root, and a wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root"? Yes. But isn't it the case that one becomes free of greed toward the very same object toward which one feels greed, and feels greed toward the very same object toward which one becomes free of greed? Yes. If one becomes free of greed toward the very same object toward which one feels greed, and feels greed toward the very same object toward which one becomes free of greed, then surely you must also say: "An unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root, and a wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root."
The Discussion of the Linking of the Wholesome and the Unwholesome is finished. ^5-690

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-2-0

##### (137) 2. Discussion of the Arising of the Six Sense Bases ^5-22-2-1-0

Do the six sense bases take shape in the mother's womb at one and the same time, neither before nor after? Yes. Does one descend into the mother's womb with all one's major and minor limbs, with no faculty lacking? That should not be said…
Does the eye base take shape with the rebirth-seeking mind? Yes. Do the hands take shape with the rebirth-seeking mind, do the feet take shape, does the head take shape, does the ear take shape, does the nose take shape, does the mouth take shape, do the teeth take shape? That should not be said…
Does the ear base… the nose base… the tongue base take shape with the rebirth-seeking mind? Yes. Do the hands take shape with the rebirth-seeking mind, do the feet take shape, does the head take shape, does the ear take shape, does the nose take shape, does the mouth take shape, do the teeth take shape? That should not be said… ^5-691

For one who has entered the mother's womb, does the eye base arise later? Yes. Does one perform action in the mother's womb to obtain an eye? That should not be said… For one who has entered the mother's womb, does the ear base… the nose base… the tongue base arise later? Yes. Does one perform action in the mother's womb to obtain a tongue? That should not be said…
For one who has entered the mother's womb, do head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth and bones arise later? Yes. Does one perform action in the mother's womb to obtain bones? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "for one who has entered the mother's womb, head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth and bones arise later"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"First there is the kalala (a fluid drop); from the kalala comes the abbuda (a froth);
from the abbuda the pesi (a lump of flesh) [variant: pesī (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)] is born; from the pesi the ghana (a firm mass) arises [variant: nibbattatī (Sī., Syā., S. Ni. 1.235), nibbattati (Pī., Ka.)];
from the ghana the limbs grow, and the head hairs, body hairs and nails.
"And whatever the mother eats — food, drink and meals —
by that the person who has entered the mother's womb is sustained there" [S. Ni. 1.235]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case, for one who has entered the mother's womb, head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth and bones arise later.
The Discussion of the Arising of the Six Sense Bases is finished. ^5-692

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-3-0

##### (138) 3. Discussion of the Proximity Condition ^5-22-3-1-0

Does ear-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of eye-consciousness the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of ear-consciousness? That should not be said…
Ear-consciousness arises immediately after eye-consciousness — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of eye-consciousness is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of ear-consciousness"? Yes. Does ear-consciousness arise for one who does not turn the mind to it… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't ear-consciousness arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If ear-consciousness arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "Ear-consciousness arises immediately after eye-consciousness." ^5-693

Does ear-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise for one who attends to the sign of visible form? Yes. Does ear-consciousness arise for one who attends to the sign of visible form? That should not be said…
Does eye-consciousness have visible form alone as its object and no other object? Yes. Does ear-consciousness have visible form alone as its object and no other object? That should not be said…
Does eye-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on visible forms? Yes. Does ear-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on visible forms? That should not be said…
Does ear-consciousness arise dependent on the eye and on visible forms? Yes. "Ear-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Eye-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms," then surely you must not say: "Ear-consciousness arises dependent on the eye and on visible forms."
Does ear-consciousness arise immediately after eye-consciousness? Yes. Is that very eye-consciousness that ear-consciousness? That should not be said… ^5-694

Does nose-consciousness arise immediately after ear-consciousness… tongue-consciousness immediately after nose-consciousness… does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of tongue-consciousness the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of body-consciousness? That should not be said… Body-consciousness arises immediately after tongue-consciousness — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of tongue-consciousness is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of body-consciousness"? Yes. Does body-consciousness arise for one who does not turn the mind to it… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't body-consciousness arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If body-consciousness arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "Body-consciousness arises immediately after tongue-consciousness." ^5-695

Does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness? Yes. Does tongue-consciousness arise for one who attends to the sign of taste? Yes. Does body-consciousness arise for one who attends to the sign of taste? That should not be said…
Does tongue-consciousness have taste alone as its object and no other object? Yes. Does body-consciousness have taste alone as its object and no other object? That should not be said…
Does tongue-consciousness arise dependent on the tongue and on tastes? Yes. Does body-consciousness arise dependent on the tongue and on tastes? That should not be said…
Does body-consciousness arise dependent on the tongue and on tastes? Yes. "Body-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Tongue-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Tongue-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes," then surely you must not say: "Body-consciousness arises dependent on the tongue and on tastes."
Does body-consciousness arise immediately after tongue-consciousness? Yes. Is that very tongue-consciousness that body-consciousness? That should not be said… ^5-696

Should it not be said that "the five kinds of consciousness arise immediately after one another"? Yes. But isn't there someone who dances, sings and plays music, and sees a visible form, hears a sound, smells a smell, tastes a taste and touches a touch? Yes. If there is someone who dances, sings and plays music, and sees a visible form, hears a sound, smells a smell, tastes a taste and touches a touch, then surely you must also say: "The five kinds of consciousness arise immediately after one another."
The Discussion of the Proximity Condition is finished. ^5-697

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-4-0

##### (139) 4. Discussion of Noble Material Form ^5-22-4-1-0

Is noble material form derived from the great elements? Yes. Is noble material form wholesome? Yes. Are the great elements wholesome? That should not be said… Are the great elements indeterminate? Yes. Is noble material form indeterminate? That should not be said… Is noble material form derived from the great elements? Yes. Is noble material form free of taints, not subject to the fetters, not subject to the knots, not subject to the floods, not subject to the bonds, not subject to the hindrances, not seized upon, not subject to clinging, not subject to defilement? Yes. Are the great elements free of taints… not subject to defilement? That should not be said… Are the great elements accompanied by taints, subject to the fetters… subject to defilement? Yes. Is noble material form accompanied by taints, subject to the fetters… subject to defilement? That should not be said… ^5-698

Should it not be said that "noble material form is derived from the great elements"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, whatever material form there is — the four great elements and material form derived from the four great elements" [M. Ni. 1.347; A. Ni. 11.15]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case noble material form is derived from the great elements.
The Discussion of Noble Material Form is finished. ^5-699

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-5-0

##### (140) 5. Discussion of "The Underlying Tendency Is One Thing" ^5-22-5-1-0

Is the underlying tendency to sensual greed one thing and obsession by sensual greed another? Yes. Is sensual greed one thing and obsession by sensual greed another? That should not be said… Is that very sensual greed that obsession by sensual greed? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to sensual greed that obsession by sensual greed? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to aversion one thing and obsession by aversion another? Yes. Is aversion one thing and obsession by aversion another? That should not be said… Is that very aversion that obsession by aversion? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to aversion that obsession by aversion? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to conceit one thing and obsession by conceit another? Yes. Is conceit one thing and obsession by conceit another? That should not be said… Is that very conceit that obsession by conceit? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to conceit that obsession by conceit? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to views one thing and obsession by views another? Yes. Is wrong view one thing and obsession by views another? That should not be said… Is that very wrong view that obsession by views? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to views that obsession by views? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to doubt one thing and obsession by doubt another? Yes. Is doubt one thing and obsession by doubt another? That should not be said… Is that very doubt that obsession by doubt? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to doubt that obsession by doubt? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to greed for existence one thing and obsession by greed for existence another? Yes. Is greed for existence one thing and obsession by greed for existence another? That should not be said… Is that very greed for existence that obsession by greed for existence? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to greed for existence that obsession by greed for existence? That should not be said…
Is the underlying tendency to ignorance one thing and obsession by ignorance another? Yes. Is ignorance one thing and obsession by ignorance another? That should not be said… Is that very ignorance that obsession by ignorance? Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to ignorance that obsession by ignorance? That should not be said… ^5-700

Should it not be said that "the underlying tendency is one thing and the obsession another"? Yes. When a wholesome or indeterminate mind is occurring in an ordinary person, should that person be called "one with underlying tendencies"? Yes. Should they be called "obsessed"? That should not be said. In that case the underlying tendency is one thing and the obsession another. When a wholesome or indeterminate mind is occurring in an ordinary person, should that person be called "one who has greed"? Yes. Should they be called "obsessed"? That should not be said. In that case greed is one thing and the obsession another.
The Discussion of "The Underlying Tendency Is One Thing" is finished. ^5-701

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-6-0

##### (141) 6. Discussion of "Obsession Is Dissociated from the Mind" ^5-22-6-1-0

Is obsession dissociated from the mind? Yes. Is it material form, nibbāna (final release), the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said… Is obsession dissociated from the mind? Yes. Is there no mind with greed, no mind with hatred, no mind with delusion… no unwholesome mind, no defiled mind? That should not be said… But isn't there a mind with greed, a mind with hatred, a mind with delusion… an unwholesome mind, a defiled mind? Yes. If there is a mind with greed, a mind with hatred, a mind with delusion… an unwholesome mind, a defiled mind, then surely you must not say: "Obsession is dissociated from the mind."
The Discussion of "Obsession Is Dissociated from the Mind" is finished. ^5-702

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-7-0

##### (142) 7. Discussion of Being Included ^5-22-7-1-0

Does greed for the realm of form lie latent in the realm of form, and is it included in the realm of form? Yes. Is it something that seeks attainment, that seeks rebirth, a pleasant dwelling in this very life; is it accompanied by, arisen together with, mixed with, associated with, does it arise together with, cease together with, have the same base and the same object as a mind that seeks attainment, a mind that seeks rebirth, a mind of pleasant dwelling in this very life? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it does not seek attainment, does not seek rebirth, is not a pleasant dwelling in this very life, and is not accompanied by, arisen together with, mixed with, associated with, does not arise together with, cease together with, have the same base and the same object as a mind that seeks attainment, a mind that seeks rebirth, a mind of pleasant dwelling in this very life? Yes. If it does not seek attainment, does not seek rebirth, is not a pleasant dwelling in this very life… and does not have the same object, then surely you must not say: "Greed for the realm of form lies latent in the realm of form and is included in the realm of form."…
Does greed for the realm of form lie latent in the realm of form, and is it included in the realm of form? Yes. Does greed for sounds lie latent in the sound element, and is it included in the sound element? That should not be said… Does greed for the realm of form lie latent in the realm of form, and is it included in the realm of form? Yes. Does greed for smells… greed for tastes… greed for touches lie latent in the touch element, and is it included in the touch element? That should not be said…
Greed for sounds lies latent in the sound element — should it not be said that "it is included in the sound element"? Yes. Greed for the realm of form lies latent in the realm of form — should it not be said that "it is included in the realm of form"? That should not be said… Greed for smells… greed for tastes… greed for touches lies latent in the touch element — should it not be said that "it is included in the touch element"? Yes. Greed for the realm of form lies latent in the realm of form — should it not be said that "it is included in the realm of form"? That should not be said… ^5-703

Does greed for the formless realm lie latent in the formless realm, and is it included in the formless realm? Yes. Is it something that seeks attainment, that seeks rebirth, a pleasant dwelling in this very life; is it accompanied by, arisen together with, mixed with, associated with, does it arise together with, cease together with, have the same base and the same object as a mind that seeks attainment, a mind that seeks rebirth, a mind of pleasant dwelling in this very life? That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it does not seek attainment, does not seek rebirth, is not a pleasant dwelling in this very life, and is not accompanied by a mind that seeks attainment… and does not have the same object? Yes. If it does not seek attainment, does not seek rebirth… and does not have the same object, then surely you must not say: "Greed for the formless realm lies latent in the formless realm and is included in the formless realm."
Does greed for the formless realm lie latent in the formless realm, and is it included in the formless realm? Yes. Does greed for sounds lie latent in the sound element, and is it included in the sound element? That should not be said… Does greed for the formless realm lie latent in the formless realm, and is it included in the formless realm? Yes. Does greed for smells… greed for tastes… greed for touches lie latent in the touch element, and is it included in the touch element? That should not be said…
Greed for sounds lies latent in the sound element — should it not be said that "it is included in the sound element"? Yes. Greed for the formless realm lies latent in the formless realm — should it not be said that "it is included in the formless realm"? That should not be said… Greed for smells… greed for tastes… greed for touches lies latent in the touch element — should it not be said that "it is included in the touch element"? Yes. Greed for the formless realm lies latent in the formless realm — should it not be said that "it is included in the formless realm"? That should not be said… ^5-704

Should it not be said that "greed for the realm of form lies latent in the realm of form and is included in the realm of form, and greed for the formless realm lies latent in the formless realm and is included in the formless realm"? Yes. But doesn't sensual greed lie latent in the sense-desire realm, and isn't it included in the sense-desire realm? Yes. If sensual greed lies latent in the sense-desire realm and is included in the sense-desire realm, then surely you must also say: "Greed for the realm of form lies latent in the realm of form and is included in the realm of form, and greed for the formless realm lies latent in the formless realm and is included in the formless realm."
The Discussion of Being Included is finished. ^5-705

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-8-0

##### (143) 8. Discussion of the Indeterminate ^5-22-8-1-0

Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. Are they a result that is indeterminate, a functional state that is indeterminate, material form, nibbāna (final release), the eye base… the touch base? That should not be said… Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. Is contact associated with speculative views indeterminate? That should not be said… Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. Are feeling… perception… intention… mind associated with speculative views indeterminate? That should not be said…
Is contact associated with speculative views unwholesome? Yes. Are speculative views unwholesome? That should not be said… Are feeling, perception, intention and mind associated with speculative views unwholesome? Yes. Are speculative views unwholesome? That should not be said… ^5-706

Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. Are they without fruit and without result? That should not be said… But don't they have fruit and result? Yes. If they have fruit and result, then surely you must not say: "Speculative views are indeterminate."
Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared that among faults wrong view is the worst [in the Aṅguttara Nikāya]? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that among faults wrong view is the worst, then surely you must not say: "Speculative views are indeterminate."
Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Wrong view, Vaccha, is unwholesome [variant: akusalaṃ (M. Ni. 2.194)]; right view is wholesome" [variant: kusalaṃ (M. Ni. 2.104)] [M. Ni. 2.194]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "speculative views are indeterminate."
Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Puṇṇa, for one with wrong view I declare one of two destinations — hell or the animal realm" [M. Ni. 2.79]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "speculative views are indeterminate." ^5-707

Should it not be said that "speculative views are indeterminate"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "‘The world is eternal’ — this, Vaccha, is indeterminate (left undeclared); ‘the world is not eternal’ — this, Vaccha, is indeterminate; ‘the world is finite’ — this, Vaccha, is indeterminate; ‘the world is infinite’ — Vaccha… ‘the soul is the same as the body’ — Vaccha… ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ — Vaccha… ‘the Tathāgata (the Buddha) exists after death’ — Vaccha… ‘the Tathāgata does not exist after death’ — Vaccha… ‘the Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death’ — Vaccha… ‘the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’ — this, Vaccha, is indeterminate" [S. Ni. 4.416, but slightly different]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case speculative views are indeterminate.
Are speculative views indeterminate? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, for a person with wrong view, whatever bodily action they have carried out and undertaken in accordance with that view, whatever verbal action… whatever mental action, whatever intention, whatever wish, whatever aspiration, whatever mental formations — all those things lead to what is undesired, unloved and disagreeable, to harm and to suffering" [A. Ni. 1.306]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "speculative views are indeterminate."
The Discussion of the Indeterminate is finished. ^5-708

#### The Fourteenth Chapter ^5-22-9-0

##### (144) 9. Discussion of "Not Included" ^5-22-9-1-0

Are speculative views not included in any realm? Yes. Are they the path, the fruit, nibbāna (final release), the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry, the path of once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, the path of non-returning, the fruit of non-returning, the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one), the fruit of arahantship, a foundation of mindfulness, a right striving, a basis of psychic power, a faculty, a power, a factor of awakening? That should not be said… ^5-709

Should it not be said that "speculative views are not included in any realm"? Yes. Should an ordinary person be called "free from greed for sensual pleasures"? Yes. Should they be called "free from views"? That should not be said. In that case speculative views are not included in any realm.
The Discussion of "Not Included" is finished.
The Fourteenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
An unwholesome root links up with a wholesome root, a wholesome root links up with an unwholesome root; the six sense bases; the six groups of consciousness; noble material form is derived from the great elements; that very underlying tendency is that obsession; obsession is dissociated from the mind; it lies latent in that very element to which it belongs; speculative views are indeterminate; speculative views are not included in any realm. ^5-710

### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-0

#### (145) 1. Discussion of Conditionality ^5-23-1-0

Is conditionality rigidly fixed? Yes. But isn't investigation a root, and isn't it also predominant? Yes. If investigation is a root and is also predominant, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of root condition, and a condition by way of predominance condition."
But isn't desire as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it? Yes. If desire as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of co-arising condition." ^5-711

But isn't energy as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it? Yes. If energy as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of co-arising condition."
But isn't energy as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it, and isn't it also a faculty? Yes. If energy as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it and is also a faculty, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of faculty condition."
But isn't energy as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it, and isn't it also a factor of the path? Yes. If energy as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it and is also a factor of the path, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of path condition." ^5-712

But isn't mind as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it? Yes. If mind as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of co-arising condition."
But isn't mind as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it, and isn't it also a nutriment? Yes. If mind as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it and is also a nutriment, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of nutriment condition."
But isn't mind as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it, and isn't it also a faculty? Yes. If mind as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it and is also a faculty, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of faculty condition." ^5-713

But isn't investigation as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it? Yes. If investigation as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of co-arising condition."
But isn't investigation as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it, and isn't it also a faculty? Yes. If investigation as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it and is also a faculty, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of faculty condition."
But isn't investigation as a predominant factor predominant over the states arisen together with it, and isn't it also a factor of the path? Yes. If investigation as a predominant factor is predominant over the states arisen together with it and is also a factor of the path, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of path condition." ^5-714

But doesn't reviewing arise taking a noble state as its weighty concern, and isn't that state also its object? Yes. If reviewing arises taking a noble state as its weighty concern, and that state is also its object, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of predominance condition, and a condition by way of object condition." ^5-715

But isn't each preceding wholesome state a condition by way of proximity condition for each following wholesome state, and isn't that also repetition? Yes. If each preceding wholesome state is a condition by way of proximity condition for each following wholesome state, and that is also repetition, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of proximity condition, and a condition by way of repetition condition."
But isn't each preceding unwholesome state a condition by way of proximity condition for each following unwholesome state, and isn't that also repetition? Yes. If each preceding unwholesome state is a condition by way of proximity condition for each following unwholesome state, and that is also repetition, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of proximity condition, and a condition by way of repetition condition."
But isn't each preceding functional indeterminate state a condition by way of proximity condition for each following functional indeterminate state, and isn't that also repetition? Yes. If each preceding functional indeterminate state is a condition by way of proximity condition for each following functional indeterminate state, and that is also repetition, then surely you must also say: "It is a condition by way of proximity condition, and a condition by way of repetition condition." ^5-716

Should it not be said that "conditionality is rigidly fixed"? Yes. Is a thing a condition by way of root condition, a condition by way of object condition, a condition by way of proximity condition, a condition by way of immediate-proximity condition? That should not be said. In that case conditionality is rigidly fixed.
The Discussion of Conditionality is finished. ^5-717

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-2-0

##### (146) 2. Discussion of Mutual Condition ^5-23-2-1-0

Is it only with ignorance as condition that there are formations, and should it not be said that "with formations as condition there is also ignorance"? Yes. But hasn't ignorance arisen together with formations? Yes. If ignorance has arisen together with formations, then surely you must also say: "With ignorance as condition there are formations, and with formations as condition there is also ignorance."
Is it only with craving as condition that there is clinging, and should it not be said that "with clinging as condition there is also craving"? Yes. But hasn't craving arisen together with clinging? Yes. If craving has arisen together with clinging, then surely you must also say: "With craving as condition there is clinging, and with clinging as condition there is also craving." ^5-718

"Monks, with ageing and death as condition there is birth; with birth as condition there is existence" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. In that case it is only with ignorance as condition that there are formations, and it should not be said that "with formations as condition there is also ignorance"; it is only with craving as condition that there is clinging, and it should not be said that "with clinging as condition there is also craving."
"Monks, with consciousness as condition there is name-and-form (mind and body); with name-and-form as condition there is also consciousness" [D. Ni. 2.58, but slightly different] — is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case with ignorance as condition there are formations, and with formations as condition there is also ignorance; with craving as condition there is clinging, and with clinging as condition there is also craving.
The Discussion of Mutual Condition is finished. ^5-719

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-3-0

##### (147) 3. Discussion of Time ^5-23-3-1-0

Is time fully formed? Yes. Is it material form? That should not be said… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness? That should not be said… Is past time fully formed? Yes. Is it material form? That should not be said… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness? That should not be said… Is future time fully formed? Yes. Is it material form? That should not be said… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness? That should not be said… Is present time fully formed? Yes. Is it material form? That should not be said… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness? That should not be said…
Are past material form, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness past time? Yes. Are there five past times? That should not be said… Are future material form, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness future time? Yes. Are there five future times? That should not be said… Are present material form, feeling, perception, mental formations and consciousness present time? Yes. Are there five present times? That should not be said…
Are the five past aggregates past time, the five future aggregates future time, and the five present aggregates present time? Yes. Are there fifteen times? That should not be said…
Are the twelve past sense bases past time, the twelve future sense bases future time, and the twelve present sense bases present time? Yes. Are there thirty-six times? That should not be said…
Are the eighteen past elements past time, the eighteen future elements future time, and the eighteen present elements present time? Yes. Are there fifty-four times? That should not be said…
Are the twenty-two past faculties past time, the twenty-two future faculties future time, and the twenty-two present faculties present time? Yes. Are there sixty-six times? That should not be said… ^5-720

Should it not be said that "time is fully formed"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these three points of discussion. Which three? One might talk about past time, monks, saying: ‘Thus it was in past time’; one might talk about future time, monks, saying: ‘Thus it will be in future time’; or one might talk now about present time, monks, saying: ‘Thus it is now, in the present.’ These, monks, are the three points of discussion" [A. Ni. 3.68; D. Ni. 3.305]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case time is fully formed.
The Discussion of Time is finished. ^5-721

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-4-0

##### (148) 4. Discussion of Moments, Instants and Short Periods ^5-23-4-1-0

Is a moment fully formed, is an instant fully formed, is a short period fully formed? Yes. Is it material form? That should not be said… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness? That should not be said… ^5-722

Should it not be said that "a short period is fully formed"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these three points of discussion. Which three? One might talk about past time, monks, saying: ‘Thus it was in past time’; one might talk about future time, monks, saying: ‘Thus it will be in future time’; or one might talk now about present time, monks, saying: ‘Thus it is now, in the present.’ These, monks, are the three points of discussion"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case a short period is fully formed.
The Discussion of Moments, Instants and Short Periods is finished. ^5-723

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-5-0

##### (149) 5. Discussion of the Taints ^5-23-5-1-0

Are the four taints free of taints? Yes. Are they the path, the fruit, nibbāna (final release), the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… a factor of awakening? That should not be said… ^5-724

Should it not be said that "the four taints are free of taints"? Yes. Are there yet other taints by which those taints would be accompanied by taints? That should not be said. In that case the four taints are free of taints.
The Discussion of the Taints is finished. ^5-725

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-6-0

##### (150) 6. Discussion of Ageing and Death ^5-23-6-1-0

Is the ageing and death of world-transcending states world-transcending? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, nibbāna (final release), the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… a factor of awakening? That should not be said… Is the ageing and death of the path of stream-entry the path of stream-entry? That should not be said… Is the ageing and death of the path of stream-entry the path of stream-entry? Yes. Is the ageing and death of the fruit of stream-entry the fruit of stream-entry? That should not be said… of the path of once-returning… of the fruit of once-returning… of the path of non-returning… of the fruit of non-returning… Is the ageing and death of the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) the path of arahantship? That should not be said… Is the ageing and death of the path of arahantship the path of arahantship? Yes. Is the ageing and death of the fruit of arahantship the fruit of arahantship? That should not be said… Is the ageing and death of the foundations of mindfulness… of the right strivings… of the bases of psychic power… of the faculties… of the powers… of the factors of awakening a factor of awakening? That should not be said… ^5-726

Should it not be said that "the ageing and death of world-transcending states is world-transcending"? Yes. Is it worldly? That should not be said. In that case it is world-transcending.
The Discussion of Ageing and Death is finished. ^5-727

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-7-0

##### (151) 7. Discussion of Perception and Feeling ^5-23-7-1-0

Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling world-transcending? Yes. Is it the path, the fruit, nibbāna (final release), the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry… a factor of awakening? That should not be said… ^5-728

Should it not be said that "the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is world-transcending"? Yes. Is it worldly? That should not be said. In that case it is world-transcending.
The Discussion of Perception and Feeling is finished. ^5-729

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-8-0

##### (152) 8. Second Discussion of Perception and Feeling ^5-23-8-1-0

Is the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling worldly? Yes. Is it material form? That should not be said… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness? That should not be said… Does it belong to the sense-desire realm? That should not be said… Does it belong to the realm of form? That should not be said… Does it belong to the formless realm? That should not be said… ^5-730

Should it not be said that "the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is worldly"? Yes. Is it world-transcending? That should not be said. In that case it is worldly.
The Second Discussion of Perception and Feeling is finished. ^5-731

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-9-0

##### (153) 9. Third Discussion of Perception and Feeling ^5-23-9-1-0

Could one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have contact at the point of death, feeling at the point of death, perception at the point of death, intention at the point of death, mind at the point of death? That should not be said… Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have no contact at the point of death, no feeling at the point of death, no perception at the point of death, no intention at the point of death, no mind at the point of death? Yes. If one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling has no contact at the point of death, no feeling at the point of death, no perception at the point of death, no intention at the point of death, no mind at the point of death, then surely you must not say: "One who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling could die."
Could one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have contact, feeling, perception, intention and mind? That should not be said… Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have no contact, feeling, perception, intention or mind? Yes. Is there death for one without contact, death for one without feeling… death for one without mind? That should not be said… But isn't there death for one with contact… death for one with mind? Yes. If there is death for one with contact… death for one with mind, then surely you must not say: "One who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling could die."
Could one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Could poison, a weapon or fire affect the body of one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling? That should not be said… Could poison not affect, could a weapon not affect, could fire not affect the body of one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling? Yes. If poison could not affect, a weapon could not affect and fire could not affect the body of one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling, then surely you must not say: "One who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling could die."
Could one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling die? Yes. Could poison, a weapon or fire affect the body of one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling? Yes. Then has that one not entered cessation? That should not be said… ^5-732

Would one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling not die? Yes. Is there a fixed course by which, being fixed, one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling would not die? There is not. If there is no fixed course by which, being fixed, one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling would not die, then surely you must not say: "One who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling would not die." ^5-733

Would one possessing eye-consciousness not die? Yes. Is there a fixed course by which, being fixed, one possessing eye-consciousness would not die? There is not. If there is no fixed course by which, being fixed, one possessing eye-consciousness would not die, then surely you must not say: "One possessing eye-consciousness would not die."
The Third Discussion of Perception and Feeling is finished. ^5-734

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-10-0

##### (154) 10. Discussion of "Leading to Rebirth among the Beings without Perception" ^5-23-10-1-0

Does the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling lead to rebirth among the beings without perception? Yes. Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have non-greed as a wholesome root, non-hatred as a wholesome root, non-delusion as a wholesome root, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration and wisdom? That should not be said… Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling not have non-greed as a wholesome root, non-hatred as a wholesome root… wisdom? Yes. If one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling does not have non-greed as a wholesome root, non-hatred as a wholesome root, non-delusion as a wholesome root, faith, energy, mindfulness, concentration and wisdom, then surely you must not say: "The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling leads to rebirth among the beings without perception."
Does the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling lead to rebirth among the beings without perception? Yes. Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have contact, feeling, perception, intention and mind? That should not be said… Does one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling have no contact, feeling, perception, intention or mind? Yes. Is there development of the path for one without contact… development of the path for one without mind? That should not be said… But isn't there development of the path for one with contact… development of the path for one with mind? Yes. If there is development of the path for one with contact… development of the path for one with mind, then surely you must not say: "The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling leads to rebirth among the beings without perception."
Does the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling lead to rebirth among the beings without perception? Yes. Are all those who enter the cessation of perception and feeling bound for rebirth among the beings without perception? That should not be said… ^5-735

Should it not be said that "the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling leads to rebirth among the beings without perception"? Yes. But isn't one without perception here and without perception there as well? Yes. If one is without perception here and without perception there as well, then surely you must also say: "The attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling leads to rebirth among the beings without perception."
The Discussion of "Leading to Rebirth among the Beings without Perception" is finished. ^5-736

#### The Fifteenth Chapter ^5-23-11-0

##### (155) 11. Discussion of the Accumulation of Action ^5-23-11-1-0

Is action one thing and the accumulation of action another? Yes. Is contact one thing and the accumulation of contact another; feeling one thing and the accumulation of feeling another; perception one thing and the accumulation of perception another; intention one thing and the accumulation of intention another; mind one thing and the accumulation of mind another; faith one thing and the accumulation of faith another; energy one thing and the accumulation of energy another; mindfulness one thing and the accumulation of mindfulness another; concentration one thing and the accumulation of concentration another; wisdom one thing and the accumulation of wisdom another; greed one thing and the accumulation of greed another… lack of moral fear one thing and the accumulation of lack of moral fear another? That should not be said… ^5-737

Is action one thing and the accumulation of action another? Yes. Has the accumulation of action arisen together with action? That should not be said…
Has the accumulation of action arisen together with action? Yes. Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with wholesome action wholesome? That should not be said…
Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with wholesome action wholesome? Yes. Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with action associated with pleasant feeling associated with pleasant feeling? That should not be said… with painful feeling… Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with action associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? That should not be said… ^5-738

Has the accumulation of action arisen together with action? Yes. Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with unwholesome action unwholesome? That should not be said…
Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with unwholesome action unwholesome? Yes. Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with action associated with pleasant feeling associated with pleasant feeling? That should not be said… with painful feeling… Is the accumulation of action that has arisen together with action associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling? That should not be said… ^5-739

Has action arisen together with the mind, and does action have an object? Yes. Has the accumulation of action arisen together with the mind, and does the accumulation of action have an object? That should not be said… Has the accumulation of action arisen together with the mind, and is the accumulation of action without an object? Yes. Has action arisen together with the mind, and is action without an object? That should not be said…
Has action arisen together with the mind, and when the mind breaks up, does action break up? Yes. Has the accumulation of action arisen together with the mind, and when the mind breaks up, does the accumulation of action break up? That should not be said…
Has the accumulation of action arisen together with the mind, and when the mind breaks up, does the accumulation of action not break up? Yes. Has action arisen together with the mind, and when the mind breaks up, does action not break up? That should not be said… ^5-740

Is the accumulation of action in the action? Yes. Is that very action that accumulation of action? That should not be said…
Is the accumulation of action in the action, and is the result produced from the accumulation of action? Yes. Is that very action that accumulation of action and that result of action? That should not be said…
Is the accumulation of action in the action, is the result produced from the accumulation of action, and does the result have an object? Yes. Does the accumulation of action have an object? That should not be said… Is the accumulation of action without an object? Yes. Is the result without an object? That should not be said… ^5-741

Is action one thing and the accumulation of action another? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, Puṇṇa, someone generates a bodily formation that is both hurtful and unhurtful [variant: sabyāpajjhampi abyāpajjhampi (Ka.); see M. Ni. 2.81], generates a verbal formation… a mental formation that is both hurtful and unhurtful. Having generated a bodily formation that is both hurtful and unhurtful, a verbal formation… a mental formation that is both hurtful and unhurtful, they are reborn in a world that is both hurtful and unhurtful. When they have been reborn in a world that is both hurtful and unhurtful, contacts that are both hurtful and unhurtful touch them. Touched by contacts that are both hurtful and unhurtful, they feel a feeling that is both hurtful and unhurtful, a mixture of pleasure and pain, like human beings, some gods and some beings in the lower world. Thus, Puṇṇa, a being is reborn from a being: one is reborn through what one does, and when one has been reborn, contacts touch one. That is why I say, Puṇṇa, that beings are heirs of their actions" [M. Ni. 2.81]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "action is one thing and the accumulation of action another."
The Discussion of the Accumulation of Action is finished.
The Fifteenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
Conditionality is rigidly fixed; dependent arising; time; moment, instant, short period; the four taints are free of taints; the ageing and death of world-transcending states is world-transcending; the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is world-transcending; the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling is worldly; one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling could die; that very path for rebirth among the beings without perception; action is one thing and the accumulation of action another.
The Third Set of Fifty.
Here is its summary:
The underlying tendencies, restraint, the aeon, the root, and the rigidly fixed. ^5-742

### The Sixteenth Chapter ^5-24-0

#### (156) 1. Discussion of Restraining ^5-24-1-0

Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. Does one person restrain another person's mind, saying "Do not be impassioned", "Do not be corrupted", "Do not be deluded", "Do not be defiled"? That should not be said… Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. Does one person restrain another person's contact that has arisen, saying "Let it not cease"? That should not be said… Does one person restrain another person's feeling that has arisen… perception that has arisen… intention that has arisen… mind that has arisen… faith that has arisen… energy that has arisen… mindfulness that has arisen… concentration that has arisen… wisdom that has arisen, saying "Let it not cease"? That should not be said…
Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. Does one person abandon greed for the sake of another… abandon hatred… abandon lack of moral fear for the sake of another? That should not be said…
Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. Does one person develop the path for the sake of another… develop a foundation of mindfulness… develop a factor of awakening for the sake of another? That should not be said…
Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. Does one person, for the sake of another, fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation and develop the path? That should not be said…
Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. Is one the doer for another; is pleasure and pain made by another; does one person do and another experience? That should not be said…
Does one person restrain another person's mind? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"By oneself alone is evil done, by oneself is one defiled;
by oneself is evil left undone, by oneself alone is one purified;
purity and impurity are one's own affair — no one can purify another" [Dha. Pa. 165]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "one person restrains another person's mind." ^5-743

Should it not be said that "one person restrains another person's mind"? Yes. But aren't there those who have attained power, and aren't there those who have achieved mastery? Yes. If there are those who have attained power and those who have achieved mastery, then surely you must also say: "One person restrains another person's mind."
The Discussion of Restraining is finished. ^5-744

#### The Sixteenth Chapter ^5-24-2-0

##### (157) 2. Discussion of Upholding ^5-24-2-1-0

Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Does one person uphold another person's mind, saying "Do not be impassioned", "Do not be corrupted", "Do not be deluded", "Do not be defiled"? That should not be said… Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Does one person produce in another non-greed as a wholesome root… produce non-hatred as a wholesome root… produce non-delusion as a wholesome root… produce faith… produce energy… produce mindfulness… produce concentration… produce wisdom? That should not be said… Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Does one person uphold another person's contact that has arisen, saying "Let it not cease"? That should not be said… Does one person uphold another person's feeling that has arisen… wisdom that has arisen, saying "Let it not cease"? That should not be said…
