Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Does one person abandon greed for the sake of another… abandon hatred… abandon delusion… abandon lack of moral fear for the sake of another? That should not be said…
Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Does one person develop the path for the sake of another… develop a foundation of mindfulness… develop a factor of awakening for the sake of another? That should not be said…
Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Does one person, for the sake of another, fully understand suffering… develop the path? That should not be said…
Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. Is one the doer for another; is pleasure and pain made by another; does one person do and another experience? That should not be said…
Does one person uphold another person's mind? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "By oneself alone is evil done… no one can purify another"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "one person upholds another person's mind." ^5-745

Should it not be said that "one person upholds another person's mind"? Yes. But aren't there those who have attained power, and aren't there those who have achieved mastery? Yes. If there are those who have attained power and those who have achieved mastery, then surely you must also say: "One person upholds another person's mind."
The Discussion of Upholding is finished. ^5-746

#### The Sixteenth Chapter ^5-24-3-0

##### (158) 3. Discussion of Giving Happiness ^5-24-3-1-0

Does one person give happiness to another? Yes. Does one person give pain to another? That should not be said… Does one person not give pain to another? Yes. Does one person not give happiness to another? That should not be said… Does one person give happiness to another? Yes. Does one person give another their own happiness, give the happiness of others, give that other person's own happiness? That should not be said… Does one person give another neither their own happiness, nor the happiness of others, nor that other person's own happiness? Yes. If one person gives another neither their own happiness, nor the happiness of others, nor that other person's own happiness, then surely you must not say: "One person gives happiness to another."
Does one person give happiness to another? Yes. Is one the doer for another; is pleasure and pain made by another; does one person do and another experience? That should not be said… ^5-747

Should it not be said that "one person gives happiness to another"? Yes. But didn't the venerable Udāyī say this: "Indeed the Blessed One has removed many painful things from us; indeed the Blessed One has brought many pleasant things to us; indeed the Blessed One has removed many unwholesome things from us; indeed the Blessed One has brought many wholesome things to us" [M. Ni. 2.148, in the Simile of the Quail Discourse]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one person gives happiness to another.
The Discussion of Giving Happiness is finished. ^5-748

#### The Sixteenth Chapter ^5-24-4-0

##### (159) 4. Discussion of Attending All at Once ^5-24-4-1-0

Does one attend to things all at once? Yes. Does one understand that mind by that same mind? That should not be said… Does one understand that mind by that same mind? Yes. Does one understand that mind as "mind" by that same mind? That should not be said… Does one understand that mind as "mind" by that same mind? Yes. Is that mind the object of that same mind? That should not be said…
Is that mind the object of that same mind? Yes. Does one contact that contact by that same contact, feel… by that same feeling… by that same perception… by that same intention… by that same mind… by that same thinking… by that same examining… by that same joy… by that same mindfulness… understand that wisdom by that same wisdom? That should not be said… ^5-749

#### The Sixteenth Chapter ^5-24-9-0

Is there material form belonging to the realm of form? Yes. That should not be said… But isn't it the case that it does not seek attainment, does not seek rebirth, is not a pleasant dwelling in this very life, and is not accompanied by, arisen together with, mixed with, associated with, does not arise together with, cease together with, have the same base and the same object as a mind that seeks attainment, a mind that seeks rebirth, a mind of pleasant dwelling in this very life? Yes. If it does not seek attainment, does not seek rebirth, is not a pleasant dwelling in this very life, and is not accompanied by a mind that seeks attainment… and does not have the same object, then surely you must not say: "There is material form belonging to the realm of form." ^5-768

Is there material form belonging to the formless realm? Yes. The Sixteenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
Restraining the mind, upholding the mind, giving happiness, attending all at once, material form is a root, material form has roots, material form is wholesome as well as unwholesome, material form is a result, there is material form belonging to the realm of form and there is material form belonging to the formless realm, all defilements are included in the sense-desire realm. ^5-775

### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-0

#### (166) 1. Discussion of a Worthy One's Accumulation of Merit ^5-25-1-0

Does a worthy one (arahant) have an accumulation of merit? Yes. Does a worthy one have an accumulation of demerit? That should not be said… Does a worthy one have no accumulation of demerit? Yes. Does a worthy one have no accumulation of merit? That should not be said… ^5-776

Does a worthy one have an accumulation of merit? Yes. Does a worthy one generate a meritorious formation, generate an imperturbable formation, perform action that leads to a destination, perform action that leads to existence, perform action that leads to sovereignty, perform action that leads to lordship [variant: ādhipaccasaṃvattanikaṃ (?)], perform action that leads to great wealth, perform action that leads to a large retinue, perform action that leads to the splendour of the gods, perform action that leads to the splendour of human beings? That should not be said… ^5-777

Does a worthy one have an accumulation of merit? Yes. Does a worthy one build up? That should not be said… Does a worthy one tear down? That should not be said… Does a worthy one abandon… Does a worthy one cling… Does a worthy one scatter… Does a worthy one bind together… Does a worthy one put out… Does a worthy one kindle? That should not be said… But doesn't a worthy one neither build up nor tear down, but stand having torn down? Yes. If a worthy one neither builds up nor tears down, but stands having torn down, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one has an accumulation of merit."
But doesn't a worthy one neither abandon nor cling, but stand having abandoned; neither scatter nor bind together, but stand having scattered; neither put out nor kindle, but stand having put out? Yes. If a worthy one neither puts out nor kindles, but stands having put out, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one has an accumulation of merit." ^5-778

Does a worthy one have no accumulation of merit? Yes. Would a worthy one give a gift? Yes. If a worthy one would give a gift, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one has no accumulation of merit."
Would a worthy one give robes… give almsfood… give lodgings… give medicines and requisites for the sick… give food to chew… give meals… give drink… pay homage to a shrine… offer a garland at a shrine… offer scents… offer ointments… walk around a shrine keeping it on their right [variant: padakkhiṇaṃ (?)]? Yes. If a worthy one would walk around a shrine keeping it on their right, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one has no accumulation of merit."
The Discussion of "A Worthy One Has an Accumulation of Merit" is finished. ^5-779

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-2-0

##### (167) 2. Discussion of "There Is No Untimely Death for a Worthy One" ^5-25-2-1-0

Is there no untimely death for a worthy one (arahant)? Yes. Is there no killer of a worthy one? That should not be said… Is there a killer of a worthy one? Yes. Is there untimely death for a worthy one? That should not be said… Is there no untimely death for a worthy one? Yes. When someone deprives a worthy one of life, do they deprive them of life while there is life and a remainder of life, or do they deprive them of life while there is no life and no remainder of life? They deprive them of life while there is life and a remainder of life. If they deprive them of life while there is life and a remainder of life, then surely you must not say: "There is no untimely death for a worthy one." Since they deprive them of life while there is no life and no remainder of life, is there no killer of a worthy one? That should not be said… ^5-780

Is there no untimely death for a worthy one? Yes. Could poison not affect, could a weapon not affect, could fire not affect the body of a worthy one? That should not be said… But couldn't poison affect, couldn't a weapon affect, couldn't fire affect the body of a worthy one? Yes. If poison could affect, a weapon could affect and fire could affect the body of a worthy one, then surely you must not say: "There is no untimely death for a worthy one."
Could poison not affect, could a weapon not affect, could fire not affect the body of a worthy one? Yes. Is there no killer of a worthy one? That should not be said… ^5-781

Is there untimely death for a worthy one? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, I do not say that intentional actions that have been done and accumulated come to an end without their result having been experienced — and that either in this very life, or in the next rebirth, or on some later occasion"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is no untimely death for a worthy one.
The Discussion of "There Is No Untimely Death for a Worthy One" is finished. ^5-782

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-3-0

##### (168) 3. Discussion of "All This Is Due to Action" ^5-25-3-1-0

Is all this due to action? Yes. Is action too due to action? That should not be said… Is all this due to action? Yes. Is all this caused by what was done in the past? That should not be said… Is all this due to action? Yes. Is all this due to the result of action? That should not be said… ^5-783

Is all this due to the result of action? Yes. Would one kill a living being as a result of action? Yes. Does killing living beings have fruit? Yes. Does the result of action have fruit? That should not be said… Is the result of action without fruit? Yes. Is killing living beings without fruit? That should not be said…
Would one, as a result of action, take what is not given… speak falsely… speak divisively… speak harshly… engage in idle chatter… break into houses… carry off plunder… rob a single house… lie in ambush on the highway… go to another's wife… destroy a village… destroy a town… would one, as a result of action, give a gift… give robes… give almsfood… give lodgings… give medicines and requisites for the sick? Yes. Do medicines and requisites for the sick have fruit? Yes. Does the result of action have fruit? That should not be said… Is the result of action without fruit? Yes. Are medicines and requisites for the sick without fruit? That should not be said… ^5-784

Should it not be said that "all this is due to action"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"By action the world goes on [variant: vattati (Pī., Ka., M. Ni. 2.460), vattate (?)], by action people go on [variant: vattati (Pī., Ka., M. Ni. 2.460), vattate (?)];
beings are bound by action, as a moving chariot is held by its linchpin [M. Ni. 2.460; Su. Ni. 659].
"By action one gains fame and praise,
by action loss, slaughter and bondage;
knowing that action works in these different ways,
how could one say in the world, ‘There is no action’?"
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case "all this is due to action."
The Discussion of "All This Is Due to Action" is finished. ^5-785

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-4-0

##### (169) 4. Discussion of What Is Bound Up with the Faculties ^5-25-4-1-0

Is only what is bound up with the faculties suffering? Yes. Is only what is bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? That should not be said… But isn't what is not bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. If what is not bound up with the faculties is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change, then surely you must not say: "Only what is bound up with the faculties is suffering."
Is what is not bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen… subject to change, and yet not suffering? Yes. Is what is bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned… subject to change, and yet not suffering? That should not be said…
Is what is bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned… subject to change, and is it suffering [this pair of questions should come before the previous pair]? Yes. Is what is not bound up with the faculties impermanent, conditioned… subject to change, and is it suffering [this pair of questions should come before the previous pair]? That should not be said… ^5-786

Is only what is bound up with the faculties suffering? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One said that what is impermanent is suffering [S. Ni. 3.15], and isn't "what is not bound up with the faculties impermanent"? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that what is impermanent is suffering [S. Ni. 3.15], and what is not bound up with the faculties is impermanent, then surely you must not say: "Only what is bound up with the faculties is suffering." ^5-787

Should it not be said that "only what is bound up with the faculties is suffering"? Yes. Just as the holy life (the life of spiritual training) is lived under the Blessed One for the full understanding of suffering bound up with the faculties, so too is the holy life lived under the Blessed One for the full understanding of suffering not bound up with the faculties? That should not be said… Just as suffering bound up with the faculties, once fully understood, does not arise again, so too does suffering not bound up with the faculties, once fully understood, not arise again? That should not be said. In that case only what is bound up with the faculties is suffering.
The Discussion of What Is Bound Up with the Faculties is finished. ^5-788

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-5-0

##### (170) 5. Discussion of "Except for the Noble Path" ^5-25-5-1-0

Except for the noble path, are the remaining formations (conditioned things) suffering? Yes. Is the origin of suffering also suffering? That should not be said… Is the origin of suffering also suffering? Yes. Are there only three noble truths? That should not be said… Are there only three noble truths? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared four noble truths — suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the way leading to the cessation of suffering? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared four noble truths — suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the way leading to the cessation of suffering — then surely you must not say: "There are only three noble truths."
Is the origin of suffering also suffering? Yes. How so? In the sense of being impermanent. Is the noble path impermanent? Yes. Is the noble path suffering? That should not be said…
Is the noble path impermanent, and yet not suffering? Yes. Is the origin of suffering impermanent, and yet not suffering? That should not be said… Is the origin of suffering impermanent, and is it suffering? Yes. Is the noble path impermanent, and is it suffering? That should not be said… ^5-789

Should it not be said that "except for the noble path, the remaining formations are suffering"? Yes. But isn't that the way leading to the cessation of suffering? Yes. If that is the way leading to the cessation of suffering, then surely you must also say: "Except for the noble path, the remaining formations are suffering."
The Discussion of "Except for the Noble Path" is finished. ^5-790

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-6-0

##### (171) 6. Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That the Community Receives Offerings" ^5-25-6-1-0

Should it not be said that "the Community receives offerings"? Yes. But isn't the Community worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If the Community is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then surely you must also say: "The Community receives offerings."
Should it not be said that "the Community receives offerings"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings, then surely you must also say: "The Community receives offerings."
Should it not be said that "the Community receives offerings"? Yes. But aren't there some who give gifts to the Community? Yes. If there are some who give gifts to the Community, then surely you must also say: "The Community receives offerings." But aren't there some who give robes to the Community… give almsfood… give lodgings… give medicines and requisites for the sick… give food to chew… give meals… give drink? Yes. If there are some who give drink to the Community, then surely you must also say: "The Community receives offerings."
Should it not be said that "the Community receives offerings"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"As fire receives the oblation, as the earth receives a great rain cloud,
so the Community, accomplished in concentration, receives offerings"?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the Community receives offerings. ^5-791

Does the Community receive offerings? Yes. Does the path receive them, does the fruit receive them? That should not be said…
The Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That the Community Receives Offerings" is finished. ^5-792

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-7-0

##### (172) 7. Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That the Community Purifies Offerings" ^5-25-7-1-0

Should it not be said that "the Community purifies offerings"? Yes. But isn't the Community worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If the Community is worthy of gifts… the unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then surely you must also say: "The Community purifies offerings."
Should it not be said that "the Community purifies offerings"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings, then surely you must also say: "The Community purifies offerings."
Should it not be said that "the Community purifies offerings"? Yes. But aren't there some who, having given a gift to the Community, make their offering succeed? Yes. If there are some who, having given a gift to the Community, make their offering succeed, then surely you must also say: "The Community purifies offerings."
But aren't there some who, having given robes to the Community… having given almsfood… having given lodgings… having given medicines and requisites for the sick… having given food to chew… having given meals… having given drink, make their offering succeed? Yes. If there are some who, having given drink to the Community, make their offering succeed, then surely you must also say: "The Community purifies offerings." ^5-793

Does the Community purify offerings? Yes. Does the path purify them, does the fruit purify them? That should not be said…
The Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That the Community Purifies Offerings" is finished. ^5-794

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-8-0

##### (173) 8. Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That the Community Eats" ^5-25-8-1-0

Should it not be said that "the Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes"? Yes. But aren't there some who provide meals for the Community, provide meals for designated monks, and provide rice gruel and drinks? Yes. If there are some who provide meals for the Community, provide meals for designated monks, and provide rice gruel and drinks, then surely you must also say: "The Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes."
Should it not be said that "the Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One spoken of "eating in a group, eating out of turn, food that is left over, food that is not left over"? Yes. If the Blessed One has spoken of "eating in a group, eating out of turn, food that is left over, food that is not left over," then surely you must also say: "The Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes."
Should it not be said that "the Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared eight kinds of drink — mango drink, rose-apple drink, drink of seeded bananas, drink of seedless bananas, madhuka drink [variant: madhupānaṃ (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.); but see Mahāva. 300], grape drink, lotus-root drink and phārusaka-berry drink? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared eight kinds of drink — mango drink, rose-apple drink, drink of seeded bananas, drink of seedless bananas, madhuka drink, grape drink, lotus-root drink and phārusaka-berry drink — then surely you must also say: "The Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes." ^5-795

Does the Community eat, drink, chew and taste? Yes. Does the path eat, drink, chew and taste; does the fruit eat, drink, chew and taste? That should not be said…
The Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That the Community Eats" is finished. ^5-796

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-9-0

##### (174) 9. Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Community Is of Great Fruit" ^5-25-9-1-0

Should it not be said that "what is given to the Community is of great fruit"? Yes. But isn't the Community worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If the Community is worthy of gifts… the unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then surely you must also say: "What is given to the Community is of great fruit."
Should it not be said that "what is given to the Community is of great fruit"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings, then surely you must also say: "What is given to the Community is of great fruit." ^5-797

Should it not be said that "what is given to the Community is of great fruit"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Give it to the Community, Gotamī; when you give it to the Community, both I and the Community will be honoured" [M. Ni. 3.376]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case what is given to the Community is of great fruit.
Should it not be said that "what is given to the Community is of great fruit"? Yes. But didn't Sakka, lord of the gods, say this to the Blessed One:
"For people who make offerings, for living beings who seek merit,
who make merit bound up with attachments — where is what is given of great fruit?
"The four who are practising and the four established in the fruit —
this Community is upright, possessed of wisdom and virtue.
"For people who make offerings, for living beings who seek merit,
who make merit bound up with attachments, what is given to the Community is of great fruit" [S. Ni. 1.262; Vi. Va. 642, 751].
"For this Community is vast and exalted,
immeasurable like the ocean, the sea;
these are the best, the disciples of the hero among men [variant: narasīhasāvakā (Ka.)];
bringers of light, they proclaim the Dhamma.
"For them it is well given, well offered, well sacrificed,
those who give a gift with the Community in mind;
that offering, gone to the Community, is well established,
of great fruit, praised by the knowers of the world.
"Recollecting such a sacrifice,
those who go about [variant: viharanti (Sī., Ka.)] in the world filled with joy,
having removed the stain of stinginess together with its root,
blameless, go to a heavenly place" [Vi. Va. 645, 754]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case what is given to the Community is of great fruit.
The Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Community Is of Great Fruit" is finished. ^5-798

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-10-0

##### (175) 10. Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Buddha Is of Great Fruit" ^5-25-10-1-0

Should it not be said that "what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit"? Yes. But isn't the Blessed One the foremost of two-footed beings, the best of two-footed beings, the chief of two-footed beings, the highest of two-footed beings, the most excellent of two-footed beings, unequalled, equal to the unequalled, without counterpart, without peer, without rival? Yes. If the Blessed One is the foremost of two-footed beings, the best of two-footed beings, the chief of two-footed beings, the highest of two-footed beings, the most excellent of two-footed beings, unequalled, equal to the unequalled, without counterpart, without peer, without rival, then surely you must also say: "What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit."
Should it not be said that "what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit"? Yes. Is there anyone equal to the Buddha in virtue, concentration and wisdom? There is not. If there is no one equal to the Buddha in virtue, concentration and wisdom, then surely you must also say: "What is given to the Buddha is of great fruit."
Should it not be said that "what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Neither in this world nor in the next
is anyone found who is better than or equal to the Buddha,
who has reached the foremost place among those worthy of gifts,
for those who seek merit and look for abundant fruit" [Vi. Va. 1047]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case what is given to the Buddha is of great fruit.
The Discussion of "It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Buddha Is of Great Fruit" is finished. ^5-799

#### The Seventeenth Chapter ^5-25-11-0

##### (176) 11. Discussion of the Purification of Offerings ^5-25-11-1-0

Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But aren't there some recipients who are worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world? Yes. If there are some recipients who are worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then surely you must not say: "A gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient."
Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of individuals, are worthy of offerings, then surely you must not say: "A gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient."
Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But aren't there some who, having given a gift to a stream-enterer, make their offering succeed? Yes. If there are some who, having given a gift to a stream-enterer, make their offering succeed, then surely you must not say: "A gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient."
But aren't there some who, having given a gift to a once-returner… to a non-returner… to a worthy one (arahant), make their offering succeed? Yes. If there are some who, having given a gift to a worthy one, make their offering succeed, then surely you must not say: "A gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient." ^5-800

Is a gift purified by the recipient? Yes. Is one the doer for another; is pleasure and pain made by another; does one person do and another experience? That should not be said…
Is a gift purified only by the giver, not by the recipient? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Ānanda, there are these four kinds of purification of offerings. Which four? There is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified by the giver, not by the recipient; there is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified by the recipient, not by the giver; there is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified both by the giver and by the recipient; there is, Ānanda, an offering that is purified neither by the giver nor by the recipient. These, Ānanda, are the four kinds of purification of offerings" [M. Ni. 3.381]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "a gift is purified only by the giver, not by the recipient."
The Discussion of the Purification of Offerings is finished.
The Seventeenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
A worthy one has an accumulation of merit; there is no untimely death for a worthy one; all this is due to action; only what is bound up with the faculties is suffering; except for the noble path, the remaining formations are suffering; the Community receives offerings; the Community purifies offerings; the Community eats, drinks, chews and tastes; what is given to the Community is of great fruit; there is a gift for purification [variant: visujjhatīti (Syā.)]. ^5-801

### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-0

#### (177) 1. Discussion of the Human World ^5-26-1-0

Should it not be said that "the Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world"? Yes. But aren't there shrines, parks, monasteries, villages, towns, cities, kingdoms and countries where the Buddha lived? Yes. If there are shrines, parks, monasteries, villages, towns, cities, kingdoms and countries where the Buddha lived, then surely you must also say: "The Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world."
Should it not be said that "the Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world"? Yes. But wasn't the Blessed One born at Lumbinī, fully awakened at the foot of the tree of awakening; didn't the Blessed One set the wheel of the Dhamma rolling at Bārāṇasī, relinquish the formation of life (his remaining life span) at the Cāpāla shrine, and attain final nibbāna (final release) at Kusinārā? Yes. If the Blessed One was born at Lumbinī… attained final nibbāna at Kusinārā, then surely you must also say: "The Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world."
Should it not be said that "the Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, on one occasion I was staying at Ukkaṭṭhā, in the Subhaga Grove, at the foot of a royal sal tree" [D. Ni. 2.91]; "Monks, on one occasion I was staying at Uruvelā, at the goatherds' banyan tree, when I had just become fully awakened" [A. Ni. 4.21]; "Monks, on one occasion I was staying at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels' feeding ground" [D. Ni. 2.180]; "Monks, on one occasion I was staying at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's park"; "Monks, on one occasion I was staying at Vesālī, in the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof" [D. Ni. 3.11]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world. ^5-802

Did the Buddha, the Blessed One, stay in the human world? Yes. But wasn't the Blessed One born in the world, didn't he grow up in the world, and doesn't he dwell having overcome the world, unstained by the world [A. Ni. 4.36]? Yes. If the Blessed One was born in the world, grew up in the world, and dwells having overcome the world, unstained by the world, then surely you must not say: "The Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world."
The Discussion of the Human World is finished. ^5-803

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-2-0

##### (178) 2. Discussion of the Teaching of the Dhamma ^5-26-2-1-0

Should it not be said that "the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One"? Yes. By whom was it taught? It was taught by a created figure. Is the created figure a conqueror, a teacher, a Fully Awakened Buddha, all-knowing, all-seeing, the lord of the Dhamma, the final authority on the Dhamma? That should not be said…
Should it not be said that "the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One"? Yes. By whom was it taught? It was taught by the venerable Ānanda. Is the venerable Ānanda a conqueror, a teacher, a Fully Awakened Buddha, all-knowing, all-seeing, the lord of the Dhamma, the final authority on the Dhamma? That should not be said… ^5-804

Should it not be said that "the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Sāriputta, I might teach the Dhamma in brief; Sāriputta, I might teach the Dhamma in detail; Sāriputta, I might teach the Dhamma both in brief and in detail; but those who understand are hard to find" [A. Ni. 3.33, in the Sāriputta Discourse]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One. ^5-805

Should it not be said that "the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "‘Monks, I teach the Dhamma through direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge; monks, I teach the Dhamma with a basis, not without a basis; monks, I teach the Dhamma with wonders, not without wonders. Since I [variant: yañcassa (Sī., Pī., Ka.)], monks, teach the Dhamma through direct knowledge and not without direct knowledge, teach the Dhamma with a basis and not without a basis, teach the Dhamma with wonders and not without wonders, it is fitting for me to give instruction, fitting to give guidance. And this is enough, monks, for you to be satisfied, enough to be pleased, enough to be glad: the Blessed One is fully awakened, the Dhamma is well proclaimed, the Community is practising well.’ And while this explanation was being spoken, the ten-thousandfold world system shook" [A. Ni. 3.126]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One.
The Discussion of the Teaching of the Dhamma is finished. ^5-806

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-3-0

##### (179) 3. Discussion of Compassion ^5-26-3-1-0

Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no loving-kindness? That should not be said… Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no sympathetic joy… no equanimity? That should not be said…
Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have loving-kindness? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have compassion? That should not be said… Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have sympathetic joy… equanimity? Yes. Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have compassion? That should not be said…
Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. Is the Blessed One without compassion? That should not be said… But isn't the Blessed One compassionate, devoted to the welfare of the world, sympathetic to the world, acting for the good of the world? Yes. If the Blessed One is compassionate, devoted to the welfare of the world, sympathetic to the world, acting for the good of the world, then surely you must not say: "The Buddha, the Blessed One, has no compassion."…
Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have no compassion? Yes. But didn't the Blessed One enter the attainment of great compassion? Yes. If the Blessed One entered the attainment of great compassion, then surely you must not say: "The Buddha, the Blessed One, has no compassion." ^5-807

Does the Buddha, the Blessed One, have compassion? Yes. Does the Blessed One have greed? That should not be said. In that case the Buddha, the Blessed One, has no compassion.
The Discussion of Compassion is finished. ^5-808

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-4-0

##### (180) 4. Discussion of Fragrant Substances ^5-26-4-1-0

Do the excrement and urine of the Buddha, the Blessed One, far surpass other fragrant substances? Yes. Does the Blessed One feed on fragrances? That should not be said… But doesn't the Blessed One eat rice and gruel? Yes. If the Blessed One eats rice and gruel, then surely you must not say: "The excrement and urine of the Buddha, the Blessed One, far surpass other fragrant substances."
Do the excrement and urine of the Buddha, the Blessed One, far surpass other fragrant substances? Yes. Are there some who bathe in the excrement and urine of the Buddha, the Blessed One, anoint themselves with it, rub themselves with it [variant: uccārenti (Sī., Pī., Ka.)], store it in a basket, put it away in a box, display it in the market, and use that scent for what a scent is used for? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Fragrant Substances is finished. ^5-809

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-5-0

##### (181) 5. Discussion of a Single Path ^5-26-5-1-0

Does one realize the four fruits of the ascetic life by a single noble path? Yes. Is there a coming together of four contacts… of four perceptions? That should not be said… Does one realize the four fruits of the ascetic life by a single noble path? Yes. By the path of stream-entry? That should not be said… By the path of once-returning… by the path of non-returning? That should not be said…
By which path? By the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one). Does one abandon identity view, doubt and clinging to rules and rituals by the path of arahantship? That should not be said… Does one abandon identity view, doubt and clinging to rules and rituals by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the abandoning of the three fetters to be the fruit of stream-entry? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the abandoning of the three fetters to be the fruit of stream-entry, then surely you must not say: "One abandons identity view, doubt and clinging to rules and rituals by the path of arahantship."
Does one abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will by the path of arahantship? That should not be said… Does one abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the weakening of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of once-returning? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the weakening of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of once-returning, then surely you must not say: "One abandons gross sensual desire and gross ill will by the path of arahantship."
Does one abandon even subtle sensual desire and even subtle ill will by the path of arahantship? That should not be said… Does one abandon even subtle sensual desire and even subtle ill will by the path of arahantship? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the abandoning without remainder of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of non-returning? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the abandoning without remainder of sensual desire and ill will to be the fruit of non-returning, then surely you must not say: "One abandons even subtle sensual desire and even subtle ill will by the path of arahantship." ^5-810

Should it not be said that "one realizes the four fruits of the ascetic life by a single noble path"? Yes. Has the Blessed One developed the path of stream-entry? Yes. Is the Blessed One a stream-enterer? That should not be said… Has the Blessed One developed the path of once-returning… the path of non-returning? Yes. Is the Blessed One a non-returner? That should not be said… ^5-811

Does the Blessed One realize the four fruits of the ascetic life by a single noble path, while disciples realize the four fruits of the ascetic life by four noble paths? Yes. Do disciples see what the Buddha, the Blessed One, has not seen, reach what he has not reached, realize what he has not realized? That should not be said…
The Discussion of a Single Path is finished. ^5-812

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-6-0

##### (182) 6. Discussion of Passing from One Meditative Absorption to Another ^5-26-6-1-0

Does one pass from one meditative absorption (jhāna) to another? Yes. Does one pass from the first meditative absorption to the third meditative absorption? That should not be said… Does one pass from one meditative absorption to another? Yes. Does one pass from the second meditative absorption to the fourth meditative absorption? That should not be said…
Does one pass from the first meditative absorption to the second meditative absorption? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the first meditative absorption the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the second meditative absorption? That should not be said…
One passes from the first meditative absorption to the second meditative absorption — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the first meditative absorption is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the second meditative absorption"? Yes. Does the second meditative absorption arise for one who does not turn the mind to it… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't the second meditative absorption arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If the second meditative absorption arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "One passes from the first meditative absorption to the second meditative absorption."…
Does one pass from the first meditative absorption to the second meditative absorption? Yes. Does the first meditative absorption arise for one who attends to sensual pleasures as dangerous? Yes. Does the second meditative absorption arise for one who attends to sensual pleasures as dangerous? That should not be said…
Is the first meditative absorption with thinking and examining? Yes. Is the second meditative absorption with thinking and examining? That should not be said… Does one pass from the first meditative absorption to the second meditative absorption? Yes. Is that very first meditative absorption the second meditative absorption? That should not be said… ^5-813

Does one pass from the second meditative absorption to the third meditative absorption? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the second meditative absorption the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the third meditative absorption? That should not be said…
One passes from the second meditative absorption to the third meditative absorption — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the second meditative absorption is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the third meditative absorption"? Yes. Does the third meditative absorption arise for one who does not turn the mind to it… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't the third meditative absorption arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If the third meditative absorption arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "One passes from the second meditative absorption to the third meditative absorption."
Does one pass from the second meditative absorption to the third meditative absorption? Yes. Does the second meditative absorption arise for one who attends to thinking and examining as dangerous? Yes. Does the third meditative absorption arise for one who attends to thinking and examining as dangerous? That should not be said…
Is the second meditative absorption with joy? Yes. Is the third meditative absorption with joy? That should not be said… Does one pass from the second meditative absorption to the third meditative absorption? Yes. Is that very second meditative absorption the third meditative absorption? That should not be said… ^5-814

Does one pass from the third meditative absorption to the fourth meditative absorption? Yes. Is the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the third meditative absorption the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the fourth meditative absorption? That should not be said…
One passes from the third meditative absorption to the fourth meditative absorption — should it not be said that "the turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the third meditative absorption is the very same turning of the mind… aspiration for the arising of the fourth meditative absorption"? Yes. Does the fourth meditative absorption arise for one who does not turn the mind to it… for one who does not aspire? That should not be said… But doesn't the fourth meditative absorption arise for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires? Yes. If the fourth meditative absorption arises for one who turns the mind to it… for one who aspires, then surely you must not say: "One passes from the third meditative absorption to the fourth meditative absorption."
Does one pass from the third meditative absorption to the fourth meditative absorption? Yes. Does the third meditative absorption arise for one who attends to joy as dangerous? Yes. Does the fourth meditative absorption arise for one who attends to joy as dangerous? That should not be said…
Is the third meditative absorption accompanied by happiness? Yes. Is the fourth meditative absorption accompanied by happiness? That should not be said… Does one pass from the third meditative absorption to the fourth meditative absorption? Yes. Is that very third meditative absorption the fourth meditative absorption? That should not be said… ^5-815

Should it not be said that "one passes from one meditative absorption to another"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, monks, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures… enters and dwells in the fourth meditative absorption" [A. Ni. 2.13; 4.163]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one passes from one meditative absorption to another.
The Discussion of Passing from One Meditative Absorption to Another is finished. ^5-816

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-7-0

##### (183) 7. Discussion of the Interval between Meditative Absorptions ^5-26-7-1-0

Is there an interval between meditative absorptions (jhānas)? Yes. Is there an interval between contacts… an interval between perceptions? That should not be said…
Is there an interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is there an interval between meditative absorptions in between the second and the third meditative absorption? That should not be said…
Is there an interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is there an interval between meditative absorptions in between the third and the fourth meditative absorption? That should not be said…
Is there no interval between meditative absorptions in between the second and the third meditative absorption? Yes. If there is no interval between meditative absorptions in between the second and the third meditative absorption, then surely you must not say: "There is an interval between meditative absorptions."
Is there no interval between meditative absorptions in between the third and the fourth meditative absorption? Yes. If there is no interval between meditative absorptions in between the third and the fourth meditative absorption, then surely you must not say: "There is an interval between meditative absorptions." ^5-817

Is there an interval between meditative absorptions in between the first and the second meditative absorption? Yes. Is there an interval between meditative absorptions in between the second and the third meditative absorption? That should not be said…
Is there an interval between meditative absorptions in between the first and the second meditative absorption? Yes. Is there an interval between meditative absorptions in between the third and the fourth meditative absorption? That should not be said…
Is there no interval between meditative absorptions in between the second and the third meditative absorption? Yes. Is there no interval between meditative absorptions in between the first and the second meditative absorption? That should not be said…
Is there no interval between meditative absorptions in between the third and the fourth meditative absorption? Yes. Is there no interval between meditative absorptions in between the first and the second meditative absorption? That should not be said… ^5-818

Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, the interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is concentration with thinking and examining the interval between meditative absorptions? That should not be said…
Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, the interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is concentration without thinking and without examining the interval between meditative absorptions? That should not be said…
Is concentration with thinking and examining not the interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, not the interval between meditative absorptions? That should not be said…
Is concentration without thinking and without examining not the interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, not the interval between meditative absorptions? That should not be said… ^5-819

Is there concentration without thinking, with examining only, in between two meditative absorptions that are present? Yes. But when concentration without thinking, with examining only, is occurring, hasn't the first meditative absorption ceased and the second meditative absorption become present? Yes. If, when concentration without thinking, with examining only, is occurring, the first meditative absorption has ceased and the second meditative absorption has become present, then surely you must not say: "Concentration without thinking, with examining only, in between two meditative absorptions that are present, is the interval between meditative absorptions." ^5-820

Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, not the interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, the first meditative absorption… the second meditative absorption… the third meditative absorption… the fourth meditative absorption? That should not be said. In that case concentration without thinking, with examining only, is the interval between meditative absorptions. ^5-821

Is concentration without thinking, with examining only, the interval between meditative absorptions? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared three kinds of concentration — concentration with thinking and examining, concentration without thinking, with examining only, and concentration without thinking and without examining [D. Ni. 3.305, 353]? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared three kinds of concentration — concentration with thinking… without examining — then surely you must not say: "Concentration without thinking, with examining only, is the interval between meditative absorptions."
The Discussion of the Interval between Meditative Absorptions is finished. ^5-822

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-8-0

##### (184) 8. Discussion of "One Hears Sound" ^5-26-8-1-0

Does one in a meditative attainment hear sound? Yes. Does one in a meditative attainment see a visible form with the eye… with the ear… with the nose… with the tongue… feel a touch with the body? That should not be said…
Does one in a meditative attainment hear sound? Yes. Is one possessing ear-consciousness in a meditative attainment? That should not be said. But isn't concentration found in one possessing mind-consciousness? Yes. If concentration is found in one possessing mind-consciousness, then surely you must not say: "One in a meditative attainment hears sound."
Is concentration found in one possessing mind-consciousness, while one possessing ear-consciousness hears sound? Yes. If concentration is found in one possessing mind-consciousness, while one possessing ear-consciousness hears sound, then surely you must not say: "One in a meditative attainment hears sound." Is concentration found in one possessing mind-consciousness, while one possessing ear-consciousness hears sound? Yes. Is there a coming together of two contacts… of two states of mind? That should not be said… ^5-823

Should it not be said that "one in a meditative attainment hears sound"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One said that sound is a thorn to the first meditative absorption (jhāna)? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first meditative absorption, then surely you must also say: "One in a meditative attainment hears sound." ^5-824

Since the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first meditative absorption, does one in a meditative attainment hear sound? Yes. The Blessed One has said that thinking and examining are a thorn to the second meditative absorption — does that one have thinking and examining? That should not be said…
Since the Blessed One has said that sound is a thorn to the first meditative absorption, does one in a meditative attainment hear sound? Yes. The Blessed One has said that joy is a thorn to the third meditative absorption… that in-and-out breathing is a thorn to the fourth meditative absorption… that the perception of material form is a thorn for one who has entered the base of the infinity of space… that the perception of the base of the infinity of space is a thorn for one who has entered the base of the infinity of consciousness… that the perception of the base of the infinity of consciousness is a thorn for one who has entered the base of nothingness… that the perception of the base of nothingness is a thorn for one who has entered the base of neither perception nor non-perception… that perception and feeling are a thorn for one who has entered the cessation of perception and feeling — does that one have perception and feeling? That should not be said…
The Discussion of "One Hears Sound" is finished. ^5-825

#### The Eighteenth Chapter ^5-26-9-0

##### (185) 9. Discussion of "One Sees a Visible Form with the Eye" ^5-26-9-1-0

Does one see a visible form with the eye? Yes. Does one see material form with material form? That should not be said… Does one see material form with material form? Yes. Does one cognize material form with material form? That should not be said… Does one cognize material form with material form? Yes. Is material form mind-consciousness? That should not be said… Does one see a visible form with the eye? Yes. Does the eye have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… But doesn't the eye have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. If the eye has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "One sees a visible form with the eye."
Does one hear a sound with the ear… smell a smell with the nose… taste a taste with the tongue… feel a touch with the body? Yes. Does one touch material form with material form? That should not be said…
Does one touch material form with material form? Yes. Does one cognize material form with material form? That should not be said… Does one cognize material form with material form? Yes. Is material form mind-consciousness? That should not be said… Does one feel a touch with the body? Yes. Does the body have turning of the mind… aspiration? That should not be said… But doesn't the body have no turning of the mind… aspiration? Yes. If the body has no turning of the mind… aspiration, then surely you must not say: "One feels a touch with the body."… ^5-826

Should it not be said that "one sees a visible form with the eye"… "one feels a touch with the body"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Here, monks, a monk sees a visible form with the eye… feels a touch with the body" [M. Ni. 1.349; A. Ni. 4.37 (see the commentary)]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one sees a visible form with the eye… feels a touch with the body.
The Discussion of "One Sees a Visible Form with the Eye" is finished.
The Eighteenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The Buddha, the Blessed One, stayed in the human world; the Dhamma was taught by the Buddha, the Blessed One; the Buddha, the Blessed One, has no compassion; the excrement and urine of the Buddha, the Blessed One, far surpass other fragrant substances; one realizes the four fruits of the ascetic life by a single noble path; one passes from one meditative absorption to another; there is an interval between meditative absorptions; one in a meditative attainment hears sound; one sees a visible form with the eye, feels a touch with the body. ^5-827

### The Nineteenth Chapter ^5-27-0

#### (186) 1. Discussion of Abandoning Defilements ^5-27-1-0

Does one abandon past defilements? Yes. Does one make cease what has ceased, make go what has gone, destroy what is destroyed, make vanish what has vanished, make completely vanish what has completely vanished? That should not be said… Does one abandon past defilements? Yes. But hasn't the past ceased? Yes. If the past has ceased, then surely you must not say: "One abandons past defilements." Does one abandon past defilements? Yes. But doesn't the past not exist? Yes. If the past does not exist, then surely you must not say: "One abandons past defilements." ^5-828

Does one abandon future defilements? Yes. Does one make unborn what is unborn, make unarisen what has not arisen, make unproduced what is not produced, make unmanifest what is not manifested? That should not be said… Does one abandon future defilements? Yes. But isn't the future unborn? Yes. If the future is unborn, then surely you must not say: "One abandons future defilements." Does one abandon future defilements? Yes. But doesn't the future not exist? Yes. If the future does not exist, then surely you must not say: "One abandons future defilements." ^5-829

Does one abandon present defilements? Yes. Does one who is impassioned abandon greed, one who is corrupted abandon hatred, one who is deluded abandon delusion, one who is defiled abandon defilements? That should not be said… Does one abandon greed by means of greed, hatred by means of hatred, delusion by means of delusion, defilements by means of defilements? That should not be said…
Is greed associated with the mind, and is the path associated with the mind? Yes. Is there a coming together of two states of mind? That should not be said…
Is greed unwholesome, and is the path wholesome? Yes. Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? That should not be said…
Do wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright states with their counterparts come face to face? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, there are these four things that are very far apart. Which four? The sky, monks, and the earth — this is the first thing that is very far apart… therefore the Dhamma of the good is far from the bad"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "wholesome and unwholesome… come face to face." ^5-830

Should it not be said that "one abandons past defilements, abandons future defilements, abandons present defilements"? Yes. Is there no abandoning of defilements? That should not be said… In that case one abandons past defilements, abandons future defilements, abandons present defilements.
The Discussion of Abandoning Defilements is finished. ^5-831

#### The Nineteenth Chapter ^5-27-2-0

##### (187) 2. Discussion of Emptiness ^5-27-2-1-0

Is emptiness included in the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Is the signless included in the aggregate of mental formations? That should not be said… Is emptiness included in the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Is the desireless included in the aggregate of mental formations? That should not be said… Should it not be said of the signless that "it is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? Yes. Should it not be said of emptiness that "it is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? That should not be said… Should it not be said of the desireless that "it is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? Yes. Should it not be said of emptiness that "it is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? That should not be said…
Is emptiness included in the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Is the aggregate of mental formations not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently arisen, not subject to destruction, not subject to passing away, not subject to fading, not subject to cessation, not subject to change? That should not be said… But isn't the aggregate of mental formations impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. If the aggregate of mental formations is impermanent… subject to change, then surely you must not say: "Emptiness is included in the aggregate of mental formations." ^5-832

Is the emptiness of the aggregate of material form included in the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Is the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations included in the aggregate of material form? That should not be said… Is the emptiness of the aggregate of feeling… of the aggregate of perception… of the aggregate of consciousness included in the aggregate of mental formations? Yes. Is the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations included in the aggregate of consciousness? That should not be said…
Should it not be said of the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations that "it is included in the aggregate of material form"? Yes. Should it not be said of the emptiness of the aggregate of material form that "it is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? That should not be said… Should it not be said of the emptiness of the aggregate of mental formations that "it is included in the aggregate of feeling… included in the aggregate of perception… included in the aggregate of consciousness"? Yes. Should it not be said of the emptiness of the aggregate of consciousness that "it is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? That should not be said… ^5-833

Should it not be said that "emptiness is included in the aggregate of mental formations"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, formations (conditioned things) are empty of a self or of what belongs to a self" [M. Ni. 3.69, in the Discourse on the Way to the Imperturbable]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case emptiness is included in the aggregate of mental formations.
The Discussion of Emptiness is finished. ^5-834

#### The Nineteenth Chapter ^5-27-3-0

##### (188) 3. Discussion of the Fruit of the Ascetic Life ^5-27-3-1-0

Is the fruit of the ascetic life unconditioned? Yes. Is it nibbāna (final release), the protection, the shelter, the refuge, the final resort, the imperishable, the deathless? That should not be said… Is the fruit of the ascetic life unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or any gap? That should not be said… ^5-835

Is the fruit of the ascetic life unconditioned? Yes. Is the ascetic life unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the ascetic life conditioned? Yes. Is the fruit of the ascetic life conditioned? That should not be said…
Is the fruit of stream-entry unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of stream-entry unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the path of stream-entry conditioned? Yes. Is the fruit of stream-entry conditioned? That should not be said…
Is the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) unconditioned? Yes. Is the path of arahantship unconditioned? That should not be said… Is the path of arahantship conditioned? Yes. Is the fruit of arahantship conditioned? That should not be said…
Is the fruit of stream-entry unconditioned, the fruit of once-returning… the fruit of non-returning… the fruit of arahantship unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there five unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there five unconditioned things? Yes. Are there five protections… or any gap? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Fruit of the Ascetic Life is finished. ^5-836

That should not be said… Is the suchness of all things unconditioned, and is nibbāna unconditioned? Yes. Are there two unconditioned things? That should not be said… Are there two unconditioned things? Yes. Are there two protections… or any gap? That should not be said… ^5-841

##### (192) 7. Discussion of the Absolutely Fixed Course ^5-27-7-1-0

Does an ordinary person have an absolutely fixed course? Yes. Is one who has killed their mother one whose course is absolutely fixed; one who has killed their father… a killer of a worthy one (arahant)… a shedder of a Buddha's blood… a splitter of the Community one whose course is absolutely fixed? That should not be said… ^5-847

Does an ordinary person have an absolutely fixed course? Yes. Would doubt arise in a person whose course is absolutely fixed? Yes. If doubt would arise in a person whose course is absolutely fixed, then surely you must not say: "An ordinary person has an absolutely fixed course."
Would doubt not arise in a person whose course is absolutely fixed? Yes. Has it been abandoned? That should not be said… Has it been abandoned? Yes. By the path of stream-entry? That should not be said… By the path of once-returning… by the path of non-returning… by the path of arahantship (the state of a worthy one)? That should not be said…

That should not be said… But isn't an unwholesome path one that does not lead out… is subject to defilement? Yes. That should not be said… By the path of once-returning… by the path of non-returning… by the path of arahantship? That should not be said…

That should not be said… By the path of once-returning… by the path of non-returning… by the path of arahantship? That should not be said…
By which path? By an unwholesome path. Is an unwholesome path… then surely you must not say: "In a person fixed in the annihilationist view, the eternalist view has been abandoned by an unwholesome path." ^5-850

Is there worldly faith, but no worldly faculty of faith? Yes. Is there worldly joy, but no worldly faculty of joy… is there worldly life, but no worldly life faculty?
