Is there worldly faith, but no worldly faculty of faith? Yes. Is there world-transcending faith, but no world-transcending faculty of faith? That should not be said… Is there worldly energy… is there worldly wisdom, but no worldly faculty of wisdom? Yes. Is there world-transcending wisdom, but no world-transcending faculty of wisdom? That should not be said… ^5-855

Are there no five faculties that are worldly? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, surveying the world with the eye of a Buddha, I saw beings with little dust in their eyes and with much dust in their eyes, with keen faculties and with dull faculties, with good qualities, easy to teach, and some who dwell seeing fear and blame in the other world" [M. Ni. 1.283; there the words "with bad qualities, hard to teach" and so on are also found]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there are five faculties that are worldly.
The Discussion of the Faculties is finished.
The Nineteenth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
One abandons past defilements, abandons future defilements, abandons present defilements; emptiness is included in the aggregate of mental formations; the fruit of the ascetic life is unconditioned; acquisition is unconditioned; the suchness of all things is unconditioned; the element of nibbāna is wholesome; an ordinary person has an absolutely fixed course; there are no five faculties that are worldly. ^5-856

### The Twentieth Chapter ^5-28-0

#### (194) 1. Discussion of the Unintentional ^5-28-1-0

Having unintentionally deprived their mother of life, does one become a person who has committed a deed with immediate result? Yes. Having unintentionally killed a living being, does one become one who kills living beings? That should not be said… Having unintentionally deprived their mother of life, does one become a person who has committed a deed with immediate result? Yes. Having unintentionally taken what is not given… having unintentionally spoken falsely, does one become one who speaks falsely? That should not be said…
Having unintentionally killed a living being, does one not become one who kills living beings? Yes. Having unintentionally deprived their mother of life, does one not become a person who has committed a deed with immediate result? That should not be said… Having unintentionally taken what is not given… having unintentionally spoken falsely, does one not become one who speaks falsely? Yes. Having unintentionally deprived their mother of life, does one not become a person who has committed a deed with immediate result? That should not be said… ^5-857

Having unintentionally deprived their mother of life, does one become a person who has committed a deed with immediate result? Yes. "Having unintentionally deprived one's mother of life, one becomes a person who has committed a deed with immediate result" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. "Having intentionally deprived one's mother of life, one becomes a person who has committed a deed with immediate result" — is there really such a discourse? Yes. If there really is the discourse "Having intentionally deprived one's mother of life, one becomes a person who has committed a deed with immediate result," then surely you must not say: "Having unintentionally deprived one's mother of life, one becomes a person who has committed a deed with immediate result." ^5-858

Should it not be said that "one who has killed their mother has committed a deed with immediate result"? Yes. But hasn't the mother been deprived of life? Yes. If the mother has been deprived of life, then surely you must also say: "One who has killed their mother has committed a deed with immediate result."
Should it not be said that "one who has killed their father has committed a deed with immediate result"? Yes. But hasn't the father been deprived of life? Yes. If the father has been deprived of life, then surely you must also say: "One who has killed their father has committed a deed with immediate result."
Should it not be said that "one who has killed a worthy one (arahant) has committed a deed with immediate result"? Yes. But hasn't a worthy one been deprived of life? Yes. If a worthy one has been deprived of life, then surely you must also say: "One who has killed a worthy one has committed a deed with immediate result."
Should it not be said that "one who has shed a Buddha's blood has committed a deed with immediate result"? Yes. But hasn't the blood of the Tathāgata (the Buddha) been shed? Yes. If the blood of the Tathāgata has been shed, then surely you must also say: "One who has shed a Buddha's blood has committed a deed with immediate result." ^5-859

Has one who splits the Community committed a deed with immediate result? Yes. Have all who split the Community committed a deed with immediate result? That should not be said… Have all who split the Community committed a deed with immediate result? Yes. Has one who splits the Community while perceiving it to be in accord with the Dhamma committed a deed with immediate result? That should not be said… ^5-860

Has one who splits the Community while perceiving it to be in accord with the Dhamma committed a deed with immediate result? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Upāli, there is one who splits the Community who is bound for the lower realms, bound for hell, who remains there for an aeon (world-age), who is incurable; Upāli, there is one who splits the Community who is not bound for the lower realms, not bound for hell, does not remain there for an aeon, and is not incurable"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "one who splits the Community while perceiving it to be in accord with the Dhamma has committed a deed with immediate result." ^5-861

Should it not be said that "one who splits the Community while perceiving it to be in accord with the Dhamma has committed a deed with immediate result"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Bound for the lower realms, bound for hell, remaining there for an aeon, is the one who splits the Community;
delighting in faction, standing on what is not the Dhamma, they fall away from security from bondage;
having split a Community that was united, they are tormented in hell for an aeon" [Cūḷava. 354; A. Ni. 10.39; Itivu. 18]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case one who splits the Community has committed a deed with immediate result.
The Discussion of the Unintentional is finished. ^5-862

#### The Twentieth Chapter ^5-28-2-0

##### (195) 2. Discussion of Knowledge ^5-28-2-1-0

Does an ordinary person have no knowledge? Yes. Does an ordinary person have no wisdom, understanding, investigation, close investigation, investigation of states, discernment, discrimination, close discrimination? That should not be said… But doesn't an ordinary person have wisdom, understanding, investigation… close discrimination? Yes. If an ordinary person has wisdom, understanding, investigation… close discrimination, then surely you must not say: "An ordinary person has no knowledge." ^5-863

Does an ordinary person have no knowledge? Yes. Could an ordinary person enter the first meditative absorption (jhāna)? Yes. If an ordinary person could enter the first meditative absorption, then surely you must not say: "An ordinary person has no knowledge."
Could an ordinary person enter the second meditative absorption… the third meditative absorption… the fourth meditative absorption… enter the base of the infinity of space, enter the base of the infinity of consciousness, the base of nothingness, the base of neither perception nor non-perception; could an ordinary person give a gift… give robes, give almsfood, give lodgings, give medicines and requisites for the sick? Yes. If an ordinary person could give medicines and requisites for the sick, then surely you must not say: "An ordinary person has no knowledge." ^5-864

Does an ordinary person have knowledge? Yes. Does an ordinary person, with that knowledge, fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, develop the path? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Knowledge is finished. ^5-865

#### The Twentieth Chapter ^5-28-3-0

##### (196) 3. Discussion of Hell Wardens ^5-28-3-1-0

Are there no hell wardens in the hells? Yes. Are there no punishments in the hells? That should not be said… Are there punishments in the hells? Yes. Are there hell wardens in the hells? That should not be said…
Among human beings, are there punishments, and are there also punishers? Yes. In the hells, are there punishments, and are there also punishers? That should not be said… In the hells, are there punishments, but no punishers? Yes. Among human beings, are there punishments, but no punishers? That should not be said… ^5-866

Are there hell wardens in the hells? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Not Vessabhū, nor the king of the ghosts,
nor Soma, Yama or King Vessavaṇa —
it is their own actions that strike them there, those driven out from here [variant: paṇuṇṇaṃ (Syā., Ka.), panunnaṃ (Sī.)] who have reached the other world"?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there are no hell wardens in the hells. ^5-867

Are there no hell wardens in the hells? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, the hell wardens make that being undergo [variant: karonti (M. Ni. 3.250; A. Ni. 3.36)] the punishment called the fivefold binding: they drive a red-hot iron stake through one hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake through the other hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake through one foot, they drive a red-hot iron stake through the other foot, they drive a red-hot iron stake through the middle of the chest; there that being feels painful, sharp, piercing feelings; and they do not die so long as that evil action has not been used up" [M. Ni. 3.250; A. Ni. 3.36]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there are hell wardens in the hells.
Are there no hell wardens in the hells? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, the hell wardens lay that being down and pare them with axes [variant: kudhārīhi (all editions)]… Monks, the hell wardens set that being feet up and head down and pare them with adzes… Monks, the hell wardens harness that being to a chariot and drive them back and forth over ground that is burning, blazing and glowing [variant: sañjotibhūtāya (Syā.)]… Monks, the hell wardens make that being climb up and down a great mountain of hot embers that is burning, blazing and glowing… Monks, the hell wardens take hold of that being feet up and head down and throw them into a red-hot metal cauldron that is burning, blazing and glowing. There they are cooked in a swirl of froth, and while being cooked in a swirl of froth they go now up, now down, now across. There they feel painful, sharp, piercing feelings, and they do not die so long as that evil action has not been used up. Monks, the hell wardens throw that being into the Great Hell. And that Great Hell, monks —
"has four corners and four doors, and is divided into equal parts;
it is surrounded by an iron wall and roofed over with iron.
"Its floor is made of iron, blazing and full of fire;
it spreads a hundred leagues (yojanas) all around and stays so at all times" [M. Ni. 3.250; A. Ni. 3.36; Pe. Va. 71]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there are hell wardens in the hells.
The Discussion of Hell Wardens is finished. ^5-868

#### The Twentieth Chapter ^5-28-4-0

##### (197) 4. Discussion of Animals ^5-28-4-1-0

Are there animals among the gods? Yes. Are there gods among the animals? That should not be said… Are there animals among the gods? Yes. Is the world of the gods the animal realm? That should not be said… Are there animals among the gods? Yes. Are there insects, moths, mosquitoes, flies, snakes, scorpions, centipedes and earthworms [variant: gaṇḍupādāti (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)] there? That should not be said… ^5-869

Are there no animals among the gods? Yes. But isn't there the great elephant called Erāvaṇa there, and a divine chariot yoked with a thousand (horses)? Yes. If there is the great elephant called Erāvaṇa there, and a divine chariot yoked with a thousand (horses), then surely you must also say: "There are animals among the gods." ^5-870

Are there animals among the gods? Yes. Are there elephant keepers, horse keepers [variant: hatthibhaṇḍā assabhaṇḍā (?)], fodder-gatherers, trainers and cooks there? That should not be said. In that case there are no animals among the gods.
The Discussion of Animals is finished. ^5-871

#### The Twentieth Chapter ^5-28-5-0

##### (198) 5. Discussion of the Path ^5-28-5-1-0

Is the path fivefold? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared the eightfold path, namely: right view… right concentration? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared the eightfold path, namely: right view… right concentration, then surely you must not say: "The path is fivefold."
Is the path fivefold? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say:
"Of paths, the eightfold is the best; of truths, the four statements;
freedom from greed is the best of states, and of two-footed beings, the one who has vision" [Dha. Pa. 273, in the Dhammapada]?
Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the path is eightfold. ^5-872

Is right speech a factor of the path, but not the path? Yes. Is right view a factor of the path, but not the path? That should not be said… Is right speech a factor of the path, but not the path? Yes. Is right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… right concentration a factor of the path, but not the path? That should not be said…
Is right action… right livelihood a factor of the path, but not the path? Yes. Is right view… right concentration a factor of the path, but not the path? That should not be said…
Is right view a factor of the path, and is it the path? Yes. Is right speech a factor of the path, and is it the path? That should not be said… Is right view a factor of the path, and is it the path? Yes. Is right action… right livelihood a factor of the path, and is it the path? That should not be said…
Is right intention… right effort… right mindfulness… right concentration a factor of the path, and is it the path? Yes. Is right speech… right action… right livelihood a factor of the path, and is it the path? That should not be said… ^5-873

Is the noble path eightfold? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Their bodily action, verbal action and livelihood have already been well purified beforehand; in this way this noble eightfold path of theirs comes to the fulfilment of its development" [M. Ni. 3.431]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the path is fivefold. ^5-874

Is the path fivefold? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Subhadda, in whatever teaching and discipline the noble eightfold path is not found, no ascetic is found there, no second ascetic is found there, no third ascetic is found there, no fourth ascetic is found there. But in whatever teaching and discipline the noble eightfold path is found, an ascetic is found there, a second… a third… a fourth ascetic is found there. In this teaching and discipline, Subhadda, the noble eightfold path is found. Here alone, Subhadda, is there an ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, here a fourth ascetic. The doctrines of others are empty of other ascetics" [D. Ni. 2.214]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the path is eightfold.
The Discussion of the Path is finished. ^5-875

#### The Twentieth Chapter ^5-28-6-0

##### (199) 6. Discussion of Knowledge ^5-28-6-1-0

Is the knowledge with twelve aspects world-transcending? Yes. Are there twelve kinds of world-transcending knowledge? That should not be said… Are there twelve kinds of world-transcending knowledge? Yes. Are there twelve paths of stream-entry? That should not be said… Are there twelve paths of stream-entry? Yes. Are there twelve fruits of stream-entry? That should not be said… Are there twelve paths of once-returning… paths of non-returning… paths of arahantship (the state of a worthy one)? That should not be said… Are there twelve paths of arahantship? Yes. Are there twelve fruits of arahantship? That should not be said… ^5-876

Should it not be said that "the knowledge with twelve aspects is world-transcending"? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "‘This is the noble truth of suffering’ — thus, monks, in regard to things not heard before, there arose in me vision, there arose knowledge, there arose wisdom, there arose true knowledge, there arose light. ‘This noble truth of suffering is to be fully understood’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been fully understood’ — thus, monks… ‘this is the noble truth of the origin of suffering [variant: dukkhasamudayo (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)]’ — thus, monks… ‘this noble truth of the origin of suffering is to be abandoned’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been abandoned’ — thus, monks… ‘this is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering [variant: dukkhanirodhā (Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)]’ — thus, monks… ‘this noble truth of the cessation of suffering is to be realized’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been realized’ — thus, monks… ‘this is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering’ — thus, monks… ‘this noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering is to be developed’ — thus, monks… ‘it has been developed’ — thus, monks, in regard to things not heard before, there arose in me vision… there arose light" [Mahāva. 15; S. Ni. 5.1081; Paṭi. Ma. 2.30]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case the knowledge with twelve aspects is world-transcending.
The Discussion of Knowledge is finished.
The Twentieth Chapter.
Here is its summary:
One who has killed their mother has committed a deed with immediate result, one who has killed their father has committed a deed with immediate result, one who has killed a worthy one has committed a deed with immediate result, one who has shed a Buddha's blood has committed a deed with immediate result, one who splits the Community has committed a deed with immediate result; an ordinary person has no knowledge; there are no hell wardens in the hells; there are animals among the gods; the path is fivefold; the knowledge with twelve aspects is world-transcending.
The Fourth Set of Fifty.
Here is its summary:
Restraining, the accumulation of merit, "stayed", and the past, and the killer of a mother. ^5-877

### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-0

#### (200) 1. Discussion of the Teaching ^5-29-1-0

Has the teaching been made new? Yes. Have the foundations of mindfulness been made new? That should not be said… Has the teaching been made new? Yes. Have the right strivings… the bases of psychic power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of awakening been made new? That should not be said… Has what was earlier unwholesome later been made wholesome? That should not be said… Has what was earlier accompanied by taints… subject to the fetters, subject to the knots, subject to the floods, subject to the bonds, subject to the hindrances, seized upon, subject to clinging… subject to defilement later been made not subject to defilement? That should not be said…
Is there anyone who makes the teaching of the Tathāgata (the Buddha) new? Yes. Is there anyone who makes the foundations of mindfulness new? That should not be said… Is there anyone who makes the right strivings… the bases of psychic power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of awakening new? That should not be said… Is there anyone who makes what was earlier unwholesome later wholesome? That should not be said… Is there anyone who makes what was earlier accompanied by taints… subject to defilement later not subject to defilement? That should not be said…
Is it possible to make the teaching of the Tathāgata new again? Yes. Is it possible to make the foundations of mindfulness new again? That should not be said… Is it possible to make the right strivings… the bases of psychic power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of awakening new again? That should not be said… Is it possible to make what was earlier unwholesome later wholesome? That should not be said… Is it possible to make what was earlier accompanied by taints… subject to defilement later not subject to defilement? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Teaching is finished. ^5-878

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-2-0

##### (201) 2. Discussion of Not Being Separated ^5-29-2-1-0

Is an ordinary person not separated from the states of the three realms? Yes. Is an ordinary person not separated from the contacts… the feelings… perceptions… intentions… states of mind… kinds of faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… the wisdom of the three realms? That should not be said…
Is an ordinary person not separated from the actions of the three realms? Yes. At the moment an ordinary person gives a robe, do they at that moment enter and dwell in the first meditative absorption (jhāna)… enter and dwell in the base of the infinity of space? That should not be said… At the moment an ordinary person gives almsfood… gives lodgings… gives medicines and requisites for the sick, do they at that moment enter and dwell in the fourth meditative absorption… enter and dwell in the base of neither perception nor non-perception? That should not be said… ^5-879

Should it not be said that "an ordinary person is not separated from the actions of the three realms"? Yes. Has an ordinary person fully understood the action that leads to rebirth in the realm of form and in the formless realm? That should not be said. In that case an ordinary person is not separated from the actions of the three realms…
The Discussion of Not Being Separated is finished. ^5-880

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-3-0

##### (202) 3. Discussion of the Fetters ^5-29-3-1-0

Is there attainment of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) without abandoning some fetter? Yes. Is there attainment of arahantship without abandoning identity view… without abandoning doubt… without abandoning clinging to rules and rituals… without abandoning greed… without abandoning hatred… without abandoning delusion… without abandoning lack of moral fear? That should not be said…
Is there attainment of arahantship without abandoning some fetter? Yes. Is a worthy one (arahant) one who has greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, contempt, rivalry, despair and defilements? That should not be said… But isn't a worthy one free from greed, free from hatred, free from delusion, free from conceit, free from contempt, free from rivalry, free from despair, free from defilements? Yes. If a worthy one is free from greed… free from defilements, then surely you must not say: "There is attainment of arahantship without abandoning some fetter." ^5-881

Should it not be said that "there is attainment of arahantship without abandoning some fetter"? Yes. Does a worthy one know the whole domain of a Buddha? That should not be said. In that case there is attainment of arahantship without abandoning some fetter.
The Discussion of the Fetters is finished. ^5-882

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-4-0

##### (203) 4. Discussion of Psychic Power ^5-29-4-1-0

Do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing (making things happen as they wish)? Yes. "May the trees always be in leaf" — do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing this? That should not be said… May the trees always be in flower… may the trees always be in fruit… may it always be moonlight… may it always be safe… may there always be plenty of food… "may there always be well-being [variant: suvuṭṭhikaṃ (Syā.)]" — do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing this? That should not be said…
Do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing? Yes. "May contact that has arisen not cease" — do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing this? That should not be said…
May feeling that has arisen… perception… intention… mind… faith… energy… mindfulness… concentration… wisdom not cease — do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing this? That should not be said…
Do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing? Yes. "May material form be permanent" — do they have the psychic power of wishing this… feeling… perception… mental formations… "may consciousness be permanent" — do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing this? That should not be said…
Do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing? Yes. "May beings who are subject to birth not be born" — do they have… "may beings who are subject to ageing not age"… "may beings who are subject to sickness not fall sick"… "may beings who are subject to death not die" — do Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing this? That should not be said… ^5-883

Should it not be said that "Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing"? Yes. But didn't the venerable Pilindavaccha resolve that the palace of Seniya Bimbisāra, king of Magadha, was "gold", and wasn't it indeed gold [Pārā. 621; Mahāva. 271]? Yes. If the venerable Pilindavaccha resolved that the palace of Seniya Bimbisāra, king of Magadha, was gold, and it was indeed gold, then surely you must also say: "Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing."
The Discussion of Psychic Power is finished. ^5-884

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-5-0

##### (204) 5. Discussion of the Buddhas ^5-29-5-1-0

Are Buddhas inferior or superior to other Buddhas? Yes. In regard to the foundations of mindfulness? That should not be said… In regard to the right strivings… the bases of psychic power… the faculties… the powers… the factors of awakening… mastery… the knowledge and vision of omniscience? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Buddhas is finished. ^5-885

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-6-0

##### (205) 6. Discussion of All Directions ^5-29-6-1-0

Do Buddhas live in all directions? Yes. Does a Buddha live in the eastern direction? That should not be said… Does a Buddha live in the eastern direction? Yes. What is that Blessed One's name, what is his birth, what is his clan, what are the names of that Blessed One's mother and father, what are the names of that Blessed One's pair of chief disciples, what is the name of that Blessed One's attendant, what kind of robe does he wear, what kind of bowl does he carry, in which village or town or city or kingdom or country is he? That should not be said…
Does a Buddha live in the southern direction… in the western direction… in the northern direction… in the direction below? That should not be said… Does a Buddha live in the direction below? Yes. What is that Blessed One's name… or country is he? That should not be said…
Does a Buddha live in the direction above? That should not be said… Does a Buddha live in the direction above? Yes. Does he live in the realm of the gods of the Four Great Kings… among the Thirty-three gods… among the Yāma gods… among the Tusita gods… among the gods who delight in creating… among the gods who wield power over the creations of others… in the Brahmā world? That should not be said…
The Discussion of All Directions is finished. ^5-886

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-7-0

##### (206) 7. Discussion of States ^5-29-7-1-0

Are all states fixed? Yes. Fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… Fixed in rightness? That should not be said… Is there no group that is not fixed? That should not be said… But isn't there a group that is not fixed? Yes. If there is a group that is not fixed, then surely you must not say: "All states are fixed."
Are all states fixed? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared three groups — the group fixed in wrongness, the group fixed in rightness, and the group that is not fixed [Dha. Sa., Triad Matrix 15]? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared three groups — the group fixed in wrongness, the group fixed in rightness, and the group that is not fixed — then surely you must not say: "All states are fixed."
Is material form fixed in the sense of being material form? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… Fixed in rightness? That should not be said… Is feeling… perception… are mental formations… is consciousness fixed in the sense of being consciousness? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… Fixed in rightness? That should not be said… ^5-887

Should it not be said that material form is fixed in the sense of being material form… feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness is fixed in the sense of being consciousness? Yes. Does material form become feeling… become perception… become mental formations… become consciousness; does feeling… perception… do mental formations… does consciousness become material form… become feeling… become perception… become mental formations? That should not be said. In that case material form is fixed in the sense of being material form, feeling… perception… mental formations… consciousness is fixed in the sense of being consciousness.
The Discussion of States is finished. ^5-888

#### The Twenty-First Chapter ^5-29-8-0

##### (207) 8. Discussion of Action ^5-29-8-1-0

Are all actions fixed? Yes. Fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… Fixed in rightness? That should not be said… Is there no group that is not fixed? That should not be said… But isn't there a group that is not fixed? Yes. If there is a group that is not fixed, then surely you must not say: "All actions are fixed."
Are all actions fixed? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared three groups — the group fixed in wrongness, the group fixed in rightness, and the group that is not fixed? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared three groups — the group fixed in wrongness, the group fixed in rightness, and the group that is not fixed — then surely you must not say: "All actions are fixed." ^5-889

Is action to be experienced in this very life fixed in the sense of being experienced in this very life? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… Fixed in rightness? That should not be said… Is action to be experienced in the next rebirth… is action to be experienced on some later occasion fixed in the sense of being experienced on some later occasion? Yes. Is it fixed in wrongness? That should not be said… Fixed in rightness? That should not be said… ^5-890

Should it not be said that action to be experienced in this very life is fixed in the sense of being experienced in this very life, action to be experienced in the next rebirth… action to be experienced on some later occasion is fixed in the sense of being experienced on some later occasion? Yes. Does action to be experienced in this very life become action to be experienced in the next rebirth, become action to be experienced on some later occasion… does action to be experienced in the next rebirth become action to be experienced in this very life, become action to be experienced on some later occasion… does action to be experienced on some later occasion become action to be experienced in this very life, become action to be experienced in the next rebirth? That should not be said. In that case action to be experienced in this very life is fixed in the sense of being experienced in this very life, action to be experienced in the next rebirth… action to be experienced on some later occasion is fixed in the sense of being experienced on some later occasion.
The Discussion of Action is finished.
The Twenty-First Chapter.
Here is its summary:
The teaching has been made new; there is someone who makes the teaching of the Tathāgata new; it is possible to make the teaching of the Tathāgata new again; an ordinary person is not separated from the states of the three realms; there is attainment of arahantship without abandoning some fetter; Buddhas or disciples have the psychic power of wishing; Buddhas are inferior or superior to other Buddhas; Buddhas live in all directions; all states are fixed; all actions are fixed. ^5-891

### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-0

#### (208) 1. Discussion of Final Nibbāna ^5-30-1-0

Is there final nibbāna (final release) without abandoning some fetter? Yes. Is there final nibbāna without abandoning identity view… without abandoning lack of moral fear? That should not be said…
Is there final nibbāna without abandoning some fetter? Yes. Is a worthy one (arahant) one who has greed… defilements? That should not be said… But isn't a worthy one free from greed… free from defilements? Yes. If a worthy one is free from greed… free from defilements, then surely you must not say: "There is final nibbāna without abandoning some fetter." ^5-892

Should it not be said that "there is final nibbāna without abandoning some fetter"? Yes. Does a worthy one know the whole domain of a Buddha? That should not be said. In that case there is final nibbāna without abandoning some fetter.
The Discussion of Final Nibbāna is finished. ^5-893

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-2-0

##### (209) 2. Discussion of a Wholesome Mind ^5-30-2-1-0

Does a worthy one (arahant) attain final nibbāna (final release) with a wholesome mind? Yes. Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while generating a meritorious formation… while generating an imperturbable formation… while performing action that leads to a destination… while performing action that leads to existence… while performing action that leads to sovereignty… while performing action that leads to lordship… while performing action that leads to great wealth… while performing action that leads to a large retinue… while performing action that leads to the splendour of the gods… while performing action that leads to the splendour of human beings? That should not be said…
Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna with a wholesome mind? Yes. Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while building up, tearing down, abandoning, clinging, scattering, binding together, putting out, kindling? That should not be said… But doesn't a worthy one neither build up nor tear down, but stand having torn down? Yes. If a worthy one neither builds up nor tears down, but stands having torn down, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna with a wholesome mind." But doesn't a worthy one neither abandon nor cling, but stand having abandoned; neither scatter nor bind together, but stand having scattered; doesn't a worthy one neither put out nor kindle, but stand having put out? Yes. If a worthy one neither puts out nor kindles, but stands having put out, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna with a wholesome mind." ^5-894

Should it not be said that "a worthy one attains final nibbāna with a wholesome mind"? Yes. But doesn't a worthy one attain final nibbāna with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending? Yes. If a worthy one attains final nibbāna with mindfulness established, mindful and clearly comprehending, then surely you must also say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna with a wholesome mind."
The Discussion of a Wholesome Mind is finished. ^5-895

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-3-0

##### (210) 3. Discussion of the Imperturbable ^5-30-3-1-0

Does a worthy one (arahant) attain final nibbāna (final release) while established in the imperturbable? Yes. But doesn't a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in the ordinary mind? Yes. If a worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in the ordinary mind, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."
Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in a functional mind? That should not be said… But doesn't a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in a mind that is a result? Yes. If a worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in a mind that is a result, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."
Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in a mind that is functional and indeterminate? That should not be said… But doesn't a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in a mind that is a result and indeterminate? Yes. If a worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in a mind that is a result and indeterminate, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."
Does a worthy one attain final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable? Yes. But didn't the Blessed One attain final nibbāna immediately after emerging from the fourth meditative absorption (jhāna) [D. Ni. 2.219]? Yes. If the Blessed One attained final nibbāna immediately after emerging from the fourth meditative absorption, then surely you must not say: "A worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable."
The Discussion of the Imperturbable is finished. ^5-896

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-4-0

##### (211) 4. Discussion of Breaking Through to the Dhamma ^5-30-4-1-0

Is there breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there, for one lying in the womb, teaching of the Dhamma, hearing of the Dhamma, discussion of the Dhamma, questioning, undertaking of virtue, guarding the doors of the sense faculties, moderation in eating, devotion to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night? That should not be said… Is there, for one lying in the womb, no teaching of the Dhamma, no hearing of the Dhamma… no devotion to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night? Yes. If, for one lying in the womb, there is no teaching of the Dhamma, no hearing of the Dhamma… no devotion to wakefulness in the first and last parts of the night, then surely you must not say: "There is breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb."
Is there breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. But aren't there two conditions for the arising of right view — the voice of another, and wise attention? Yes. If there are two conditions for the arising of right view — the voice of another, and wise attention — then surely you must not say: "There is breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb."
Is there breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and without clear comprehension? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Breaking Through to the Dhamma is finished. ^5-897

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-5-0

##### (212-4) 5-7. The Three Discussions ^5-30-5-1-0

Is there attainment of arahantship (the state of a worthy one) for one lying in the womb? Yes. Is there attainment of arahantship for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and without clear comprehension? That should not be said… ^5-898

Is there breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is dreaming? Yes. Is there breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and without clear comprehension? That should not be said… ^5-899

Is there attainment of arahantship for one who is dreaming? Yes. Is there attainment of arahantship for one who is asleep, heedless, unmindful and without clear comprehension? That should not be said…
The Three Discussions are finished. ^5-900

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-6-0

##### (215) 8. Discussion of "Indeterminate" ^5-30-6-1-0

Is every state of mind of one who is dreaming indeterminate? Yes. Could one kill a living being in a dream? Yes. If one could kill a living being in a dream, then surely you must not say: "Every state of mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate."
Could one, in a dream, take what is not given… speak falsely, speak divisively, speak harshly, engage in idle chatter, break into houses, carry off plunder, rob a single house, lie in ambush on the highway, go to another's wife, destroy a village, destroy a town; could one engage in sexual intercourse in a dream, could impure fluid be emitted by one who is dreaming; could one, in a dream, give a gift, give robes, give almsfood, give lodgings, give medicines and requisites for the sick, give food to chew, give meals, give drink, pay homage to a shrine, offer a garland at a shrine, offer scents, offer ointments… walk around a shrine keeping it on their right? Yes. If one could, in a dream, walk around a shrine keeping it on their right, then surely you must not say: "Every state of mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate." ^5-901

Should it not be said that "every state of mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate"? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One declared that the mind of one who is dreaming is of no account? Yes. If the Blessed One has declared that the mind of one who is dreaming is of no account, then surely you must also say: "Every state of mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate."
The Discussion of "Indeterminate" is finished. ^5-902

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-7-0

##### (216) 9. Discussion of Repetition Condition ^5-30-7-1-0

Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, killing living beings, when pursued, developed and cultivated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the realm of ghosts; the lightest result of killing living beings, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to a short life" [A. Ni. 8.40]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is some repetition condition.
Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, taking what is not given, when pursued, developed and cultivated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the realm of ghosts; the lightest result of taking what is not given, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to loss of wealth… the lightest result of sexual misconduct, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to rivalry and hostility… the lightest result of false speech, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to being falsely accused… the lightest result of divisive speech, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to being divided from one's friends… the lightest result of harsh speech, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to disagreeable sounds… the lightest result of idle chatter, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to words that no one accepts; drinking liquor and wine, monks, when pursued… the lightest result of drinking liquor and wine, for one who becomes a human being, is that it leads to madness" [A. Ni. 8.40]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is some repetition condition. ^5-903

Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, wrong view, when pursued, developed and cultivated, leads to hell, leads to the animal realm, leads to the realm of ghosts"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is some repetition condition.
Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Wrong intention… wrong concentration, monks, when pursued, developed… leads to the realm of ghosts"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is some repetition condition. ^5-904

Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, right view, when pursued, developed and cultivated, plunges into the deathless, has the deathless as its final resort, has the deathless as its culmination"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is some repetition condition.
Is there no repetition condition at all? Yes. But did the Blessed One not say: "Monks, right intention, when pursued, developed and cultivated… monks, right concentration, when pursued, developed and cultivated, plunges into the deathless, has the deathless as its final resort, has the deathless as its culmination"? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case there is some repetition condition.
The Discussion of Repetition Condition is finished. ^5-905

#### The Twenty-Second Chapter ^5-30-8-0

##### (217) 10. Discussion of the Momentary ^5-30-8-1-0

Do all things last only a single moment of mind? Yes. Does the great earth last for the duration of a mind, does the great ocean last, does Sineru, king of mountains, last, does water last, does fire last, does air last, do grass, wood and trees last for the duration of a mind? That should not be said…
Do all things last only a single moment of mind? Yes. Is the eye base arisen together with eye-consciousness? That should not be said… Is the eye base arisen together with eye-consciousness? Yes. But didn't the venerable Sāriputta say this: "Friends, if the internal eye is intact but external visible forms do not come within its range, and there is no corresponding bringing to mind, then there is no manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness [variant: viññāṇabhāvassa (many editions)]. Friends, if the internal eye is intact and external visible forms come within its range, but there is no corresponding bringing to mind, then there is no manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness. But when, friends, the internal eye is intact, and external visible forms come within its range, and there is the corresponding bringing to mind, then there is the manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness" [M. Ni. 1.306]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the eye base is arisen together with eye-consciousness."
Is the ear base… the nose base… the tongue base… the body base arisen together with body-consciousness? That should not be said… Is the body base arisen together with body-consciousness? Yes. But didn't the venerable Sāriputta say this: "Friends, if the internal body is intact but external touches do not come within its range, and there is no… Friends, if the internal body is intact and external touches come within its range, but there is no… But when, friends, the internal body is intact, and external touches come within its range, and there is the corresponding bringing to mind, then there is the manifestation of the corresponding section of consciousness" [M. Ni. 1.306]? Is there really such a discourse? Yes. In that case it should not be said that "the body base is arisen together with body-consciousness." ^5-906

Should it not be said that "all things last only a single moment of mind"? Yes. Are all things permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change? That should not be said. In that case all things last only a single moment of mind.
The Discussion of the Momentary is finished.
The Twenty-Second Chapter.
Here is its summary:
There is final nibbāna without abandoning some fetter; a worthy one attains final nibbāna with a wholesome mind; a worthy one attains final nibbāna while established in the imperturbable; there is breakthrough to the Dhamma for one lying in the womb; there is attainment of arahantship for one lying in the womb; there is breakthrough to the Dhamma for one who is dreaming; there is attainment of arahantship for one who is dreaming; every state of mind of one who is dreaming is indeterminate; there is no repetition condition at all; all things last only a single moment of mind. ^5-907

### The Twenty-Third Chapter ^5-31-0

#### (218) 1. Discussion of a Shared Intention ^5-31-1-0

May sexual intercourse be engaged in with a shared intention? Yes. With a shared intention, should one become a non-ascetic, become a non-monk, become one cut off at the root, become one who has incurred defeat (expulsion from the monastic order)? That should not be said… May sexual intercourse be engaged in with a shared intention? Yes. With a shared intention, may one kill a living being, take what is not given, speak falsely, speak divisively, speak harshly, engage in idle chatter, break into houses, carry off plunder, rob a single house, lie in ambush on the highway, go to another's wife, destroy a village, destroy a town? That should not be said…
The Discussion of a Shared Intention is finished. ^5-908

#### The Twenty-Third Chapter ^5-31-2-0

##### (219) 2. Discussion of the Appearance of Worthy Ones ^5-31-2-1-0

Do non-human beings, in the appearance of worthy ones (arahants), engage in sexual intercourse? Yes. Do non-human beings, in the appearance of worthy ones, kill living beings… take what is not given, speak falsely, speak divisively, speak harshly, engage in idle chatter, break into houses, carry off plunder, rob a single house, lie in ambush on the highway, go to another's wife, destroy villages… destroy towns? That should not be said…
The Discussion of the Appearance of Worthy Ones is finished. ^5-909

#### The Twenty-Third Chapter ^5-31-3-0

##### (220-4) 3-7. Discussion of Acting at Will through Sovereign Power and So On ^5-31-3-1-0

Does the bodhisatta (a Buddha-to-be) go to the lower world because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. Does the bodhisatta, because of acting at will through sovereign power, go to hell, go to the Sañjīva hell, go to the Kālasutta hell, go to the Tāpana hell, go to the Mahātāpana hell [variant: patāpanaṃ (Sī., Syā., Kaṃ., Pī.)], go to the Saṅghātaka hell, go to the Roruva hell… go to the Avīci hell? That should not be said…
Does the bodhisatta go to the lower world because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. "The bodhisatta goes to the lower world because of acting at will through sovereign power" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there really is no discourse "The bodhisatta goes to the lower world because of acting at will through sovereign power," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta goes to the lower world because of acting at will through sovereign power." ^5-910

Does the bodhisatta enter a womb because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. Would the bodhisatta, because of acting at will through sovereign power, be reborn in hell, be reborn in the animal realm? That should not be said…
Does the bodhisatta enter a womb because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. Does the bodhisatta have psychic power? That should not be said… Does the bodhisatta have psychic power? Yes. Has the bodhisatta developed the basis of psychic power consisting of desire… the basis of psychic power consisting of energy… the basis of psychic power consisting of mind… the basis of psychic power consisting of investigation? That should not be said…
Does the bodhisatta enter a womb because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. "The bodhisatta enters a womb because of acting at will through sovereign power" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there really is no discourse "The bodhisatta enters a womb because of acting at will through sovereign power," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta enters a womb because of acting at will through sovereign power." ^5-911

Did the bodhisatta practise severe austerities because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. Did the bodhisatta, because of acting at will through sovereign power, adopt the view "The world is eternal"… "The world is not eternal"… "The world is finite"… "The world is infinite"… "The soul is the same as the body"… "The soul is one thing and the body another"… "The Tathāgata (the Buddha) exists after death"… "The Tathāgata does not exist after death"… "The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death"… did he adopt the view "The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"? That should not be said…
Did the bodhisatta practise severe austerities because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. "The bodhisatta practised severe austerities because of acting at will through sovereign power" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there really is no discourse "The bodhisatta practised severe austerities because of acting at will through sovereign power," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta practised severe austerities because of acting at will through sovereign power." ^5-912

Did the bodhisatta, because of acting at will through sovereign power, practise another kind of austerity [variant: amaraṃ tapaṃ (S. Ni. 1.137)] and acknowledge another teacher? Yes. Did the bodhisatta, because of acting at will through sovereign power, adopt the view "The world is eternal"… did he adopt the view "The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death"? That should not be said… ^5-913

Did the bodhisatta acknowledge another teacher because of acting at will through sovereign power? Yes. "The bodhisatta acknowledged another teacher because of acting at will through sovereign power" — is there really such a discourse? There is not. If there really is no discourse "The bodhisatta acknowledged another teacher because of acting at will through sovereign power," then surely you must not say: "The bodhisatta acknowledged another teacher because of acting at will through sovereign power."
The Discussion of Acting at Will through Sovereign Power is finished. ^5-914

#### The Twenty-Third Chapter ^5-31-4-0

##### (225) 8. Discussion of Counterfeits ^5-31-4-1-0

Is there something that is not greed but resembles greed? Yes. Is there something that is not contact but resembles contact, something that is not feeling but resembles feeling, something that is not perception but resembles perception, something that is not intention but resembles intention, something that is not mind but resembles mind, something that is not faith but resembles faith, something that is not energy but resembles energy, something that is not mindfulness but resembles mindfulness, something that is not concentration but resembles concentration, something that is not wisdom but resembles wisdom? That should not be said… ^5-915

Is there something that is not hatred but resembles hatred, something that is not delusion but resembles delusion, something that is not a defilement but resembles a defilement? Yes. Is there something that is not contact but resembles contact… something that is not wisdom but resembles wisdom? That should not be said…
The Discussion of Counterfeits is finished. ^5-916

#### The Twenty-Third Chapter ^5-31-5-0

##### (226) 9. Discussion of the Not Fully Formed ^5-31-5-1-0

Is material form not fully formed? Yes. Is material form not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently arisen, not subject to destruction, not subject to passing away, not subject to fading, not subject to cessation, not subject to change? That should not be said… But isn't material form impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change? Yes. If material form is impermanent, conditioned… subject to change, then surely you must not say: "Material form is not fully formed."
Is only suffering fully formed? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One said that what is impermanent is suffering [S. Ni. 3.15], and that "material form is impermanent"? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that what is impermanent is suffering, and that "material form is impermanent," then surely you must not say: "Only suffering is fully formed."… ^5-917

Is feeling… perception… are mental formations… is consciousness… the eye base… the base of mental objects… the eye element… the element of mental objects… the eye faculty… the faculty of one who has final knowledge not fully formed? Yes. Is the faculty of one who has final knowledge not impermanent… not subject to change? That should not be said… But isn't the faculty of one who has final knowledge impermanent, conditioned… subject to change? Yes. If the faculty of one who has final knowledge is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to passing away, subject to fading, subject to cessation, subject to change, then surely you must not say: "The faculty of one who has final knowledge is not fully formed."
Is only suffering fully formed? Yes. But hasn't the Blessed One said that what is impermanent is suffering, and that "the faculty of one who has final knowledge is impermanent"? Yes. If the Blessed One has said that what is impermanent is suffering, and that "the faculty of one who has final knowledge is impermanent," then surely you must not say: "Only suffering is fully formed."
The Discussion of the Not Fully Formed is finished.
The Twenty-Third Chapter.
Here is its summary:
Sexual intercourse may be engaged in with a shared intention; non-human beings, in the appearance of worthy ones, engage in sexual intercourse; the bodhisatta goes to the lower world because of acting at will through sovereign power, enters a womb, practised severe austerities, practised another kind of austerity, acknowledged another teacher; there is something that is not greed but resembles greed, something that is not hatred but resembles hatred, something that is not delusion but resembles delusion, something that is not a defilement but resembles a defilement; material form is not fully formed, the faculty of one who has final knowledge is not fully formed.
The Small Half-Set of Fifty.
Here is its summary:
Made new, final nibbāna, a shared intention.
Summary of the sets of fifty:
The Great, the Fixed Course, the Underlying Tendencies, Restraining, and the Small as the fifth;
crushing the doctrines of others, well grounded in the root of the discourses,
they illuminate the Teacher's doctrine in the book Points of Discussion.
Thirty-five recitation sections.
The book Points of Discussion is finished. ^5-918
